strings.book.death_notice.text:
ROYAL BUREAU OF RECORDS — DISTRICT OF BELLWETHER

Notice of Administrative Decease:
Be it known that the bearer of this writ expired seventeen (17) winters past. All chattels were auctioned to cover municipal interment fees. Remaining balance due: 142 crowns in unpaid burial tax.

If you wish to contest your deceased status, report in person to Clerk Oakhaven at the Bellwether Records Office and submit Form 27-B.

The Bureau regrets your loss.

(Below, in smaller print: Late payment by the deceased incurs interest at the reduced posthumous rate of 4% per annum. Haunting the Records Office does not count as payment.)
strings.book.form_27b.text:
FORM 27-B: APPLICATION FOR TEMPORARY EXEMPTION FROM BEING DEAD

Section I: Applicant certifies under penalty of perjury that they are currently breathing, corporeal, and occupying no more than one (1) point in history.
Section II: Attach corroborating ledger entry from Annex III.
Section III: Applicants who are in fact dead should not fill out this form. Please see Form 27-C (Resignation from Being Alive).

The counter-signature box is already stamped, in ink that has stayed wet for seventeen years:
APPROVED - M. MORVATH, CHIEF ARCHIVIST, ANNEX III
strings.book.uncounted_ledger.text:
FOLIO I (the oldest hand):
"We did not strike the seven cities out of malice. When the flaw in the world's foundation widened, every name spoken aloud gave the Hunger another door. We wrote them here instead, and signed the Seal of Names over them, so the dark could not find them. Let Annex III keep this book until the world is mended."

FOLIO IX (Morvath's hand, seventeen years ago):
"The Seal has cracked. Tonight we strike Oakhallow, all four hundred and twelve. The children go below to the Nursery. The others we scatter with their memories sealed: a baker's elder girl to Bellwether, a child of the Mill Lane houses to wherever the road takes them. Those we could not reach in time, the Hunger reached first. May whoever reads this forgive the ink."

FINAL FOLIO (a hand nobody has written yet):
"A traveller walks into Bellwether carrying a notice of their own death. The ink of their name is fading, and so is the Seal. At the next new moon Bellwether will be uncounted, unless the Seal is signed again by a name freely given by its owner."
strings.book.tome_ember.text: On the Ignition of Aether: Speak the syllable of cinder and project the spark outward.
strings.book.tome_mend.text: Litany of the Dawn: Recall the body's unblemished pattern from yesterday's ledger.
strings.book.tome_ward.text: Treatise on Abjuration: Fold ambient stone-memory into a shield before the blow lands.
strings.book.tome_glimmer.text: Cantrip of the Archivist: A steady light that neither smokes nor scorches vellum.
strings.book.tome_veil.text: Notes on Un-Noticing: Step between the lines of the observer's attention.

strings.quest.legally_deceased.title: Legally Deceased
strings.quest.legally_deceased.summary: The Royal Bureau of Records insists you died seventeen years ago. Clear your name—or uncover why it was erased.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage0: Speak with Clerk Oakhaven inside the Bellwether Records Office.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal0: I arrived in Bellwether carrying a formal notice declaring that I died seventeen years ago and owe burial taxes. I should confront the local records clerk.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage10: Travel east along the Old Road to the abandoned Registry Annex and retrieve Form 27-B.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal10: Clerk Oakhaven informed me that I am legally dead and cannot file a correction without Form 27-B, which is stored in the old Registry Annex east of town, closed seventeen years ago for 'refurbishment'. He handed me the brass key to the Annex door. The key says I may not enter without Form 27-B.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage20: Explore the Registry Annex & Forgotten Crypt to find Form 27-B and the truth behind the altered records.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal20: Kaelen of the Ashbound warned me that the Registry Annex has sunk: its upper offices fell into an older crypt, and the skeletons inside still keep office hours. Whoever struck my name worked down there.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage30: Return to Clerk Oakhaven in Bellwether with Form 27-B and The Uncounted Ledger.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal30: Deep beneath the Annex I laid Chief Archivist Morvath's shade to rest and recovered Form 27-B and the Uncounted Ledger. The Archivists of Annex III have hidden names from something called the Hunger since the Great Silence. Seventeen years ago they hid Oakhallow, and me. The final folio says Bellwether will be struck at the next new moon unless the Seal of Names is signed again.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage100: Chapter Zero Complete: You entrusted the Uncounted Ledger to the Royal Bureau.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal100: I surrendered the Uncounted Ledger to Clerk Oakhaven. My legal existence is restored, my burial arrears are waived, and the Bureau has quietly dispatched riders to the capital. Whether the High Chroniclers mean to mend what lies beneath the Annex or bury it deeper, I can't yet say.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.stage101: Chapter Zero Complete: You kept the Uncounted Ledger for the Ashbound.
strings.quest.legally_deceased.journal101: I made Clerk Oakhaven stamp Form 27-B and kept the Uncounted Ledger out of the Bureau's hands. I am legally alive again, and I carry four hundred years of hidden names. The Ashbound will want to read them aloud.
strings.dlg.clerk.greeting: "Name? ...Ah. Deceased. Seventeen years ago, third column from the bottom." The clerk dips his quill without looking up. "Terribly sorry for your loss. If you're here to pay your burial arrears, the coffer is on the left. If you're here to complain about being dead, the queue is also on the left. It's the same coffer."
strings.dlg.clerk.explain_27b:
"Yes, and that's highly irregular." Oakhaven produces a pamphlet titled So You Are Unexpectedly Alive. "You'll need Form 27-B: Application for Temporary Exemption from Being Dead. Three copies, please.

Unfortunately our last stack was stored in the old Registry Annex down the eastern road. It was closed seventeen years ago for 'refurbishment'. Then the floorboards started humming, and nobody from the Bureau has been inclined to go and ask why."

He slides a brass key across the desk. "Fetch a copy yourself. Do try to come back alive. Well. More alive."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_persuade_fee: [Persuasion] "If I'm retrieving Bureau property from a hazardous ruin, I'm entitled to a courier stipend."
strings.dlg.clerk.persuade_stipend: Oakhaven blinks behind his spectacles, consults a subsection of the municipal code, and sighs. "Sub-clause 14: Perilous Retrieval by a Non-Living Contractor. Very well. Thirty-five crowns in advance. Try not to die a second time; the paperwork is dreadful."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_where_annex: "Remind me where the Registry Annex is."
strings.dlg.clerk.annex_directions: "Follow the cobbles east out of Bellwether onto the Old Road. Past Oakhallow's boundary stone, past the ruined watch-arch, and you'll find the Annex door set into the cliff. Go down. Keep going down. If the stairs are still going down when you think they shouldn't, that's the Annex."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_race_dwarf: [Dwarf] "My clan's stone-rolls don't misplace a living person by seventeen years, clerk."
strings.dlg.clerk.dwarf_remark: "With respect to the mountain vaults, master dwarf, parchment is much more accommodating when history changes its mind."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_race_elf: [Elf] "This ink smells of Silence-era abjuration, not clerical error."
strings.dlg.clerk.elf_remark: Oakhaven lowers his voice. "Then you understand why I don't go down into the Annex cellar myself."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_have_proof: "I have Form 27-B—and this Uncounted Ledger from the vault beneath the Annex."
strings.dlg.clerk.inspect_ledger:
Oakhaven's ink-stained fingers tremble as he turns the stone-vellum pages. "Annex III's hand. And this... these entries are dated next month."

He reads the final folio twice, then a third time with his lips moving. "It says the Great Silence wasn't a catastrophe. It was an erasure, deliberate, to hide people from something. It says the Seal beneath the Annex is failing and that Bellwether, this town, my office, my good inkwell, will be struck at the new moon."

He looks up. "Give me the Ledger. It belongs in the Royal Vault, where the High Chroniclers can decide what to do with it."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_surrender_ledger: "Take the Ledger. The Bureau has the resources to warn the realm."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_keep_ledger: "No. Stamp my Form 27-B, Oakhaven, and I'll take the Ledger to those who won't bury the truth."
strings.dlg.clerk.ending_bureau:
Oakhaven stamps Form 27-B with a resounding thud, then twice more for luck, and locks the Ledger inside his iron safe. "You are officially alive, citizen. Congratulations. Your burial arrears are hereby waived, and the Bureau treasury owes you compensation for seventeen years of being wrongly deceased."

He counts out the coins, then hesitates. "When the High Chroniclers read this, Edrath will never be the same. I only hope they read all of it."
strings.dlg.clerk.ending_independent:
Oakhaven swallows hard. Then he stamps your Form 27-B three times, signs it, countersigns it, and initials his own signature.

"Legally, you exist again. Off the record?" He glances at the window. "Run. If the Bureau learns that book walked out of this office, they'll send people who don't use forms. And if the Ledger is right, the road beyond Bellwether is waking up."

He presses a small purse into your hand. "Petty cash. For a courier who was never here."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_back: "Let's return to the matter at hand."
strings.dlg.merchant.greeting: "Welcome to Bellwether Provisions! Whether you're legally alive, administratively misplaced, or somewhere in between, your gold spends the same."
strings.dlg.merchant.choice_rumors: "Heard anything strange along the Old Road?"
strings.dlg.merchant.rumors:
"Caravan guards swear there used to be a whole market-borough two leagues east called Oakhallow. Nobody can remember who lived there, and the road-sign's been blank since before I took over this shop."

He taps a dusty account book. "But my predecessor's ledger, seventeen years old, says Oakhallow still owes this shop for twelve barrels of salt. Somebody existed long enough to run up a tab. If you meet them, mention it."
strings.dlg.marta.greeting: "Come in out of the damp, traveler. The fire's warm, even if half the town is pretending the sky doesn't look wrong at dusk."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_remember_me: "Do you remember me, Marta? The Bureau claims I died seventeen years ago."
strings.dlg.marta.remember_witness: Marta stares at you closely, rubbing her temples. "I... I remember pouring ale for your father when you were a child—no, wait. Half the memory feels like pages torn out of a book. Something in that Annex down the Old Road is eating our yesterdays."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_rest: "Could I rest by the hearth a moment?"
strings.dlg.marta.rested: "There now. Warm soup and a dry cloak do wonders for the living."
strings.dlg.fenwick.greeting: "Shh! Keep your voice down! And if you see a translucent gentleman shelving books in the history aisle, do NOT engage him."
strings.dlg.fenwick.ghost_fees: "Certainly not! Hauntings require municipal certification. Those apparitions are merely delinquent patrons who expired before paying their late fees—and until they settle three centuries of overdue fines, I refuse to acknowledge them!"
strings.dlg.fenwick.choice_train_magic: "Can you teach me anything of Collegium magic?"
strings.dlg.fenwick.train_magic: "A fellow seeker of illumination! Take this Glimmer primer and remember: light reveals what the ledgers try to hide."
strings.dlg.aldous.greeting: "May the Last Dawn keep your name written in the sun's memory, traveler."
strings.dlg.aldous.choice_silence: "What does the Church teach about the Great Silence?"
strings.dlg.aldous.great_silence: "That the gods drew a curtain of mercy across a broken world. Though between you and me... curtains are meant to keep something out, not merely hide the view."
strings.dlg.aldous.choice_blessing: "I could use a blessing for the road ahead."
strings.dlg.aldous.blessed: Aldous traces a warm golden circle above your brow. Your wounds ache less.
strings.dlg.scout.greeting: "Halt—ah, steady. You don't move like one of those bone-rattlers from the ruin. I'm Kaelen of the Ashbound."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_annex: "I'm heading into the Registry Annex for Form 27-B."
strings.dlg.scout.annex_warning: "Watch your footing inside. The upper offices collapsed into an older pre-Silence vault. Look for an iron wall-lever in the eastern archive to raise the crypt portcullis—and check the cracked northern wall if you have keen eyes."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_orc_kinship: [Orc] "Good to see another of the marches out here, Kaelen."
strings.dlg.scout.orc_gift: "Blood and stone, cousin! Take these healing draughts. Don't let the Bureau clerks write your story for you."
strings.dlg.spirit.greeting: "...Are you real? Or another line of ink waiting to be scraped from the vellum?"
strings.dlg.spirit.choice_who: "Who are you? What happened in this vault?"
strings.dlg.spirit.explain_prison:
The spirit gathers itself, thin as breath on glass. "I was an Archivist of Annex III. Our order has kept the Uncounted Vaults since the Great Silence: four hundred years of quiet clerks guarding names the world must not speak."

"Seventeen years ago the Seal of Names cracked. Chief Archivist Morvath ordered the erasure. A whole town in one night, into the Ledger. Then he bound himself to the book so that nothing could ever take it, and the binding ate him. He guards it still, in the northern sanctum, and he no longer knows what he's guarding it from."

A cold key settles into your palm. "Open the sanctum. Set him free. Read the Ledger. The ink is fading, and when it is gone, Bellwether is next."
strings.map.edrath.name: The Borderlands of Edrath
strings.story.prologue.1:
Edrath, in the four hundred and twelfth year after the Great Silence.

The kingdoms keep their ledgers carefully now. What is written down, exists. What is struck out was never there at all.
strings.story.prologue.2:
Seventeen years ago, by order of the Royal Bureau of Records, you died.

You do not remember it. Nobody does. That is rather the point of a ledger.
strings.story.prologue.3: This morning a notice arrived anyway, sealed in Bureau wax: proof of your death, and a bill for your burial.
strings.story.prologue.4: So you have walked to Bellwether, where the rain never quite stops, to argue with a clerk about whether you are alive.
strings.ui.prologue.continue: Click or press E to continue
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.title: A Name Worth Keeping
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.summary: Someone scratched a question onto Oakhallow's boundary stone: why do they remember a baker's daughter from a town that no longer exists?
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage0: Ask Marta at the Lantern Inn about Oakhallow and its baker's daughter.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal0: Oakhallow's boundary stone claims 412 souls lived where the forest now stands. Beneath the carving, fresh charcoal: "Why do I remember the baker's daughter?" Marta bakes Bellwether's bread. If anyone remembers a baker, it might be her.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage10: Search the Registry Annex's archive for any record of Oakhallow's baker and his daughter.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal10: Marta's hands knew the Oakhallow braid before her mind did. She remembers a girl with flour on her nose who taught her to fold the dough, but not the girl's name, nor any town called Oakhallow. If the Bureau ever wrote the child down, the record is in the Annex.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage20: The girl was Ilse Brannock. Ask the Uncounted Witness in the crypt what "moved to Vault III" means.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal20: A struck census folio names the baker's household: Tomas Brannock and his daughter Ilse, aged nine, "moved to Vault III for safekeeping." The spirit in the crypt calls itself a remnant of Annex III.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.stage30: Return to Bellwether and speak Ilse Brannock's name to Marta.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal30: The Witness says the Archivists hid the children first: names into the Ledger, bodies into a long sleep, memories out of every mind that loved them. But a name held truly by someone who remembers cannot be unmade. Marta still dreams of the girl with flour on her nose. I should say the name to her.
strings.quest.bakers_daughter.journal100: I said the name aloud in the Lantern Inn and Marta's face changed like a window opening. Ilse was her little sister. Marta is a Brannock too, sent to Bellwether seventeen years ago under a borrowed name, with her memories sealed and nothing left of her family but a bread recipe she couldn't explain. She is baking the braid again tonight.
strings.dlg.marta.choice_oakhallow: "Do you know anything about a town called Oakhallow? Or a baker's daughter?"
strings.dlg.marta.oakhallow:
Marta's hands stop moving in the dough. "Oakhallow... no. Never heard of it." She looks down. Her fingers have folded the loaf into a tight four-strand braid without her noticing. "That's odd. A girl taught me this. Flour on her nose, laughing at my clumsy knots. I can see her plain as day. I can't for the life of me tell you her name."

She wipes her hands slowly. "If the Bureau ever wrote her down, it'll be in those vaults under the Annex. Find her for me?"
strings.dlg.marta.choice_ilse: "Marta... the baker's daughter. Her name was Ilse. Ilse Brannock."
strings.dlg.marta.ilse:
For a long moment Marta doesn't breathe. Then she laughs, and the laugh breaks halfway into something else.

"Ilse. Little Ilse. She was my sister. We grew up above our father's ovens on Mill Lane, in Oakhallow. Kettleburn isn't even my name. It's the name on the paper they gave me when I woke up in Bellwether, seventeen, with a bread recipe and no family. Brannock. I'm Marta Brannock."

"Seventeen years I've been baking her braid and I couldn't remember why." She presses a warm loaf and a pouch of coins into your hands. "Don't argue. Somebody gave me back my family today. Bread is the least I can do."
strings.dlg.spirit.choice_ilse: "Do you know what became of a girl named Ilse Brannock? Her record says 'moved to Vault III'."
strings.dlg.spirit.ilse:
The spirit flickers like a candle in a draught. "Vault III. The children's vault. We hid them first. Their names went into the Ledger, their bodies into a long sleep, their memories out of every mind that loved them. That was the price: the Hunger cannot find what no one remembers."

"But a name held truly by someone who remembers cannot be unmade. If anyone still dreams of her, say her name to them. Say it aloud."
strings.bark.marta.1: Mind the puddles. Seventeen years of rain, and the roof still finds new ways to leak.
strings.bark.marta.2: Odd. I keep setting out one more bowl than I have guests.
strings.bark.marta.3: Bread's nearly done. Smells like winter mornings somewhere I've never been.
strings.bark.marta.ilse: I've baked the braid for her again. Silly, isn't it? It's good to be silly.
strings.bark.vaelen.1: Potions, arrows, lockpicks! Everything a dead person needs!
strings.bark.vaelen.2: The Bureau taxes the living and the dead alike. Guess which pays more reliably.
strings.bark.vaelen.3: Heading east? Buy two of everything. Nobody comes back from the Annex with change.
strings.bark.fenwick.2: The history aisle is closed. For... reshelving. Indefinitely.
strings.bark.fenwick.3: Three centuries of overdue fines. I will collect. Eventually.
strings.bark.aldous.1: The sun remembers what we forget.
strings.bark.aldous.2: Pray for the uncounted, friend. Even if you cannot remember who they were.
strings.bark.clerk.1: Form 88-A is for vanished spouses. Form 27-B is for vanished selves.
strings.bark.clerk.2: Next! ...Ah. The deceased. Still upright, I see.
strings.bark.clerk.3: Have you retrieved the form? The Bureau does not accept 'I was busy being dead'.
strings.bark.scout.1: Hear that? The road hums at night. Like a choir with no mouths.
strings.bark.scout.2: Every stone out here was somebody's doorstep once.
strings.bark.scout.3: Back from the dark, and still yourself? Good. Keep it that way.
strings.bark.spirit.1: Say my name... no. I have forgotten it too.
strings.bark.spirit.2: The ink is cold down here. It remembers everything we tried not to.
strings.line.sentinel.alert: HALT. YOUR NAME IS NOT ON THE LIST.
strings.line.keeper.alert: A name walks in my halls. I will strike it from the page!
strings.line.keeper.death: The ink... is running. Forgive me, little ones...
strings.ending.ilse: In the Lantern Inn, Marta now bakes an Oakhallow braid every morning and sets it by the window. She says it is for someone who is coming home.
strings.map.vault_three.name: Vault III: The Nursery
strings.quest.vault_three.title: The Sleepers of Vault III
strings.quest.vault_three.summary: Beneath the crypt, the Archivists hid the children of erased towns in an enchanted sleep. Something down there is still keeping them.
strings.quest.vault_three.stage0: Follow the floury handprints down into Vault III.
strings.quest.vault_three.journal0: In the crypt, a child's handprints in old flour lead to a gap in the west wall and a stair going down, deeper than the Annex was ever built.
strings.quest.vault_three.stage10: The hidden children sleep in the Nursery. Find what keeps them asleep: descend to the Seal Chamber.
strings.quest.vault_three.journal10: I found Ilse Brannock asleep beneath clouded glass, nine years old for seventeen years, whispering her sister's name. Rows of small sarcophagi line the Nursery, forty of them. Someone below is still singing them to sleep. The Night-Warden's hymnal speaks of a Seal that must be signed before morning can come.
strings.quest.vault_three.stage100: Completed: you signed the Seal of Names.
strings.quest.vault_three.journal100: The Lullaby Warden sang its last verse and fell silent. I signed the Seal of Names with my own name, the one the Bureau struck out seventeen years ago, and the ink held. The sleepers are safe a while longer, and Bellwether will not be uncounted at the new moon. The rain over the village has stopped.
strings.story.seal.1:
The quill is cold, and the ink beneath it is older than the Bureau, older than Edrath's kings.

The Seal asks only one thing: a name, written by its owner, freely given.
strings.story.seal.2:
You write the name the Bureau struck out seventeen years ago. Your own.

For a moment the ink does not take. Then, letter by letter, it soaks into the vellum like rain into dry ground.
strings.story.seal.3: All around the chamber, the old runes on the monoliths brighten, then settle to a steady glow. Somewhere above, in the Nursery, forty small chests rise and fall a little easier.
strings.story.seal.4: And far above the Annex, above the Old Road, the rain over Bellwether stops for the first time in seventeen years.
strings.flour.handprints.title: Handprints in Old Flour
strings.item.seal_quill.name: Archivist's Seal-Quill
strings.item.seal_quill.desc: A raven quill with a nib of black iron, still wet with ink that never dries. It wrote the Seal of Names. Worn at the belt, it steadies the mind. +2 Will, +2 Intellect.
strings.enemy.lullaby_warden.name: The Lullaby Warden
strings.line.warden.alert: Hush now. Hush. It isn't morning yet.
strings.line.warden.death: Who will... sing them... to sleep...
strings.ending.seal: Beneath the Annex, the Seal of Names holds, signed in your own hand. The rain has stopped over Bellwether, and at the next new moon the village is still on every map.
strings.map.seal_chamber.name: The Seal Chamber
strings.dlg.marta.choice_sleeper: "Beneath the Annex, there's a girl asleep under glass. Flour on her hands. She looked like you."
strings.dlg.marta.sleeper_unnamed:
Marta sets the bread knife down very carefully, as if it might break.

"Asleep. Under the ground." She presses a floury palm flat against her chest. "That's a cruel story to tell a baker, traveler. Why does it hurt like it's mine?"

She shakes her head. "If she has a name, find it. I can't. I've tried."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_ilse_alive: "Marta, there's more. Ilse isn't dead. I found her asleep in a vault beneath the Annex."
strings.dlg.marta.ilse_alive:
Marta grips the edge of the counter. "Asleep." Her voice is very small. "Seventeen years, and she's still nine?"

You tell her about the Nursery: the clouded glass, the rows of little sarcophagi, the girl whispering her sister's name.

"Then something down there is keeping her." Marta wipes her eyes with the back of her wrist and leaves a streak of flour. "Whatever it is, you go back down and you make it stop singing. Please. I'll keep the hearth lit."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_ilse_alive_safe: "Marta, Ilse isn't dead. She's asleep beneath the Annex, and she's safe now. I signed the Seal that keeps them."
strings.dlg.marta.ilse_alive_safe:
Marta sits down on the flour sacks as if her knees have simply quit.

"Asleep. Safe." She looks toward the window, at the dry street and the first clean sky Bellwether has seen in seventeen years. "That's why the rain stopped, isn't it? You did that."

She takes your hand in both of hers. They are warm and smell of yeast. "When she wakes she'll want breakfast. She always wanted breakfast. I'll be ready."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_seal_signed: "I went back down, Marta. The Warden is silent and the Seal is signed. Ilse is safe."
strings.dlg.marta.seal_signed:
Marta closes her eyes and listens: no rain on the shutters, only the fire. "I heard it stop. I was kneading and the whole house went quiet, and I knew."

She presses a warm loaf into your arms, wrapped in a cloth embroidered with an oak leaf. "Oakhallow's mark. I didn't know I could sew it until this morning."
strings.bark.marta.dry: No rain. I keep going to the window to make sure.
strings.bark.marta.alive: Every morning I set the braid by the window. Every morning is one closer.
strings.dlg.clerk.rain_stopped:
"Yes. I noticed." Oakhaven straightens a stack of forms that is already straight. "I've filed it under Irregularities, Meteorological. Then something else happened, and I have no form for it."

He opens the great register of the dead and turns it toward you. Your entry has faded to the colour of weak tea. Beneath it, in a neat grey hand that is not his, forty new lines have appeared overnight. All children. Some from Oakhallow, some from places he has never heard of. Every one is marked not deceased, held in trust.

"Whoever you are," he says quietly, "I think the Bureau owes you an apology. I'm not authorised to issue one. Consider this... unofficial."
strings.bark.clerk.dry: Forty new entries overnight, and none of them in my handwriting. Most irregular. Most... welcome.
strings.bark.clerk.puddles: My inkwell has been watered down by the leak for seventeen years. Today it isn't. I don't trust it.
strings.ending.ilse_alive: She tells everyone who asks that her sister is only sleeping, and for once in Bellwether nobody argues with a record.
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_who_struck: "Who actually struck my name, Oakhaven? Somebody wrote me down as dead."
strings.dlg.clerk.who_struck:
Oakhaven pages back through the register of the dead until the paper changes colour. "Here. Your entry, and a few hundred others, all in one night, seventeen years ago. The strike-marks came down from Annex III, the old Archive office. Annex III struck names; we downstairs simply recorded what was left. A struck name with no body attached goes in the deceased column. That's procedure."

He hesitates. "Annex III was staffed by Archivists. Old order. Older than the Bureau, some said. Very quiet, very polite, wore a great deal of grey. One morning they simply weren't there any more, and the building had sunk two storeys into the hill. I filed it under Subsidence."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_key_paradox: "This key says 'Do not enter without Form 27-B'. The form is inside."
strings.dlg.clerk.key_paradox:
"Yes." Oakhaven considers this for a long moment. "Yes, I see the difficulty."

He takes out a fresh sheet, writes TEMPORARY WAIVER OF THE REQUIREMENT TO HOLD FORM 27-B IN ORDER TO OBTAIN FORM 27-B, stamps it twice, and folds it into your pocket. "There. If any skeletons ask, show them that."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_arrears: "And if I simply don't pay the burial tax?"
strings.dlg.clerk.arrears:
"Then you'll be posthumously in arrears, and the Bureau will pursue your estate." He checks a ledger. "Your estate was auctioned seventeen years ago to pay for your funeral. Which you did not attend. Which is, in fairness, traditional."

"In practice," he lowers his voice, "nobody has ever collected from the dead. They are notoriously hard to find. You, unfortunately, are standing in my office."
strings.dlg.clerk.choice_have_proof_sealed: "I have Form 27-B, the Uncounted Ledger, and some good news about the new moon."
strings.dlg.clerk.inspect_ledger_sealed:
Oakhaven turns the stone-vellum pages with the care of a man defusing something. He reaches the final folio and stops.

The prophecy is still there: a traveller, a notice of death, Bellwether struck at the new moon. But beneath it the page has written one more line, in fresh dark ink that smells faintly of rain:

"The Seal is signed. Bellwether is counted."

Oakhaven reads it several times. "I have worked for the Bureau for thirty-one years," he says at last, "and this is the first document that has ever made me want to weep. Now. The Ledger belongs in the Royal Vault. Doesn't it?"
strings.bark.clerk.4: If you're here about the floorboards humming, that's Form 61-H. We're out of those as well.
strings.dlg.merchant.choice_rumors_bureau: "What do you make of the Bureau?"
strings.dlg.merchant.rumors_bureau:
"The Bureau?" Vaelen grins. "Finest customers in Edrath. They buy ink by the barrel, parchment by the cartload, and every winter they order a hundred candles for a building they've never set foot in."

"The old Annex on the Old Road. Paid in advance, every year, for seventeen years. Delivery instructions: leave at the door, do not knock, do not listen to the singing." He shrugs. "I don't. A merchant's ears are for prices."
strings.bark.vaelen.dry: Rain's stopped. Do you know how many oilskin cloaks I'm holding? I blame you, somehow.
strings.dlg.marta.news:
"News?" Marta laughs and slaps flour off her apron. "Vaelen's raised the price of lamp oil again. Fenwick's cats have been banned from the library, and the library has been banned from Fenwick's cats. And the Bureau sent a man to count the rain barrels, so now we have to pay tax on weather."

Her smile thins. "And people keep forgetting things. Not keys and kettles. Whole streets. Old Hobb swore last week his cottage used to have a neighbour. Now there's a hedge there, and the hedge looks very sure of itself."
strings.dlg.marta.choice_father: "Marta... do you remember your father? Tomas Brannock, the baker."
strings.dlg.marta.father:
Marta is quiet for a long time. Her hands go on kneading without her.

"I remember his hands. Burn scars across both thumbs from the oven door. He hummed when the bread was proving, always the same four notes." She hums them, and stops. "That's all. I can't see his face. I've been trying all night."

She sets the dough aside. "The census had his name struck through in red, didn't it. Not 'moved'. Not 'held in trust'. Just struck." She nods slowly, as if agreeing with someone. "Then I'll remember his hands. It's more than the Bureau left me."
strings.dlg.fenwick.history:
Fenwick glances left, glances right, and beckons you to the roped-off shelf. He pulls down a volume: A Gazetteer of the Eastern Marches. Half the pages are blank. Not torn out. Blank, with page numbers.

"Seventeen years ago, overnight, every book in this library that mentioned Oakhallow forgot it. Gazetteers, tax rolls, a very bad romance novel set at the Oakhallow summer fair. All blank." He reshelves it lovingly. "A blank book is still a book. It is still due back on Thursday. But I couldn't bear the patrons asking what used to be written there."
strings.dlg.fenwick.choice_history_after: "Has anything come back to the history aisle?"
strings.dlg.fenwick.history_after:
Fenwick is standing in the history aisle with a candle and an expression of profound, trembling joy.

"Page forty-one of the Gazetteer. 'Oakhallow: a market-borough known for its braided breads, its summer fair, and its unusually litigious goats.' It came back this morning." He clutches the book. "And the romance novel. All of it. It is so much worse than I remembered. I've never been happier."
strings.bark.fenwick.dry: Ink is coming back to the blank pages. Shh. Shh! I'm trying to watch.
strings.dlg.aldous.hunger:
Aldous stops smiling. "Not in the pulpit. In the margins. The oldest hymnals have a verse the Church stopped singing: 'Speak not the names of the hidden, lest the Hunger hear and come to dine.'"

"We teach that the Great Silence was the gods drawing a curtain of mercy. The margins say something hungry lives beyond the edge of the world and finds its way in through names, the way a draught finds a keyhole. The Silence was not the gods. It was clerks. Very brave clerks, with very good ink."

He smiles again, a little shakily. "Don't repeat that to the Bishop. He's terribly fond of the curtain."
strings.dlg.aldous.bells:
"It has. And at noon the chapel bell rang by itself, forty times. I counted." Aldous looks up at the clear sky as if it might be withdrawn. "Forty. I don't know what it was counting. But I wrote it down, and I'll keep writing it down, every day, so it can't be lost."

"That's what the Ashbound say, isn't it? Somebody has to remember things on purpose."
strings.bark.aldous.dry: Forty bells at noon. I wrote it down. I'll write it down again tomorrow.
strings.dlg.scout.ashbound:
Kaelen taps a charcoal-stained journal. "Chroniclers. Walkers. People who noticed that the maps keep getting smaller and decided to be rude about it."

"When a village vanishes, the Bureau files it. We go and look. We count the wells, the hearthstones, the graves. We write down what we find on paper the Bureau doesn't own, and then we read it aloud to each other round the fire, so it's written in more than one place." A shrug. "Ash is what's left when something burns. It still remembers the shape of the wood."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_ledger: "I found the Uncounted Ledger beneath the Annex."
strings.dlg.scout.ledger:
Kaelen goes very still. "Show me." Kaelen reads with moving lips, gets as far as Folio IX, and sits down in the middle of the road.

"Four hundred and twelve. I counted their wells." The Ledger comes back to you carefully, in both hands. "The Ashbound would keep this safe and read it aloud until every name in it is remembered by somebody. The Bureau would lock it in a vault. I can't make you choose. But I know which one I'd trust with my name."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_road_quiet: "Do you hear the road humming now?"
strings.dlg.scout.road_quiet:
Kaelen goes quiet and listens. Wind in the pines. A bird. Nothing else.

"It stopped at dawn. First quiet night on this road since I started walking it." Kaelen studies you with new interest. "Whatever you did down there, I'm writing it down. Your name too, if you'll let me. In ink the Bureau doesn't own."
strings.bark.scout.dry: Listen. Nothing. Do you know how long I've waited to hear nothing?
strings.dlg.spirit.choice_oakhallow: "What happened to the rest of Oakhallow?"
strings.dlg.spirit.oakhallow:
The spirit is silent so long you think it has faded. "Four hundred and twelve," it says at last. "Forty children we carried below to the Nursery. Some of the grown ones we scattered with their memories sealed: a baker's eldest to Bellwether, others down the road to wherever there was room."

"The rest... The Hunger came through the crack before the ink was dry. It does not kill. It unwrites. There is nothing left of them to bury, and nothing to mourn, because no one remembers there was anyone. That is why I stayed. Someone had to remember that there was something to forget."
strings.dlg.spirit.morvath:
"Don't be." The spirit's outline steadies, a little. "He used to bring honey cakes down to the Nursery on feast days and leave one on every lid. He wrote every name in that Ledger himself, so that if anyone ever came to undo it, they would know he had not done it lightly."

"He would have stamped your Form 27-B, you know. He hated being responsible for anyone being dead. Especially on paper."
strings.dlg.spirit.choice_remembered: "The Seal is signed. Do you feel any different?"
strings.dlg.spirit.remembered:
The spirit brightens like a lamp turned up. For the first time you can see a face: young, ink-stained, ears that stick out a little.

"Wendel," it says, astonished. "Wendel Ashcombe. Junior Archivist. Filing." A pause. "And misfiling, on occasion. Morvath said I had a gift for it."

"I remember my mother's kitchen. I remember I was owed two weeks' wages." It laughs, a dry papery sound. "Thank you. When the children wake, tell them a clerk named Wendel kept the lamps lit. I think I can rest now. Eventually. I'd like to see the sky once, first."
strings.bark.spirit.named: Wendel Ashcombe. Wendel Ashcombe. I like saying it.
strings.ending.marta_testimony: Marta's testimony that she remembered you was entered into the record: the first living witness in seventeen years.
strings.ending.spirit_waiting: Somewhere beneath the Annex, a spirit with no name waits for the Seal to be renewed.
strings.ending.spirit_named: Down in the Nursery, a junior archivist named Wendel Ashcombe keeps the lamps lit, and signs his name on everything.
strings.ending.no_seal: Bellwether will be uncounted at the next new moon, unless someone does something about it.
strings.game.dedication: For Toasty, the TaoistDragon. Get well soon, friend.
strings.item.letter_opener.name: Morvath's Letter-Opener
strings.item.letter_opener.description: The Chief Archivist's silver letter-opener. Slits envelopes, wax seals and, it is rumoured, one auditor. Tiny, fast and vicious: built for critical hits.
strings.item.baggy_umbrella.name: Baggy's Trusty Umbrella
strings.item.baggy_umbrella.description: A furled black umbrella with a hooked cane handle. Baggy carried it for seventeen years in Bellwether's rain and never once opened it, "for dramatic reasons". Quick, well balanced, and the brass ferrule picks a lock if you're patient.
strings.item.sabrino_hat.name: Sabrino's Pointed Hat
strings.item.sabrino_hat.description: Tall, dented and gloriously purple, with a sash that smells of garlic and brimstone. Makes your spells hit harder and your opinions louder. Mildly cursed: you can't stop thinking about dinner.
strings.item.tome_frost.name: Tome: Frost Lance
strings.item.tome_frost.description: Use from inventory to permanently learn Frost Lance.
strings.item.tome_siphon.name: Tome: Siphon Ink
strings.item.tome_siphon.description: Use from inventory to permanently learn Siphon Ink. The pages are blotted with something that isn't quite ink.
strings.item.tome_sabrino.name: Grimoire: Sabrino's Questionable Fireball
strings.item.tome_sabrino.description: Use from inventory to learn Sabrino's Questionable Fireball. Banned by the Bureau, the Collegium, and two cookery schools. The margins are full of recipes.
strings.book.tome_frost.text: On the Patience of Ice: Fire is impatient. Frost waits. Draw the cold out of the air, sharpen it on your breath, and let it fly faster than the warmth can follow.
strings.book.tome_siphon.text: Litany of the Dawn, Read Backwards: What the wound takes, the hand may take back. Strike with ink; drink the ink. The Church does not teach this page. The Church tore this page out. Somebody glued it back in.
strings.book.tome_sabrino.text:
SABRINO'S QUESTIONABLE FIREBALL
(a recipe, sort of)

Ingredients:
- One fireball, standard
- A second fireball, hidden inside the first
- Garlic (for flavour)
- Absolutely no restraint

Method:
Gather the flame in both hands as if kneading dough. Whisper something rude about the Bureau. Throw. The fireball bursts on impact and singes everything within a good three paces, including, if you are careless, yourself, the furniture and the wedding cake.

Note from the author: The Bureau classifies this spell as a war crime. I classify it as dinner.
strings.spell.frost_lance.name: Frost Lance
strings.spell.frost_lance.desc: A fast shard of ice. Hits harder than Ember Bolt and flies straighter, but costs more mana.
strings.spell.siphon_ink.name: Siphon Ink
strings.spell.siphon_ink.desc: A slow bolt of black ink that returns 60% of the damage it deals to you as health. Governed by Restoration.
strings.spell.sabrino_fireball.name: Sabrino's Questionable Fireball
strings.spell.sabrino_fireball.desc: A slow, heavy fireball that bursts on impact, scorching every enemy within 3.5 m. Expensive, glorious, and legally a war crime.
strings.synergy.sabrino.name: Sabrino's Doctrine
strings.synergy.sabrino.desc: Set it on fire, then convince everyone you weren't there. Banned in three kingdoms and one cookery school.
strings.synergy.baggy.name: Baggy's Hunch
strings.synergy.baggy.desc: You notice the weak spot, eventually. People tell you things, because you look as though you'd mean well with them.
strings.synergy.cutpurse.name: Cutpurse's Grace
strings.synergy.cutpurse.desc: Quick fingers, quicker blade. Locks open and arteries too.
strings.synergy.liturgy.name: Iron Liturgy
strings.synergy.liturgy.desc: Every blow is a prayer, and the Dawn answers: wounds you deal knit your own.
strings.npc.detective_baggy.name: Baggy
strings.npc.detective_baggy.title: Private Eye (Licence Pending)
strings.dlg.baggy.greeting:
A figure in a long, rain-dark coat is studying the boundary stone through a magnifying glass, very closely, from the wrong side.

"Ah! A witness. Or a suspect. Possibly both, it's early in the investigation." A hand is offered, then withdrawn to check for clues, then offered again. "Baggy. Private eye. Mostly private. The eye is still in training."
strings.dlg.baggy.case:
"The Case of the Missing Town." Baggy lowers the magnifying glass dramatically. "This stone says four hundred and twelve people lived here. I have searched every inch of this forest, and I have found: zero people, one bucket, and a goat who refused to answer questions."

"So either the stone is lying, or someone made a whole town disappear. I don't think stones lie." A pause. "That's actually my best clue."
strings.dlg.baggy.board:
"Be my guest! It's all on the board." Baggy waves at the lectern behind. "I've narrowed it down to four suspects. One of them is the hedge."

Leaning in, conspiratorially: "Between us? I don't think it was the hedge. But you have to rule these things out. That's procedure. I read it in a pamphlet."
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_stone: "Somebody wrote on this stone in charcoal. 'Why do I remember the baker's daughter?' Was that you?"
strings.dlg.baggy.stone:
Baggy goes a bit pink. "Ah. You've cracked it. Yes. That was me. Note to self. I'm terrible at remembering where I put things, so I write them on the nearest flat surface."

The magnifying glass is turned over and over in nervous hands. "When I was little, seven maybe, a girl with flour on her nose gave me a sweet roll. Still warm. She said I looked like I needed it, which was true. I can see her face plain as anything. I can't remember her name, or the town, or my own street."

"Everybody in Bellwether says I'm imagining it. I'm a detective. I don't imagine things. I deduce them, badly, but sincerely."
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_ilse: "Baggy, the baker's daughter. Her name was Ilse Brannock. You weren't imagining her."
strings.dlg.baggy.ilse:
For once Baggy says nothing at all. The magnifying glass slowly lowers.

"Ilse," Baggy says, very softly, trying the name out like a key in a lock. "Ilse Brannock. Mill Lane. The bakery with the blue shutters." A shaky laugh. "Oh, I remember the shutters now. I REMEMBER THE SHUTTERS."

The umbrella is pressed into your hands. "Here. Take it. A good detective knows when someone else solved the case. I'm not a good detective, but I know that much." A sniff. "Case closed. Well. One case. The goat is still a person of interest."
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_thanks: "Thank you, Baggy. You never gave up on her."
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_sabrino: "Have you ever heard of a witch called Sabrino?"
strings.dlg.baggy.sabrino:
Baggy brightens like a lamp. "The Sabrino Affair! My first case! The Bureau hired me to tail the Italian Witch. I followed Sabrino for three weeks."

"Every single night Sabrino would turn around, spot me hiding behind a barrel, and invite me to dinner. Every night! Gnocchi. Risotto. Something on fire for dessert, which I think was on purpose."

A satisfied sigh. "I never caught Sabrino. I did gain eleven pounds. Best case of my life. Don't tell the Bureau."
strings.dlg.baggy.sabrino_where:
Baggy taps the side of a nose. "Professional secret. But." A glance up and down the road. "Last time I saw Sabrino, the hat was getting caught on every branch on this road. Said something about hiding it 'under a pine on the north side of the road, back toward Bellwether, right up against the wall, where the Bureau never looks because the Bureau never looks at anything.'"

"I never went to look. Felt rude. You go. Tell me if there's garlic involved. There's always garlic involved."
strings.dlg.baggy.advice:
Baggy produces a battered notebook titled DETECTIVE'S RULES (DRAFT).

"Rule one: look for weak spots. Agility and a sharp eye make you land the lucky blow more often. Every point of Agility over ten is half a chance in a hundred, and Perception adds more as it grows. Daggers love a critical hit. That letter-opener the Archivists kept? Vicious. Allegedly. I've never seen it. I'd like to."

"Rule two: skills that grow together help each other. Train two that suit each other and something clicks. Check your Character sheet, it lists every pairing, and the Combat Sheet shows the numbers."
strings.dlg.baggy.advice2:
"Rule three: a mace cracks bones better than a blade. The skeletons in that Annex absolutely hate it. Rule four: spells cost less as you practise them, and a good hat helps more than you'd think. Rule five-"

Baggy squints at the page. "Rule five just says 'buy more bread'. I stand by it."

"Rule six is the important one: when somebody's having a rotten time, sit with them a while. You don't have to solve anything. Just be there. That's most of the job, honestly."
strings.dlg.baggy.rain:
Baggy is staring straight up at the clear sky with deep professional suspicion.

"Seventeen years of drizzle, and now this. Blue. Bright. Open. Nothing that open is innocent." A long pause. "I've been carrying an umbrella my whole adult life. I don't know what to do with my arms."

Then, quietly, a grin. "It's nice, though. Isn't it? I think I'll write it down. 'Weather: suspicious. Mood: excellent.'"
strings.bark.baggy.1: Hmm. That hedge has moved. Or I have. Noting it down.
strings.bark.baggy.3: If anyone asks, I'm undercover. As a person standing in the rain.
strings.bark.baggy.4: Four hundred and twelve. That's a lot of people to misplace. Even for the Bureau.
strings.bark.baggy.ilse: Blue shutters. I remember the blue shutters.
strings.bark.baggy.dry: No rain. Highly suspicious. Delightful, but suspicious.
strings.bark.clerk.sabrino: Form 13-S: Sightings of the Witch Sabrino. We have nine hundred of those. Most are of the hat.
strings.bark.fenwick.sabrino: Eleven years overdue. ELEVEN. And the return slot still smells of garlic.
strings.dlg.fenwick.overdue:
Fenwick's eye twitches. "Sabrino." He says it the way other men say plague. "Cooking With Fire: One Hundred and One Recipes, borrowed eleven years ago. Renewed once, by fireball, through the window."

"Every year on the due date a postcard arrives. 'Still reading! Page 40 is magnificent! - S.' Page 40 is the soufflé. Nobody needs eleven years for the soufflé." He straightens his robes. "If you ever find that book, I will waive every fine you have ever incurred. And the cats will forgive you."
strings.item.sabrino_gnocchi.name: Sabrino's Gnocchi
strings.item.sabrino_gnocchi.description: Pillowy potato gnocchi in brown butter and sage. Eating it feels like being hugged by someone who believes in you. +15% spell power for 5 minutes.
strings.item.ash_pepper_stew.name: Ash-Pepper Stew
strings.item.ash_pepper_stew.description: Hot enough to make your eyes water and your aim improve. Nobody understands why. +8% critical chance for 5 minutes.
strings.item.oakhallow_braid.name: Oakhallow Braid
strings.item.oakhallow_braid.description: Marta's four-strand braid, baked the way a girl with flour on her nose once taught her. Slowly mends you: +1.5 health per second for 5 minutes.
strings.item.sweet_roll.name: Baggy's Emergency Sweet Roll
strings.item.sweet_roll.description: Slightly squashed from living in a coat pocket. Baggy keeps a supply 'for clues and emergencies'. +0.3 critical multiplier for 3 minutes.
strings.item.grave_truffle.name: Grave-cap Truffle
strings.item.grave_truffle.description: A knobbly black truffle that grows only where it's very quiet for a very long time. Sabrino would know what to do with it.
strings.item.ash_pepper.name: Ash-Pepper
strings.item.ash_pepper.description: A glowing red gland from an Ash Crawler. Hot to the touch. Sabrino calls it 'the only good thing about those horrible little ovens with legs'.
strings.item.vallo_red.name: Bottle of Vallo Red
strings.item.vallo_red.description: A dusty bottle of good red wine from the hills of Vallo. Vaelen swears it's the last one. Vaelen swears that about every bottle.
strings.item.ladle_of_justice.name: The Ladle of Justice
strings.item.ladle_of_justice.description: Sabrino's own copper ladle, warm from a hundred kitchens. It has stirred risottos, settled arguments and once, memorably, a ghost. Restores mana on every hit and is unkind to spirits.
strings.item.bone_spectacles.name: Bone Clerk's Spectacles
strings.item.bone_spectacles.description: Wire-rimmed reading glasses, still perched on the nose of a clerk who had no nose. Everything looks slightly more like a typo. +1 Intellect, +5% critical chance, +5% lockpick chance.
strings.enemy.bone_clerk.name: Bone Clerk
strings.enemy.ink_wraith.name: Ink Wraith
strings.enemy.truffle_hog.name: Truffle Hog
strings.quest.dinner.title: Dinner at Eight
strings.quest.dinner.summary: Sabrino, the Italian Witch, is in Bellwether and has decided this sad, rainy town needs a proper dinner. Everyone is invited. Especially the lonely ones.
strings.quest.dinner.stage0: Sabrino's note says dinner is at eight. Find Sabrino: a witch would hide in the warmest kitchen in Bellwether, the Lantern Inn.
strings.quest.dinner.journal0: Sabrino's note under the pine ended with a dinner invitation. The Bureau has chased Sabrino across three kingdoms, and Sabrino still finds time to invite the detective who's tailing them to dinner. I should find this witch.
strings.quest.dinner.stage10: Bring Sabrino a Grave-cap Truffle (they grow in the crypts, and the Truffle Hogs love them), Ash-Pepper (from an Ash Crawler) and a bottle of Vallo Red (Vaelen sells it).
strings.quest.dinner.journal10: Sabrino is cooking in the Lantern Inn's kitchen and has decided Bellwether needs a feast. 'Seventeen years of rain and nobody has eaten together? Unacceptable.' I'm the one gathering ingredients, apparently.
strings.quest.dinner.stage20: Invite at least three guests to dinner at the Lantern Inn, then tell Sabrino. Marta, Baggy, Kaelen, Fenwick, Brother Aldous, Clerk Oakhaven and Vaelen could all use a good meal.
strings.quest.dinner.journal20: The ingredients are in the pot and the inn smells like a dream. Now we need people. Sabrino says a dinner without guests is just cooking, and cooking alone is how witches go strange.
strings.quest.dinner.stage100: Completed: dinner was served at the Lantern Inn.
strings.quest.dinner.journal100: For one evening the whole table was full. People who had been alone with their missing memories for seventeen years sat shoulder to shoulder, passed the bread and laughed. Sabrino gave me the Ladle of Justice and told me to come back hungry. I think I will.
strings.npc.witch_sabrino.name: Sabrino
strings.npc.witch_sabrino.title: The Italian Witch (Wanted)
strings.bark.sabrino.1: Who seasons a stew with only salt and sadness? This town. That's who.
strings.bark.sabrino.2: Mamma mia, the damp in this place! My hat has gone soft.
strings.bark.sabrino.3: Come back tomorrow. I'm making the soufflé. Page forty. Do NOT tell Fenwick.
strings.bark.sabrino.4: Eight o'clock! Dinner is always at eight. Even when it's ten.
strings.dlg.sabrino.greeting:
A tall purple hat is bent double under the inn's kitchen beam. Beneath it a witch is stirring three pots at once, one with each hand and one with a spell.

"Ah! A guest! Finally!" Sabrino flings open both arms and a ladle goes with them. "Sabrino. Witch, chef, and, according to the Bureau, a war criminal. Allegedly. Extensively. Mostly for the goose. Sit! Have you eaten? You look like you haven't eaten since the Great Silence."
strings.dlg.sabrino.choice_poster: "There's a wanted poster with your face on it by the town gate."
strings.dlg.sabrino.poster:
"I know! Isn't it wonderful?" Sabrino beams. "They finally drew my good side. The last one gave me a chin like a cabbage."

"1,412 counts of Unlicensed Fireballing. Pfft. Every one of those fireballs had a licence. My licence. I wrote it myself. Beautiful penmanship." A wink. "The cheese wheel, I admit. The cheese wheel was a tragedy. We do not speak of the cheese wheel."
strings.dlg.sabrino.choice_dinner: "I found your note under the pine. It said dinner was at eight."
strings.dlg.sabrino.dinner_plan:
Sabrino stops stirring. That is how you know it's serious.

"You found my hat. Good. It was getting lonely." Sabrino gazes out at the rain. "I have been in this town three days. Do you know what I have seen? People eating alone. At the window. Every night. Setting out one bowl. Or worse, an extra bowl for somebody they can't remember."

"No. Basta. We are making a dinner. A real one. Everybody at one table." Sabrino counts on floury fingers. "I need three things. A Grave-cap Truffle from the old crypts: the Truffle Hogs dig them up, horrible creatures, delicious taste in fungus. Ash-Pepper, from those little lava ovens with legs on the Old Road. And a bottle of Vallo Red, which Vaelen is pretending not to have."

"You bring the ingredients. I bring the magic. Together we fix this town. Sì?"
strings.dlg.sabrino.need:
"A Grave-cap Truffle. The crypts under the Annex, or deeper, where it is quiet. Follow the Truffle Hogs, they are never wrong about fungus, only about everything else.

Ash-Pepper: kill an Ash Crawler and take its little glowing heart. It does not need it any more. And the Vallo Red from Vaelen. Pay whatever he asks. Then tell him it was too much. He will be thrilled."
strings.dlg.sabrino.choice_ingredients: "Truffle, Ash-Pepper and Vallo Red. All here."
strings.dlg.sabrino.cooking:
Sabrino takes the truffle in both hands like a newborn, sniffs the pepper, and uncorks the wine with a fingertip spark.

"Perfetto." Everything goes into the pot at once, which is not how cooking works, and the whole inn fills with a smell so good that two people outside stop walking in the rain.

"Now. The important part." Sabrino points the ladle at you. "Guests. A dinner without guests is just cooking, and cooking alone is how witches go strange. Bring me at least three people. Bring everyone. Bring the lonely ones especially. They always say no first. Ask twice."
strings.dlg.sabrino.guests_status:
"At least three! A dinner for two is a date. A dinner for three is a party. A dinner for ten is a miracle, and we are overdue a miracle."

"Ask Marta, she has been cooking for this town seventeen years and nobody cooks for her. Ask the detective in the long coat, obviously. Ask the Ashbound one with the journal, the librarian, the priest, even that clerk. Especially the clerk. Nobody ever invites the clerk."
strings.dlg.sabrino.choice_serve: "Our guests are on their way, Sabrino. Let's eat."
strings.dlg.sabrino.dinner:
"Then we eat!" Sabrino whips off the hat, hangs it on the beam, and pushes every table in the Lantern Inn into one long line with a single wave of the ladle.

"Sit, sit, sit. Not there, that chair is for the soup."
strings.dlg.sabrino.choice_after: "Thank you, Sabrino. For all of it."
strings.dlg.sabrino.choice_baggy: "Baggy's with me. You two know each other?"
strings.dlg.sabrino.about_baggy:
Sabrino lights up like a stove. "Baggy! My favourite detective! Three weeks this one followed me. Hid behind a barrel every night. Very bad at hiding. The hat was sticking out."

"So every night I said, 'Baggy, come out, the risotto is getting cold,' and every night Baggy said 'I am not here,' and then ate two helpings." Sabrino lowers the voice. "Keep this one close, eh? People who keep showing up are rare. Rarer than truffles."
strings.dlg.sabrino.magic:
"Three rules of magic, from Sabrino." Fingers go up one at a time.

"One: Intellect makes your fire hotter. Every point. Never let anyone tell you to put points into Might. Might is for carrying shopping.

Two: spells get cheaper as you practise them, and a good hat, a really good hat, makes them stronger. Mine is the best hat. You have seen it.

Three: train Elemental and Illusion together and something wonderful happens. The Bureau calls it Sabrino's Doctrine. I call it 'setting things on fire and then politely not being there'."

Sabrino taps your forehead. "And eat before a fight. A spell on an empty stomach is a sad little spell."
strings.dlg.sabrino.choice_shop: "Can I buy something to eat for the road?"
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_join: "Baggy, want to work this case together? I could use a partner."
strings.dlg.baggy.join:
Baggy goes completely still, the way people do when they're trying not to look too pleased.

"A partner. Me?" The magnifying glass is polished very quickly on a sleeve. "Nobody's ever... well. The goat, once, but that was more of a hostage situation."

Then, all at once, a huge grin. "Yes! Absolutely yes. I'll watch your back. I'm very good at backs. Here, take these, I always carry spares." Two squashed sweet rolls are pressed into your hand. "If you get hurt I've got more. Lead the way, partner. I'll be right behind you. Literally. That's how following works."
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_wait: "Could you wait here for a while, Baggy?"
strings.dlg.baggy.wait: "Stakeout. Got it." Baggy nods seriously. "I'll head back to the boundary stone and keep an eye on the hedge. Come and get me when you need me. I mean it. Any time. I'm not busy. I'm never busy."
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_invite: "Baggy, Sabrino is cooking dinner at the Lantern Inn tonight. You're invited."
strings.dlg.baggy.invite:
"Sabrino's here? In Bellwether?" Baggy's hand goes to the coat pocket where a notebook labelled THE SABRINO AFFAIR lives. Then it comes away again, empty.

"I'll come. Strictly in a professional capacity. I'll bring handcuffs." A pause. "I don't own handcuffs. I'll bring a napkin. A professional napkin."
strings.dlg.invite.choice: "Sabrino is cooking a dinner at the Lantern Inn tonight. Will you come?"
strings.dlg.invite.marta: Marta laughs in disbelief. "Somebody's cooking for me? In my own inn?" She looks at her hands, which have been kneading dough for other people for seventeen years. "I'll come. I'll bring the braid. Try and stop me."
strings.dlg.invite.kaelen: Kaelen looks up from the journal. "A dinner. With people." A slow nod. "The Ashbound eat round fires and read names to each other. I've been doing it alone out here for months. A table would be... yes. I'll come. I'll bring the journal. Somebody should read the names."
strings.dlg.invite.fenwick: "Sabrino?" Fenwick's eye twitches. "SABRINO? The cookbook thief? At a DINNER?" A long, trembling pause. "...Will there be soufflé?" Another pause. "I'll come. For the book. Purely for the book. I'll wear my good robe."
strings.dlg.invite.aldous: Brother Aldous's face softens. "The Church of the Last Dawn teaches that a shared meal is the oldest prayer there is." He smiles. "It also teaches that I'm not allowed to cook, after the incident. I'll be there. I'll say grace. A short one. I promise."
strings.dlg.invite.oakhaven: Clerk Oakhaven blinks. "An invitation? For me?" He turns it over as if checking for a stamp. "Nobody has invited me anywhere in nineteen years. There isn't even a form for it." He fills one out anyway. "Form 1-D, Declaration of Attendance at Dinner. Approved. By me. I'll be there, unofficially."
strings.dlg.invite.vaelen: "Dinner? Free dinner?" Vaelen is already taking off the apron. "I've been selling food to this town for nine years and nobody's ever fed me back. I'll bring wine. Well. I'll sell you wine and then bring it. Fine, I'll bring it. Don't tell anyone."
strings.dlg.invite.wendel:
The spirit flickers, astonished. "Me? Wendel? To dinner?" A papery laugh. "I can't eat, you know. I haven't eaten in seventeen years."

"But I can smell. I think. I haven't smelled garlic since the Silence cracked." The glow steadies. "Set a place for me. If there's a chair with my name on it, I'll find my way. Names are how we find things, after all."
strings.story.dinner.1:
The Lantern Inn has never been this full. Every table has been pushed into one long line down the middle of the room, and every chair, stool and upturned barrel in Bellwether has been borrowed to go around it.

Outside, it is dark. Inside, it is warm, and loud, and it smells like garlic and brown butter and bread. Sabrino moves along the table with three pots and a ladle, and nobody's bowl is ever allowed to be empty for long.
strings.story.dinner.marta:
Marta sits at a table she didn't set, eating food she didn't cook, and keeps trying to get up to help. Sabrino keeps sitting her back down.

Her braid is in the middle of the table. At the end, as always, she has set out one more bowl than there are guests. Nobody asks about it. Somebody passes it the bread.
strings.story.dinner.baggy:
Halfway through the second course Baggy stands, clears their throat, and taps a glass.

"Sabrino. By the authority vested in me by a pamphlet, I am placing you under-"

A plate of gnocchi arrives in front of Baggy.

"-under... consideration. Pending dessert." Baggy sits down. The table cheers. The Sabrino Affair is, officially, closed.
strings.story.dinner.kaelen:
Between courses Kaelen opens the charcoal-stained journal and reads aloud: names from Oakhallow's well, from Kaelen's own counting, from the census in the Annex. One by one, slowly.

After each name, without anyone deciding to, the whole table says it back.
strings.story.dinner.fenwick:
Sabrino slides a singed, gravy-spotted book across the table to Fenwick. Cooking With Fire: One Hundred and One Recipes. Eleven years overdue. Page forty is dog-eared.

Fenwick holds it for a long moment, then announces in a shaking voice that all fines are waived, for everyone, forever. Then he asks for the soufflé recipe.
strings.story.dinner.aldous:
Brother Aldous stands to say grace. He promised it would be short.

"For the counted and the uncounted," he says. "For the ones at this table, and the ones we can't remember, who are surely at a table somewhere. Amen."

It is short. Nobody minds that he had to stop in the middle.
strings.story.dinner.oakhaven: Clerk Oakhaven arrives exactly on time, in a pressed coat, carrying Form 1-D in a folder. By the third glass of Vallo Red he has taken off the coat. By the fourth he is teaching Sabrino the Bureau's official drinking song, which has eleven verses and a section for stamping.
strings.story.dinner.vaelen: Vaelen brought the wine and tried, briefly, to put it on a tab. Sabrino paid in risotto. Vaelen considers this the best deal of the decade and says so, several times, to everyone.
strings.story.dinner.wendel:
At the end of the table there's a chair with a name card that says WENDEL in Sabrino's beautiful handwriting.

At some point, nobody can say exactly when, the candle beside it starts burning a little bluer, and the steam from the bowl in front of it curls as though someone is leaning over it, breathing in.
strings.story.dinner.end:
Much later, when the pots are empty and the candles are stubs and Sabrino is asleep in a chair with the hat over their face, you step outside for some air.

You came to Bellwether to argue with a ledger about whether you exist. Standing in the doorway, with the noise of the table still warm at your back, it occurs to you that a ledger was never the proof.

This was. Being remembered. Being missed when you're not at the table. Being saved a seat.

Inside, someone calls your name. You go back in.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.bellwether: Bellwether! Home of rain, forms, and the best bread in the Marches. I'd live here if I could remember where I live.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.old_road: The Old Road. Mind the rats. And the hedge. Mostly the hedge.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.annex: So this is the Annex. Very... filing-cabinet. I can smell old ink and older secrets. Stay close, partner.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.vault_three:
Children. All asleep. Oh.
...We'll be quiet. We'll be very, very quiet.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.seal_chamber: I don't like this room. It feels like it's reading us. Let's do what we came to do and go home.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.1: You know, I've been talking to that hedge for weeks. It's nice to talk to somebody who answers.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.2: Deduction: you're good at this. Evidence: you're still alive. Case closed.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.3: I keep a list of everyone who was kind to me. It's short. You're on it. Second page, though. The first page is mostly bakers.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.4: If you ever want to stop and sit for a bit, we can. Detectives sit all the time. It's called a stakeout.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.5: Do you hear that? ...No, me neither. Just checking we were both listening.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.6: I used to walk this road on my own every day. It's a lot shorter with company.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.7: Fun fact: a group of detectives is called a 'mystery'. I made that up. Still counts.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.8: Partner? Thanks for letting me tag along. I mean it. You didn't have to.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.ilse: Blue shutters. I keep thinking about the blue shutters. Thank you for that.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.seal: The sky's so big without the rain. I keep looking up and walking into things. Worth it.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.rain: My coat has been damp for seventeen years. It's not a coat any more. It's a lifestyle.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.ledger: A whole ledger of hidden names. Somebody should read them all out loud one day. Maybe us.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.dinner: Best dinner of my life. Don't tell Sabrino I said that. Do tell Sabrino. Actually, I'll tell Sabrino.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.sabrino: Sabrino's in town. I can smell the garlic from here. That's not a deduction, that's just my nose.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.friend: Whatever happens down there, you're not doing it alone. That's the whole point of a partner.
strings.comp.baggy.combat.1: Behind you! No, the other behind!
strings.comp.baggy.combat.4: You take the left, I'll take the... also left. We'll both take the left.
strings.comp.baggy.combat.5: Suspect is hostile! Engaging umbrella-adjacent tactics!
strings.comp.baggy.kill.3: Got it! Wait, did I get it? I got it!
strings.comp.baggy.kill.4: Teamwork! Write that down. I'll write that down.
strings.comp.baggy.heal.1: You're bleeding! Here, eat this. It's a sweet roll. It's medicinal. I've decided.
strings.comp.baggy.heal.2: Easy, partner. Sit for a second. Eat. I've got your back.
strings.comp.baggy.heal.3: Emergency sweet roll! This is exactly the emergency I've been saving it for!
strings.comp.baggy.level.1: Look at you! You're getting stronger. I'm getting... more enthusiastic. That counts.
strings.comp.baggy.level.2: Promotion! I'd give you a badge if I had one. I don't. Have a sweet roll instead.
strings.map.hollowmere.name: Hollowmere Grounds
strings.map.hollowmere_manor.name: Hollowmere Manor
strings.item.hollowmere_key.name: Key to Hollowmere Manor
strings.item.hollowmere_key.description: A heavy iron key with a bow shaped like a wine glass. Hollis says it was 'acquired'. Hollis does not elaborate.
strings.item.study_key.name: Study Key
strings.item.study_key.description: Found in a drawer clearly labelled 'STUDY KEY - DO NOT LOOK HERE'. Security at Hollowmere was a matter of trust.
strings.item.dented_bucket.name: Dented Bucket
strings.item.dented_bucket.description: A tin bucket with a dent in it. Worn on the head, it makes you look ridiculous (-1 Presence) and makes shopkeepers strangely unable to keep track of their stock (+10% shop discount). Nobody knows why this works. It just does.
strings.item.party_hat.name: Percival's Party Hat
strings.item.party_hat.description: A pointed paper hat in four colours, made for a party nobody came to. Wearing it makes you feel, briefly, like the guest of honour. +3 Presence, slowly mends you.
strings.item.rat_crown.name: Crown of the Rat King
strings.item.rat_crown.description: A tiny golden crown, sized for a very large rat. It fits you if you push. +2 Agility, +4% critical chance, -1 Presence because people can tell where it's been.
strings.item.cape_brooding.name: Cape of Eternal Brooding
strings.item.cape_brooding.description: Black velvet, blood-red lining, and a high collar to stare moodily out of. Sparkles faintly in sunlight, which ruins the effect. +2 Presence, 3% life steal.
strings.item.hollowmere_signet.name: Hollowmere Signet
strings.item.hollowmere_signet.description: Sir Percival's own ring, given freely at the end of a very good party. It feels warm, like a hand on your shoulder. +2 Presence, +1 Will, slowly mends you.
strings.item.silver_sword.name: Silver Sword of the Grey
strings.item.silver_sword.description: One of Hollis's two swords. The silver one is for monsters; the steel one is for people. Hollis is unclear which one is for rats. Deals heavy extra damage to spirits.
strings.item.moonlit_jerky.name: Rolf's Moonlit Jerky
strings.item.moonlit_jerky.description: Dried and smoked under a full moon by a werewolf who swears there's no wolf in it. Chewy. Restores stamina quickly for 5 minutes.
strings.item.field_guide.name: Hollis's Field Guide to the Restless Dead
strings.item.field_guide.description: A battered notebook full of ghost lore, card-game scores and one very detailed drawing of a horse.
strings.book.field_guide.text:
HOLLIS'S FIELD GUIDE TO THE RESTLESS DEAD
(abridged. unabridged. Hollis edition.)

Find THREE kinds of evidence. Match them below. Do not guess. Guessing is how you end up on the Lawn.

BANSHEE: Wailing, Cold Spots, Ectoplasm Handprints. Screams. You'll know.

POLTERGEIST: Floating Objects, Spirit Box, Ectoplasm Handprints. Throws things AT you.

WRAITH: Ghost Writing, Spirit Box, Wailing. Talks too much. Through trumpets, mostly.

LINGERING HOST: Cold Spots, Ghost Writing, Floating Objects. Rare. Doesn't throw things - it ARRANGES them. Not angry. Lonely. They don't need killing. They need company. (Killing works too. I'm not your mother.)

MIMIC: All of the evidence, all at once, slightly wrong. If the chest has teeth, it's not a ghost, it's a chest.

NOT GHOSTS (cross these off):
- Bite marks: vampire. Annoying, not evidence.
- Claw marks: werewolf. See above.
- Your own footprints: you. Stop it.

Scribbled in the margin: 'Trout - last seen chapel roof. How.'
strings.enemy.animated_armor.name: Animated Armour
strings.enemy.wailing_footman.name: Wailing Footman
strings.enemy.rat_king.name: The Rat King
strings.enemy.wrathful_host.name: Sir Percival, the Wrathful Host
strings.line.armor.alert: HALT. ARE YOU ON THE GUEST LIST.
strings.line.rat_king.alert: SQUEAK. (You are trespassing in the Royal Larder.)
strings.line.rat_king.death: squeak... (avenge me, my eleven hundred children...)
strings.line.host.alert: If you won't stay for dinner... you will stay FOREVER.
strings.line.host.death: ...it was... a lovely party... wasn't it...
strings.quest.rats.title: Rats. It's Always Rats.
strings.quest.rats.summary: Vaelen has a rat problem, and is deeply, sincerely sorry that your next adventure is a rat problem.
strings.quest.rats.stage0: Clear the rats out of Bellwether's streets.
strings.quest.rats.journal0: Vaelen apologised four times before even mentioning the word 'rats'. They're in the streets, in the grain, in the Records Office filing. Every adventurer's first job, and here I am, several adventures in, doing it anyway.
strings.quest.rats.stage20: The rats came from the south. Follow them to Hollowmere Manor's kitchen (the back door is always open) and deal with whatever's sending them.
strings.quest.rats.journal20: The street rats are dead, but they were all heading somewhere: south, through the gap in the village wall, towards Hollowmere Manor. Something is organising them.
strings.quest.rats.stage40: The Rat King is dead. Tell Vaelen.
strings.quest.rats.journal40: In Hollowmere's kitchen I found the Rat King: a rat the size of a dog, wearing a tiny golden crown, sitting on a throne of stolen bread. I have killed a king. It was a rat. I feel complicated about this.
strings.quest.rats.journal100: Vaelen paid me, thanked me, and then apologised again, for the rats, the cliché, and the fact that there will absolutely be more rats one day. There are always more rats.
strings.quest.haunt.title: Case File #1: The Hollowmere Haunting
strings.quest.haunt.summary: Something haunts Hollowmere Manor, south of Bellwether. Six hunters have gone in. Two came back. One was a horse.
strings.quest.haunt.stage0: Something haunts Hollowmere Manor. Hollis the Grey, the monster hunter by Bellwether's east gate, is offering a contract (and a key). Or try the kitchen door.
strings.quest.haunt.journal0: The sign at Hollowmere's gate says 'You must gather your party before venturing forth', and somebody has written underneath it, 'we tried, nobody came.' The manor is supposedly haunted. A monster hunter in Bellwether has the contract.
strings.quest.haunt.stage10: Investigate Hollowmere Manor. Find at least three kinds of evidence (check Hollis's Field Guide), then tell Hollis what haunts it. Beware of red herrings.
strings.quest.haunt.journal10: Hollis gave me a key, a field guide and a long look. 'Three kinds of evidence. Don't guess. And whatever you do, don't hide in the wardrobe.' The guide lists five kinds of ghost and, helpfully, two things that are not ghosts at all.
strings.quest.haunt.stage20: It's a Lingering Host: Sir Percival Hollowmere. Hollis can banish him, or you could find out what he actually wants. He's in the ballroom.
strings.quest.haunt.journal20: Cold spots, ghost writing, a table that lays itself. Not angry. Lonely. Sir Percival Hollowmere threw the finest parties in the Marches, outlived every guest he ever had, and has been laying the table for ninety years for people who never come. Hollis says he can be banished. I'm not sure he needs to be.
strings.quest.haunt.stage30: Hollis has made the banishing salt. Go to the Hollowmere ballroom and put Sir Percival to rest.
strings.quest.haunt.journal30: I told Hollis to do it his way. The salt is laid, the doors are open, and somewhere in the ballroom the gramophone has stopped skipping. It's playing all the way through now. That can't be good.
strings.quest.haunt.stage100: Completed: Sir Percival was banished. Collect your fee from Hollis.
strings.quest.haunt.journal100: The Wrathful Host is gone. Hollowmere is quiet. The table doesn't lay itself any more. I'm not sure if that's better.
strings.quest.haunt.stage101: Completed: Sir Percival had one last party, and is at peace.
strings.quest.haunt.journal101: Hollowmere's ballroom was full for one night, and Sir Percival danced the last waltz all the way through. When the music stopped he smiled, signed the guest book himself, and was gone. He left me his ring. The table hasn't laid itself since. It doesn't need to.
strings.npc.hunter_hollis.name: Hollis the Grey
strings.npc.hunter_hollis.title: Monster Hunter (Contracts Open)
strings.bark.hollis.3: Fancy a hand of cards? No? ...Hmm.
strings.bark.hollis.4: Seen a horse? Answers to Trout. Usually found somewhere it can't possibly be.
strings.bark.hollis.dry: Rain's stopped. Wind's still howling, though. Wind always howls.
strings.dlg.hollis.greeting:
A broad, scarred man with white hair, cat-yellow eyes and two swords on his back looks you up and down, decides you are probably not a monster, and looks slightly disappointed about it.

"Hmm."
strings.dlg.hollis.who:
"Hollis. Monster hunter. They call me the Grey." He gestures vaguely at his hair. "Not very imaginative, villages."

"I kill monsters for coin. Ghosts, wraiths, the odd drowned thing in a well. Mostly I play cards and look for my horse. Monsters come second. Third, if the cards are good."
strings.dlg.hollis.contract:
Hollis studies you for a long moment. "Six went in. Two came back. One was a horse. Not mine. I asked."

He hands over a heavy iron key and a battered notebook. "Key to the front door. Field guide. Three kinds of evidence, then come back and tell me what it is. Don't guess. Guessers end up on the lawn out front with a funny line on their headstone."

"And whatever happens in there," he adds, "don't hide in the wardrobe. It always looks in the wardrobe."
strings.dlg.hollis.need_evidence:
"Walk the house. Look for what doesn't belong. Cold where it should be warm. Writing nobody wrote. Things moving that shouldn't. Write down three, match them in the guide."

He taps the notebook. "And mind the red herrings. That house has a vampire in the attic and a werewolf in the garden. Neither of them is the ghost. Both of them are going to make a mess of your evidence."
strings.dlg.hollis.choice_identify: "I've got my evidence. I know what haunts Hollowmere."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_poltergeist: "A Poltergeist. Things are moving on their own."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_vampire: "It's the vampire. There were bite marks."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_werewolf: "It's the werewolf. There were claw marks."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_host: "A Lingering Host. Cold spots, ghost writing, and the table lays itself."
strings.dlg.hollis.id_trenchcoat: "A vampire and a werewolf, standing on each other's shoulders, in a long coat."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_banshee: "Wrong. A Banshee would've screamed the windows out by now. That wailing's coming from the garden." He sips something. "It's a dog. A very big dog. With opinions. Go and ask it."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_poltergeist: "Wrong. A Poltergeist throws things. At your head. Usually the heaviest thing in the room." He frowns. "Is anything in that house being thrown? Or is it being... tidied?"
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_wraith: "Wrong. A Wraith never shuts up. It'd have talked your ear off through that spirit trumpet. Did it answer you?" He waits. "Hmm. Thought not."
