strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_vampire: "Ashgrave? He bites decanters. Drinks beetroot juice. Writes poetry about being a monster." Hollis shudders slightly. "Harmless. Insufferable. Not a ghost."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_werewolf: "Rolf? The gardener? He knocks with his claws and wipes his feet. Most polite thing on the estate." A pause. "Has no shirts. Not a ghost."
strings.dlg.hollis.wrong_trenchcoat:
Hollis stares at you for a very long time.

"...No."

Another long pause.

"But I'd pay to see it."
strings.dlg.hollis.right_host:
Hollis puts his cup down, slowly. "A Lingering Host." He nods. "Good. That's right. That's the rare one."

"Sir Percival Hollowmere. Threw parties for sixty years. Outlived every guest. Died at the head of a table laid for twelve, waiting." He looks out at the rain. "A Host isn't angry. It's lonely. It lays the table and waits for company that doesn't come, and it'll do that until the house falls down."

"I can banish him. Salt, silver, an hour's work. That's the contract." He shrugs. "Or you go and talk to him. He's showing himself in the ballroom now you know what he is. Your call. I get paid either way."
strings.dlg.hollis.choice_banish: "Do it your way, Hollis. Banish him."
strings.dlg.hollis.banish: "You're sure? Once it's done, it's done. No more parties. No more anything."
strings.dlg.hollis.banish_go:
Hollis hands you a pouch of salt mixed with silver filings. "Spread it at the ballroom doors. He'll come to you. He won't be polite about it."

"Hmm." He looks away. "Make it quick."
strings.dlg.hollis.paid:
Hollis counts out two hundred crowns, then, after a moment, unbuckles the silver sword from his back and holds it out.

"Take it. You've earned it. And I've got another." He looks at the coins. "Funny. Ninety years of waiting for guests, and the last one to visit was us."

"Hmm."
strings.dlg.hollis.choice_peace: "Sir Percival's at peace. He had his party."
strings.dlg.hollis.peace:
Hollis hears the whole story without interrupting, which is apparently a first.

"A party. You threw a ghost a party." He counts out the coins. "Hundred and twenty. Less than the banishing fee. I'm docking you for making me feel things."

Then, gruffly, quietly: "Good work. Better than mine would've been."
strings.dlg.hollis.cards:
Hollis's eyes light up for the first time. He produces a deck from nowhere, along with a small folding table, two stools and a candle. "Vaults and Vagrants. Highest hand wins. Losing hand buys the next round. Twenty-five crowns a game."

He shuffles with terrifying speed. "I should warn you. I've been playing this game instead of doing my job for nine years."
strings.dlg.hollis.cards_win:
You lay down your hand. Hollis looks at it. Then at you. Then at his own hand, which is extremely bad.

"Hmm," he says, in an entirely new tone, and pays up. "Again tomorrow. I'll be here. I'm always here. I've a contract I'm meant to be doing, but... cards."
strings.dlg.hollis.cards_lose:
Hollis lays down a hand so good that it might not be from the same deck.

"Hmm," he says, with deep satisfaction. "Don't feel bad. Took me nine years to get this good. Ignored three kings, two plagues and a dragon to do it."
strings.dlg.hollis.horse:
"Trout." Hollis sighs. "Chapel roof, last I heard. Before that, a well. Inside the well. Standing, not swimming. Before that, the top of a church spire in another kingdom."

"I whistle, she appears next to me. Sometimes in the wall. Sometimes upside down." He shrugs. "Good horse, though. Never complains."
strings.dlg.hollis.knee:
"No. Used to be a dungeon delver. Proper adventurer. Tombs, dragons, the lot."

He shifts his weight. "Then I took a crossbow bolt to the... well. It doesn't matter where. Changed careers. Every guard in three kingdoms tells the same story now. Copying me, I reckon."
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_pitch:
Vaelen winces like a man about to deliver bad news at a funeral.

"I'm so sorry. I want you to know that I know. I KNOW." He takes a deep breath. "It's rats."

"I know you've fought skeletons and shades and very probably worse. I know you have a sword with a name. And I'm standing here asking you to go and hit rats, like you're some farm boy on his first day." He wrings his hands. "I'd have given you a dragon if I had one. I don't. I have rats. Everywhere. In the grain, in the streets, in the Records Office filing. Oakhaven is furious. They've eaten Form 27-B."

"Please. I'll pay. And I'll never speak of it again."
strings.dlg.vaelen.choice_advance: [Persuasion - a sure thing] "I'll need half up front."
strings.dlg.vaelen.advance_ok: Vaelen counts out twenty crowns, then a few more, then takes a few back. "Half up front. Fair. Don't spend it on rat poison, it doesn't work. They've unionised."
strings.dlg.vaelen.advance_fail:
You open your mouth to negotiate. What comes out is: "Actually, I'll pay YOU twenty crowns for the privilege."

Vaelen blinks. You blink. Neither of you knows how it happened. It was a ninety-five percent chance. Somewhere, very far away, a game master is laughing so hard they've fallen off their chair.

"I'm... not going to take your money," Vaelen says kindly. "Do you want to try that again?"
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_pitch_again: "From the top, then," says Vaelen, politely pretending it never happened.
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_status: "Still rats?" Vaelen sighs. "The ones in town keep heading south. Through the gap in the wall, towards that old manor. If something down there is sending them, it's a big something. A royal something. Mind your ankles."
strings.dlg.vaelen.choice_rats_done: "The Rat King is dead. It was wearing a crown."
strings.dlg.vaelen.rats_done:
"A crown?" Vaelen stares at you. "An actual crown? On a rat?"

He pays you, generously, then adds two potions. "For the trauma." Then, quietly: "Thank you. Really. And I'm sorry. And there will be more rats one day. There are always more rats. But that day is not today."
strings.dlg.vaelen.choice_bucket: [Wearing a bucket on your head] "Good afternoon."
strings.dlg.vaelen.bucket:
Vaelen squints at you. "Why is there a bucket on your head?"

A long pause.

"You know what? I can't see your eyes. I can't see where you're looking. If anything were to walk off my shelves right now, I'd never know who took it." He turns his back, very deliberately, and starts counting candles. "Lovely bucket. Shame if someone left with a couple of tonics."

Two stamina tonics are somehow in your pocket.
strings.npc.vampire_ashgrave.name: Lord Ashgrave
strings.npc.vampire_ashgrave.title: Vampire (Lodger, Upstairs)
strings.bark.ashgrave.1: Do not look at me. I am a monster. ...You can look a little bit.
strings.bark.ashgrave.2: I have been seventeen for three hundred years. It is exhausting.
strings.bark.ashgrave.3: The rain suits me. It matches my soul. And it hides the sparkling.
strings.dlg.ashgrave.greeting:
A pale young man in a long black coat is standing by the window, staring out at the rain with tremendous intensity. A shaft of grey light falls across his cheek, and his skin glitters faintly, like it has been dusted with sugar.

"Do not come any closer," he says, without turning round. "I am dangerous. I am a monster. You should run."

He waits. You don't run. He looks quietly pleased.
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_ghost: "Are you the ghost that haunts this house?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.ghost:
"A ghost? Please." He sweeps his cape. "I am something far darker. I am a creature of the night. A predator. A beast in a man's form."

"I am also a lodger. I rent the master bedroom. Sir Percival charges very reasonable rates and has never once asked about the coffin." He lowers his voice. "The ghost is downstairs. He is very lonely. It is extremely awkward at breakfast."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.decanters:
Ashgrave goes very still. "That was me."

"I do not drink the blood of the living. I am not that kind of monster. I am trying to be better." He gestures at the decanters with a trembling hand. "Beetroot juice. It's the right colour. If I bite through the stopper it feels... authentic."

"Not evidence. Merely shame. Please cross it off."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_why: "Why are you living in a haunted manor?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.why:
"Ninety years ago, Sir Percival invited me to a party." Ashgrave sighs. "I arrived fashionably late. Eighty-nine years late. Everyone else had died of old age."

"So I stayed. To be polite." He stares out of the window. "Also, there is a werewolf in the garden. He thinks I don't know he looks up at this window every night. I do know. I look back. It is very complicated."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.sparkle:
"I do not sparkle." A shaft of light hits him and he glitters like a festival. "I SHIMMER. Ominously."

"In the old stories, vampires burst into flame in daylight. Proper, dignified, tragic flames. I got this." He looks down at his glittering hands. "Three hundred years. Do you know how hard it is to be taken seriously as a creature of the night when you look like a wedding cake?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_team: "Rolf in the garden says you're 'not like other vampires'. You both keep asking who I like better."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team:
Ashgrave turns from the window at last, very dramatically, and nearly trips on his cape.

"You are not like other adventurers," he says, intensely. "I have watched you. You have a... scent. Of road dust and cheap bread and ambition."

"The wolf will tell you he can protect you. The wolf will take his shirt off. The wolf ALWAYS takes his shirt off." He steps closer. "Choose."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.choice_team_sabrino: "Honestly? Team Sabrino. Have you tried the gnocchi?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team_ash:
Ashgrave's face does something complicated that might be joy, if joy had been locked in a crypt for three centuries.

"I knew it." He unfastens his cape and drapes it round your shoulders. "Take this. When you wear it, think of me. Brood occasionally. Stare out of windows. And never, ever stand in direct sunlight wearing it. Trust me on that."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team_rolf:
"The wolf." Ashgrave turns back to the window. "Of course. The wolf. Everyone always chooses the wolf. He has the warmth. He has the abs. He has a SHIRT budget, apparently."

He sighs, enormously. "Go, then. I shall brood. It is what I do best." A pause. "Tell him I said... nothing. Tell him nothing."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.team_sabrino:
Ashgrave blinks. "Who is Sabrino?"

You explain. The hat. The fireballs. The gnocchi. Ashgrave listens with growing horror.

"A third option," he whispers. "There was a THIRD OPTION?" He sits down on his coffin. "Three hundred years of brooding, and nobody told me there was a third option."
strings.npc.werewolf_rolf.name: Rolf
strings.npc.werewolf_rolf.title: Werewolf (Head Gardener)
strings.bark.rolf.1: I'm not wearing a shirt because I'm a werewolf. It's practical. ...It's mostly practical.
strings.bark.rolf.2: Moon's out. Nobody's calling. Time for a quick howl.
strings.bark.rolf.3: If you see Ashgrave, don't tell him I asked about him.
strings.dlg.rolf.greeting:
A huge, shaggy man with golden eyes, a heroic jaw and absolutely no shirt is weeding a flowerbed in the pouring rain, very carefully, so as not to hurt the worms.

"Oh! A visitor!" He stands, wipes his hands on his trousers, and tries to look broody and mysterious. He lasts about two seconds before beaming. "Sorry. Hello. I'm Rolf. I'm a werewolf. Don't be scared. I'm mostly gardener."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_howl: "I heard wailing out here. Was that you?"
strings.dlg.rolf.howl:
Rolf goes bright red under the fur. "That was me. Sorry. I howl when I'm sad."

"Full moon comes round, nobody calls, the vampire upstairs doesn't come down, and I just... howl about it. It's a werewolf thing. It's a feelings thing. Mostly a feelings thing." He scuffs a foot. "Did it sound like a ghost? People always think it's a Banshee. I'm not a Banshee. I'm a Rolf."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_claws: "There are claw marks on the kitchen door."
strings.dlg.rolf.claws:
"I knock," says Rolf, sadly. "I knock with my claws, because they're always out after the change, and nobody ever answers, and I knock a bit harder, and..." He holds up enormous hands. "I always wipe my feet, though. Always. Manners cost nothing."

"Not ghost evidence. Just me, being a bit much."
strings.dlg.rolf.shirt:
"Transformation." Rolf gestures at himself. "Every full moon, I change, and the shirt doesn't. I've lost forty-one shirts. Forty-one. Vaelen won't sell me any more. He says it's 'not a sustainable relationship'."

He looks up at an upstairs window. "Ashgrave says it's for attention. It is NOT for attention." He flexes slightly. "Mostly not for attention."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_ghost: "What do you know about the ghost?"
strings.dlg.rolf.ghost:
"Sir Percival? He's lovely." Rolf's face goes soft. "He hired me ninety years ago. Before I was a wolf, even. Every evening he'd lay the table and ask if I'd like to come in for dinner, and I'd say yes, and then I'd get nervous and stay in the garden."

"He's still laying it. Every night. Twelve places." Rolf wipes his eyes with a very large paw. "I should go in, one of these days. I should really go in."
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_team_rolf: "Ashgrave asked me to choose between you. I chose you."
strings.dlg.rolf.team_rolf:
Rolf freezes. Then he hugs you, which is a lot like being hugged by a warm, damp bear.

"Nobody ever chooses me! Everyone always picks the pale brooding one!" He lets go and presses a bundle of wrapped jerky into your hands. "Moonlit jerky. My own recipe. There's no wolf in it. I promise. Probably."

Then, more quietly, looking up at the window: "Did he... say anything? About me?"
strings.dlg.rolf.choice_team_other: "Ashgrave asked me to choose between you..."
strings.dlg.rolf.team_other:
Rolf's ears droop. "You chose him. Or the witch. I heard about the witch. Everyone's heard about the witch."

Then he shrugs, enormous shoulders rising and falling, and smiles anyway. "That's all right. Here. Have some jerky anyway. A choice is a choice, but a snack is a snack."
strings.npc.ghost_percival.name: Sir Percival Hollowmere
strings.npc.ghost_percival.title: The Host (Deceased, Still Hosting)
strings.bark.percival.1: Welcome, welcome! Do come in! Is it just you? ...Oh. Just you.
strings.bark.percival.2: Twelve places. I always lay twelve. You never know who might drop in.
strings.bark.percival.peace: What a party. What a party!
strings.dlg.percival.greeting:
The ballroom grows cold, and then, quite suddenly, it is full of candlelight that isn't there. An old man in a velvet coat drifts across the dance floor towards you, beaming, both translucent arms held wide.

"A guest! A guest, at last! Welcome to Hollowmere! Can I take your coat? Can I take your hat? I can't, actually, my hands go straight through things, but it's the thought." He looks past you, hopeful. "Is it just you? Are the others parking the carriage?"
strings.dlg.percival.who:
"The very same! Host of the Year, eleven years running!" He bows so deeply his head goes through the floor for a moment. "Hollowmere was famous for its parties. Three hundred guests. Fireworks. A string quartet. A swan made entirely of jelly."

His smile wobbles. "Then the guests got older. And fewer. And then one year it was just me and the jelly swan. And then it was just me."
strings.dlg.percival.choice_why: "Why are you still here, Sir Percival?"
strings.dlg.percival.why:
He looks around the empty ballroom for a long time.

"I laid the table for my last party. Twelve places. I sent out the invitations. I wound the gramophone. And then I sat at the head of the table and waited." He smiles, very gently. "I'm still waiting. That's all. A host can't leave until the party's over, you see. And it can't be over if it never started."

"If someone came... if enough people came... I think I could finally have the last dance."
strings.dlg.percival.choice_guests: "Sir Percival, your guests are here. All of them. I brought the whole town."
strings.dlg.percival.choice_me: [Persuasion] "I'm here. I'm a guest. That has to count for something."
strings.dlg.percival.me_fail:
Sir Percival smiles at you, so kindly it hurts.

"It counts for a great deal, my dear. More than you know." He looks at the eleven empty chairs. "But a party for one is just... dinner. And I've had ninety years of dinner."

"Perhaps you know some people who could do with a good meal? Lonely ones. They're always the best guests."
strings.dlg.percival.party: The ballroom doors open, and the town walks in.
strings.dlg.percival.party_me:
Sir Percival looks at you for a long, long moment. Then he laughs, a real laugh, warm and surprised.

"You know, you're right. A party is just people who chose to be in the same room. And you chose." He offers you a translucent arm. "Would you do me the honour?"
strings.dlg.percival.thanks:
"Wonderful. Wonderful!" He's fainter now, the colour of morning mist, but beaming. "I don't have long, I think. I wanted to say goodbye properly. A good host always sees his guests to the door."

"Do throw parties. Lots of them. Invite the lonely ones first. They always say no the first time. Ask twice."
strings.story.party.1:
They come up the drive in the rain, under umbrellas and cloaks and one very large hat: everyone you've met, everyone you asked, and a few people who simply heard there was a party at Hollowmere and couldn't believe it.

The ballroom candles light themselves. The gramophone plays the waltz, and for the first time in ninety years, it doesn't skip.
strings.story.party.dinner: Sabrino arrives last, at exactly eight, carrying three pots and a ladle, takes one look at the twelve empty places on the table and declares them a crime against hospitality. Within the hour, every one of them is full, and so is everyone sitting in them.
strings.story.party.baggy: Baggy dances. Badly. Enthusiastically. At one point Baggy dances with a suit of armour that turns out to be ornamental, and then, later, with one that turns out not to be. Nobody is hurt. Everybody cheers.
strings.story.party.pair:
Lord Ashgrave comes down from the master bedroom for the first time in ninety years, and stands awkwardly by the punch bowl, glittering faintly. Rolf comes in from the garden, and for once remembers to put on a shirt.

They stand on opposite sides of the room for most of the evening. Then, during the slow song, somebody, possibly a ghost, gives them both a little push.
strings.story.party.hollis: Hollis sits in the corner with a deck of cards and loses every single hand to Sir Percival, who can see through the backs of them. He doesn't seem to mind. At one point you are fairly sure he smiles.
strings.story.party.small:
It's only the two of you in the great ballroom: you, and a ghost in a velvet coat. The gramophone plays the waltz. You are not a very good dancer. Sir Percival is a terrible one. Neither of you cares.

Somewhere upstairs, a door opens, and you hear the shuffle of a vampire and the pad of a werewolf creeping to the banister to watch. By the second verse, they're humming along.
strings.story.party.end:
At the end of the last waltz, Sir Percival Hollowmere bows to the room, signs his own name in the guest book in a looping, happy hand, and thanks everyone for coming.

Then he takes off his ring, presses it into your palm with fingers that are almost warm, and walks out through the ballroom doors into the morning. He doesn't look back. He doesn't need to.

The table at Hollowmere never lays itself again. It doesn't have to. Somebody is always coming to dinner now.
strings.dlg.baggy.choice_haunt: "Baggy, any thoughts on the Hollowmere haunting?"
strings.dlg.baggy.haunt:
Baggy's eyes light up. "Case number two! A haunted manor! This is the best day of my life. Again."

The notebook comes out. "Detective's rule for ghosts: evidence lies. People lie more. Werewolves and vampires lie the most, mostly about their feelings. So if you find something that LOOKS like evidence, ask whoever might have left it."

"Claw marks? Ask the one with claws. Bite marks? Ask the one with fangs. What's left over is your ghost." Baggy taps the side of a nose. "Elementary. I read that in a pamphlet too."
strings.comp.baggy.zone.hollowmere: A haunted manor in the rain. With a graveyard. On a dark night. I've never felt more like a detective in my life.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.hollowmere_manor: Okay. Okay okay okay. Rules: we don't split up, we don't read anything out loud in Latin, and we don't hide in the wardrobe.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.1: Sorry! Sorry. Got stuck on a door. Doors are the natural enemy of the follower.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.2: I was right behind you, then I was stuck on a barrel for a while. It's fine. We've made our peace.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.3: Did you know you can't walk through a table? I've checked. Several times. Just now.
strings.comp.baggy.catchup.4: Found you! I took the scenic route. Through a wall, I think. Don't ask.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.initiative: Roll for initiative! ...Sorry. I've always wanted to say that.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.map: Do you ever feel like someone's watching us? From above? Moving us around a big map, rolling dice to see what happens next?
strings.comp.baggy.idle.manor: That vampire and that werewolf. You can tell, can't you? They should just talk to each other.
strings.comp.baggy.idle.hollis: That monster hunter, Hollis. I asked him for tips and he just said 'Hmm.' I wrote it down. I think it's profound.
strings.bark.clerk.rules: Technically, page 212 of the municipal code says you can file while falling. Don't test it.
strings.bark.marta.quest: An adventurer told me he'd be right back after 'just one more quest'. That was a fortnight ago. His soup's gone cold.
strings.bark.fenwick.respawn: Someone keeps putting the same book back on the same shelf, every morning, in exactly the same spot. I didn't do it. Nobody did it.
strings.bark.scout.chests: Every chest on this road refills itself every few days. Nobody knows who does it. The Ashbound have theories.
strings.bark.aldous.stack: A traveller asked me to bless his sword forty times in a row. I explained the blessings don't stack. He tried anyway.
strings.bark.vaelen.hoard: You're carrying forty swords. FORTY. Where do you even keep them?
strings.tip.1: You can avoid dying by not taking damage.
strings.tip.2: Enemies are considerably less dangerous after they die.
strings.tip.3: The Bureau does not accept death as an excuse for late payment.
strings.tip.4: Hoarding forty swords 'just in case' is a valid lifestyle. Your carry weight disagrees.
strings.tip.5: If a door is locked, the key is usually in the drawer labelled 'KEY - DO NOT LOOK HERE'. Architects are like that.
strings.tip.6: Quick save often. Quick save before talking to anyone. Quick save before quick saving.
strings.tip.7: A natural 20 is not a personality.
strings.tip.8: Splitting the party is a time-honoured tradition. So are funerals.
strings.tip.9: Your companion is not stuck on a door. Your companion is thinking.
strings.tip.10: Mimics can be identified by their teeth, their tongue, and the fact that you are already inside one.
strings.tip.11: Bards can seduce many things. Gravity is not one of them.
strings.tip.12: Quest givers will wait for you forever. They do not eat. They do not sleep. They are always exactly where you left them. Don't think about it too much.
strings.tip.13: Sparkling in sunlight is not a recognised defensive ability.
strings.tip.14: That mannequin in the hall is fine. Don't look at the mannequin.
strings.tip.15: Wolves in this region carry, on average, 0.3 pelts each. Plan your fetch quests accordingly.
strings.tip.16: The real treasure was the friends you made along the way. The other real treasure was in the sealed room.
strings.tip.17: Hiding in the wardrobe has never once worked. It always looks in the wardrobe.
strings.tip.18: If your horse is on the roof, it is not your fault. It is never your fault. It is always the horse.
strings.tip.19: Wearing a bucket on your head may affect how shopkeepers perceive you. And their stock.
strings.tip.20: Ninety-five percent is not one hundred percent. The dice know this. The dice have always known this.
strings.tip.21: When in doubt, eat something. Sabrino insists.
strings.tip.22: Rats. It's always rats. You may as well get good at rats.
strings.campaign.chapter_zero.name: Chapter Zero: Legally Deceased
strings.campaign.chapter_zero.desc: The main story. The Bureau says you died seventeen years ago. The Bureau is wrong, mostly.
strings.campaign.tales.name: Tales of Bellwether
strings.campaign.tales.desc: Small stories from a rainy village: rats, dinners, and the people who live there.
strings.campaign.hollowmere.name: The Hollowmere Mysteries
strings.campaign.hollowmere.desc: Hollis the Grey's case files: a haunted manor, a silent harbour, and whatever comes next, just as soon as he finishes this hand of cards.
strings.dlg.odette.root:
A small woman in a very large magenta hat sweeps towards you with both arms out, a silver-topped cane in one hand and a feather boa trailing behind her like a comet's tail.

"DARLING. Look at you. Look at that FACE. That is a face that has suffered. That is a face that has been declared legally deceased. You," she jabs the cane at your nose, "are exactly what the theatre has been missing."
strings.dlg.odette.root.c2: "Who do we still need for the cast?"
strings.dlg.odette.root.c5: "I got the script back from Mortimer Quill."
strings.dlg.odette.root.c8: "We have a crown, a dragon and something that goes bang."
strings.dlg.odette.who:
"Madame Odette Velour! Impresario! Director! Visionary! Founder, owner and, as of last Tuesday, sole remaining member of the Velour Travelling Players!"

She lowers her voice. "The rest of the troupe left over artistic differences. Mostly about being paid. Philistines."

"I have a cart, a costume trunk, and the greatest play ever written. The Tragedie of the Uncounted King. Five acts. Two intervals. One dragon. All I need now is a cast. And a lead." The cane swings round to point at you again. "Hmm? HMM?"
strings.dlg.odette.aud_1:
Odette thrusts a crumpled sheet of paper into your hands and retreats three paces, framing you with her fingers.

"The Great Speech of the Uncounted King. Act Five. Read it to me, darling. From the top. Make me FEEL something."

The paper reads:

    Though the ledger strike my name, though the ink run dry,
    Though every clerk in every hall forget that I was I,
    I stand here still, I breathe here still, and this I swear:
    A name held true by one who loves is never truly bare.

"How will you play it?"
strings.dlg.odette.aud_1.c0: [Dramatic] Fling one arm at the heavens and bellow every word.
strings.dlg.odette.aud_1.c1: [Haunted] Whisper it, as if the words might break.
strings.dlg.odette.aud_1.c2: [As Sabrino] Do it as a flamboyant Italian witch. With hand gestures.
strings.dlg.odette.aud_1.c3: [As Baggy] Do it as a nervous detective who has just found a clue.
strings.dlg.odette.aud_1.c4: [As Hollis] Read the whole thing, then say "Hmm."
strings.dlg.odette.aud_2:
Odette has gone very still. Her hand is pressed to her heart. A single tear is making its way through a remarkable quantity of face powder.

"That," she says at last, "was a CHOICE. I have seen kings weep and dwarves faint and once a goose stand up and applaud, and I have never seen anything like that."

She snaps back to business. "Now. The last line. Act Five, the King stands before the Bureau itself, and cries: 'I AM COUNTED!' It is the line that brings the house down. Give me EVERYTHING you have."
strings.dlg.odette.aud_2.c0: [Presence] Take a breath. Give it everything. "I AM COUNTED!"
strings.dlg.odette.aud_2.c1: [Play it safe] Say it clearly, with quiet dignity.
strings.dlg.odette.aud_win:
Your voice rings off the rooftops of Bellwether. Somewhere a dog barks back. Three windows open. Marta, in the inn doorway, drops a loaf.

Odette is applauding with her whole body. "BRAVO! BRAVISSIMO! The rafters, darling, you hit the RAFTERS, and we're outdoors!"
strings.dlg.odette.aud_flub:
You take a mighty breath, open your mouth, and what comes out is: "I AM CUCUMBER!"

There is a long silence. Somewhere, a crow laughs.

Odette doesn't blink. "Interesting. INTERESTING. A bold reinterpretation. The King, in his hour of despair, identifies with a humble vegetable. It's avant-garde. It's subversive. We'll workshop it."
strings.dlg.odette.aud_safe:
"I am counted," you say, quietly and clearly, and for a moment the rain seems to hush to listen.

Odette lowers her cane. "Oh," she says softly. "Oh, that's lovely. Understated. Nobody ever does it understated." Then, briskly: "Louder on the night, though. The back row is always full of farmers."
strings.dlg.odette.aud_3:
"Did you get the part? DARLING. You were always going to get the part. The only other person who auditioned was a goat, and it ate the script."

She produces a long list. "Now! A play needs a cast. Prince Valiant, the Ghost of the Old King, the Dragon, a Herald, a Narrator, a Second Guard, a prompter and somebody who knows about fire. I have none of these. You know everyone in this soggy little town. Go and find me at least four. Charm them! Bribe them! Lie to them about the money!"
strings.dlg.odette.cast_status:
Odette consults her list with a monocle she was not wearing a moment ago.

"PRINCE VALIANT: dashing, heroic, ideally owns a sword. THE GHOST OF THE OLD KING: pale, tragic, good at standing very still. THE DRAGON: large, menacing, one line. THE HERALD: loud, official, fond of paperwork. THE NARRATOR: a commanding voice, a love of words. THE SECOND GUARD: anyone, honestly. A PROMPTER: somebody who remembers everything and whispers well. And PYROTECHNICS: somebody who is not afraid of fire, or the law."

She lowers the monocle. "Four at the very least. Eight if you love me."
strings.dlg.odette.cast_done:
Odette counts your recruits on her fingers, then counts them again, then hugs you so hard your spine makes a noise.

"A CAST! A real cast! Do you know how long it has been since I had a cast that wasn't me in four different hats?"

She flings open her costume trunk with a flourish. "And now, the script! The only copy of The Tragedie of the Uncounted King, written in my own fair hand, bound in velvet, kept safe in..."

The trunk is empty except for a single card. On it, in spidery red ink: "One and a half stars. Derivative. - M.Q."

Odette screams. It is, you have to admit, an excellent scream. Very well projected.
strings.dlg.odette.stolen:
"MORTIMER QUILL." She spits the name like a bad oyster. "The most feared critic in the history of the stage. He panned my first play, my second play, and my wedding. He gave the moon two stars. He said the sea was 'overlong'."

"He has been dead for two hundred years, darling. It hasn't slowed him down."

She grips your sleeve. "He'll have torn it up. He always tears them up. He scatters the pages wherever he goes, like a toddler with opinions. Find them. Find the pages, find Mortimer, and get my play BACK."
strings.dlg.odette.script_status:
"Five pages, darling, five! He'll have strewn them across the whole province. Look anywhere dusty, gloomy, or important. Critics adore all three."

"And when you've found the trail's end, you'll find HIM. Some draughty old house, no doubt, full of books to sneer at."
strings.dlg.odette.script_back:
You hand Odette the velvet-bound script. She holds it to her chest, rocks it like a baby, and kisses the cover three times.

"My PLAY. My beautiful, bruised, heavily annotated play." She flips it open and her eyebrows climb. "He's written in the margins. In red. 'Act Three: needs a dragon.' Well. It HAS a dragon. 'Then it needs a better one.' Hmph."

"Now. We need a rehearsal space. Something grand. Atmospheric. Haunted, ideally. I hear there's a manor south of town with a ballroom and its own ghost." She is already walking. "Meet me at Hollowmere, darling! Bring the cast! Bring SNACKS!"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub:
Odette has turned the Hollowmere ballroom into a theatre: a low stage at the far end, chalk marks on the floor, a folding chair labelled DIRECTOR in letters a foot high.

"PLACES, everyone! Act One, Scene One!" Nobody moves to their places. Somebody is on fire, briefly. "Darling, you're the lead. Leads solve problems. Who shall we deal with first?"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c0: Deal with Rolf, who has a question about the costume.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c1: Deal with Lord Ashgrave, who has notes on his death scene.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c2: Deal with Hollis, who will not roar.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c3: Deal with Baggy, who is investigating the scenery.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c4: Deal with Sabrino and the small fire.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c5: Deal with Marta, whose prompting is very loud.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c6: Deal with Fenwick, who keeps shushing the actors.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hub.c7: Deal with Clerk Oakhaven, who has stopped the rehearsal.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_rolf:
ROLF (holding up a frilly white shirt with enormous puffed sleeves): "Madame Odette says Prince Valiant wears THIS."

He turns it round. It has a ruff. "I'm a werewolf. If I get excited during the sword fight, I change. If I change, this shirt explodes. That'll be shirt number forty-two." He looks at you with enormous golden eyes. "What do I do?"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_rolf.c0: [Practical] "Wear it. If it explodes, it explodes. That's live theatre."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_rolf.c1: [Kind] "Go shirtless. It's a bold artistic choice. Odette will love it."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_rolf.c2: [Sneaky] "Put the shirt on Ashgrave instead and see what happens."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_rolf_2:
Rolf puts the shirt on with tremendous solemnity. The ruff frames his jaw. He looks, unfortunately, magnificent.

ODETTE (from the director's chair): "YES. That's my prince. Do NOT get excited."

ROLF: "I'm already a bit excited."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_rolf_3:
ODETTE (rising slowly from the director's chair): "A shirtless prince. Raw. Primal. Unprecedented." She sits back down. "I hate that I love it."

Rolf flexes, very slightly, in the direction of the upstairs gallery. Somebody up there drops a candlestick.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_rolf_4:
Five minutes later Lord Ashgrave is wearing a frilly white shirt with a ruff. He has caught sight of himself in a mirror and appears to be having a crisis.

ASHGRAVE: "I look like a wedding cake. A HAPPY wedding cake."

ROLF (very quietly): "...You look nice."

Nobody speaks for a while.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_ashgrave:
LORD ASHGRAVE (lying flat on the stage, arms folded across his chest): "I have notes on my death scene."

He raises one finger without opening his eyes. "The script says, 'The Ghost of the Old King fades away.' Fades. Away. Three hundred years of brooding, and I am asked to simply FADE." He sits bolt upright. "A death scene should last at least forty minutes. There should be a monologue. There should be WEATHER."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_ashgrave.c1: [Flattering] "Less is more. You could do it with one look. Only you could."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_ashgrave.c2: [Blunt] "Two minutes, Ashgrave. People have dinners to get home to."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_ash_2:
ASHGRAVE: "Ten minutes." He considers. "With thunder?"

YOU: "With thunder."

ASHGRAVE: "And a single tear?"

YOU: "Two tears, if you can manage it."

ASHGRAVE (lying back down, satisfied): "I can manage nine."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_ash_3:
Ashgrave opens his eyes. He looks at you for a very long time, with the full weight of three centuries of tragedy.

Then he looks at the empty seats, just once, the way you'd look at the sea.

Odette, in the director's chair, has quietly started crying. "Fine," she sniffs. "FINE. One look. Keep the look."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_ash_4:
ASHGRAVE: "Two minutes." He sits up very slowly. "Two. Minutes."

"In my day, people died properly. Over several days. In verse." He lies back down. "I shall do it in two minutes. And it will be the longest two minutes of their lives."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hollis:
HOLLIS (in a dragon costume made of a green blanket and two oven gloves, arms folded): "No."

ODETTE: "It says ROAR, darling. In capitals. With three exclamation marks."

HOLLIS: "I don't roar. I've killed eleven real dragons. None of them roared. They hissed, mostly. One of them coughed."

He looks at you. "Hmm."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hollis.c0: [Encouraging] "Just do your normal 'Hmm', but louder. Make it menacing."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hollis.c1: [Bargain] "Roar once, properly, and I'll play you at cards afterwards."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hollis.c2: [Respect] "Play it your way. Show them what a real dragon sounds like."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hol_2:
Hollis takes a deep breath, fills his chest, and delivers the loudest, most menacing "HMMMMMMM" ever heard in the Marches. The chandelier rattles. A Wailing Footman in the next room drops a tray.

ODETTE (very quietly): "...That'll do."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hol_3:
HOLLIS (instantly): "Deal."

He throws back his head and ROARS. It is genuinely terrifying. Two candles go out. Ashgrave hides behind a curtain. Rolf's ears go flat.

Hollis lowers his head. "Hmm. Deal the cards."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_hol_4:
Hollis drops into a low crouch in his blanket. He doesn't roar. He just goes absolutely, completely still, and breathes, slowly, through his nose.

It is the most frightening thing you've ever seen on a stage. Odette has climbed onto her chair.

HOLLIS (standing up, brushing off the oven gloves): "That's what they do right before."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_baggy:
BAGGY (crawling around the back of the stage with a magnifying glass): "Don't mind me! Investigating! This painted castle backdrop has a door in it, but the door doesn't open. Why would a castle have a door that doesn't open? Who are they keeping OUT?"

ODETTE: "It's SCENERY, darling."

BAGGY: "That's exactly what a suspicious door would want us to think."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_baggy.c0: [Join in] Get down and investigate with Baggy.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_baggy.c1: [Redirect] "Baggy, the Second Guard investigates. That's your character's whole thing."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_baggy.c2: [Remind] "Baggy. Your line. Do you remember your line?"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_bag_2:
The two of you crawl round the backdrop for a while, Odette screaming the whole time. Eventually you find that the painted door has a small real hinge, and behind it, a small real cupboard, and in the cupboard, a small real bottle of wine with a note: 'For opening night. Don't tell Odette. - the previous cast.'

BAGGY (holding it up, beaming): "Case CLOSED."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_bag_3:
Baggy's eyes widen. "The Second Guard... is a detective." The magnifying glass trembles. "Method acting. I've been method acting this ENTIRE time."

Baggy stands, squares both shoulders, and adds, with enormous dignity: "Who goes there. And WHY."

ODETTE: "...Keep the 'and why'."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_bag_4:
BAGGY: "My line. Yes. Of course I remember my line. My line is... 'Who goes there.'" A pause. "Who GOES there. WHO goes there. Who goes THERE. Who goes there?" Another pause. "Which one's right? They're all right, aren't they? That's the problem with a good line."

You spend twenty minutes on 'Who goes there.' It is, in the end, perfect.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_sabrino:
The left-hand curtain is on fire. Sabrino is standing next to it, beaming, with a ladle.

SABRINO: "It is FINE. It is a rehearsal fire. It is practising." The fire gets bigger. "For the dragon scene! I am testing the special effects! Fireworks in Act Three, a little smoke in Act Four, and for the finale..." Sabrino makes an explosion noise with both hands.

ODETTE (from behind her chair): "THE CURTAINS ARE VELVET."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_sabrino.c0: [Calm] Put the fire out with Sabrino's soup pot. Discuss safety afterwards.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_sabrino.c1: [Enthusiastic] "Bigger! The back row deserves to feel the heat!"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_sabrino.c2: [Bureaucratic] "Have you filed the correct pyrotechnics form?"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_sab_2:
The fire goes out with a hiss and a smell of minestrone. Sabrino looks into the empty pot, heartbroken.

SABRINO: "That was dinner."

ODETTE: "That was my CURTAIN."

SABRINO (brightening): "Then tonight, we eat the curtain. I can do things with velvet. You would be amazed."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_sab_3:
SABRINO: "FINALLY. Somebody who UNDERSTANDS."

The fire gets very much bigger. Then it turns green. Then it turns into the shape of a goose, honks once, and goes out on its own.

Everyone stares at Sabrino. Sabrino stares at the smoke. "...I did not do that," Sabrino says. "I am going to take the credit, but I did not do that."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_sab_4:
SABRINO: "A FORM?" Sabrino's hat quivers with outrage. "I have set fire to the finest stages in seven kingdoms! I have never filled in a form in my LIFE!"

From the side of the stage, Clerk Oakhaven, or the memory of him, coughs meaningfully. Sabrino puts the fire out with one finger, extremely sulkily.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_marta:
MARTA (from the prompter's box, at a volume that could stop a cart): "LINE: 'THOUGH THE LEDGER STRIKE MY NAME.'"

Everyone flinches.

MARTA: "Sorry. Sorry! I'm used to calling orders across a full tavern." She clears her throat and tries again, in what she clearly thinks is a whisper: "LINE: 'THOUGH THE LEDGER-'"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_marta.c0: [Gentle] Show Marta how to whisper so only the actor can hear.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_marta.c1: [Inspired] "Keep it loud. Make it part of the show. The audience will love you."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_marta.c2: [Honest] "Marta, you could just learn the lines and come on stage."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_mar_2:
You crouch by the prompter's box and show her: lips close, breath soft, words shaped rather than spoken. Marta practises. By the fifth try it's perfect: a voice right at your ear, warm and sure, like someone reading you a story.

MARTA (whispering, smiling): "I used to read to Ilse like this. Funny what your mouth remembers."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_mar_3:
ODETTE: "A PROMPTER WHO IS PART OF THE PLAY. A chorus of one! A Greek tragedy with a bakery! Oh, I'm going to be SO FAMOUS."

Marta looks pleased and alarmed in equal measure. "So I just... shout the lines? On purpose?"

ODETTE: "WITH CONVICTION."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_mar_4:
Marta goes red to the ears. "On the STAGE? Me?" She looks at the boards, at the lights, at the empty chairs. "I'm a baker. I'm not... I don't..."

Then, quietly: "I'll stay in the box. But thank you for asking. Nobody's ever asked." She squeezes your hand. "LINE," she whispers, perfectly, "'THOUGH THE LEDGER STRIKE MY NAME.'"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_fenwick:
FENWICK (from the narrator's lectern, every time anyone speaks): "SHH!"

ROLF: "I'm not even-"

FENWICK: "SHHH!"

ODETTE: "Darling, you are the NARRATOR, the actors are SUPPOSED to talk-"

FENWICK: "I have spent forty years in a library. I cannot hear voices in a room full of words without shushing them. It is a REFLEX."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_fenwick.c0: [Clever] Give Fenwick a bell to ring instead. One ring per shush.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_fenwick.c1: [Patient] Hold a reading of the script, library-style. Silent. Turn the pages together.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_fenwick.c2: [Bribe] "Sabrino has your cookbook. You can have it back after the show."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_fen_2:
Fenwick rings the bell. Then rings it again. Then rings it in a little rhythm. By the end of the scene he is accompanying the entire sword fight on bell, with tremendous dramatic timing.

ODETTE: "...Keep the bell. Keep ALL of the bell."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_fen_3:
For one strange, peaceful half-hour the whole cast sits on the edge of the stage and reads the script in total silence, turning pages together. Hollis reads with his lips moving. Ashgrave weeps quietly at Act Two. Rolf falls asleep on Baggy's shoulder.

FENWICK (closing the script, whispering): "There. Now you understand it. Now you can make noise."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_fen_4:
Fenwick stops mid-shush. His mouth stays in the shape of the 'sh' for several seconds.

FENWICK: "The cookbook. ELEVEN YEARS OVERDUE." He straightens his robe with trembling dignity. "I shall narrate like no narrator has ever narrated. I shall narrate the paint off the walls."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_oakhaven:
CLERK OAKHAVEN (standing centre stage, holding up one hand): "I'm afraid I must stop the rehearsal."

ODETTE: "WHY."

OAKHAVEN: "Form 12-F, Fire Safety in Places of Public Entertainment. Section three: 'No live flames within six feet of any curtain.' Section four: 'No dragons.'" He looks at Hollis in the blanket. "I'll need to see the dragon's papers."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_oakhaven.c0: [Bureaucratic] Fill in Form 12-F on the spot, in triplicate.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_oakhaven.c1: [Theatrical] "The dragon is a metaphor, Oakhaven. For grief."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_oakhaven.c2: [Distract] "Oakhaven, your Herald costume has a very official hat."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_oak_2:
You fill in Form 12-F in triplicate, while the whole cast watches in silence. Under 'Nature of dragon' you write 'Hollis.' Under 'Is the dragon licensed?' you write 'He has eleven real ones on his record.'

Oakhaven reads it twice, stamps it, and hands it back with real respect. "Exemplary. You have the soul of a clerk."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_oak_3:
OAKHAVEN: "A metaphor." He writes it down. "For grief." He writes that down too. He looks at Hollis for a long time. Hollis looks back, in his oven gloves.

OAKHAVEN (quietly): "There's no form for grief." He closes his folder. "Carry on."
strings.dlg.odette.reh_oak_4:
Oakhaven looks at the Herald's hat: three tiers, gold braid, a plume like a startled pheasant. He puts it on. He looks in the mirror.

OAKHAVEN: "The fire safety inspection is concluded. Everything is fine. I am the Herald."

He does not take the hat off for the rest of the day.
strings.dlg.odette.reh_done:
Odette climbs onto her director's chair and claps her hands three times.

"That's a WRAP on rehearsal, my darlings! You are a disaster. A beautiful, magnificent disaster. Which is exactly what every great company is the night before it opens."

She turns to you. "Props, darling! We need three. A CROWN for the King. A DRAGON costume that isn't a blanket. And SOMETHING THAT GOES BANG for Act Three. Get them, and we open!"
strings.dlg.odette.reh_done.c0: "A crown, a dragon, and a bang. On it."
strings.dlg.odette.props_status:
"A CROWN: the King must have a crown. Paper will do, gold would be better, a crown with a story would be best.

A DRAGON: that blanket is an insult to dragons. Try the quartermaster. He sells everything.

SOMETHING THAT GOES BANG: fireworks, thunder, a controlled explosion. Ask the witch. Or a clerk, clerks confiscate everything."
strings.dlg.odette.props_status.c0: [Offer the Rat King's crown] "Will a real crown do? It was a rat's."
strings.dlg.odette.props_ratcrown:
Odette holds the tiny golden crown up to the light. "A real crown. Taken from a real king. In real combat." She lowers her voice. "Was it a very large rat?"

You nod. She sighs with deep satisfaction. "Method props. Divine. I'll give it back after the show, darling."
strings.dlg.odette.props_done:
Odette lays them out on the edge of the stage like holy relics: the crown, the dragon, the thing that goes bang.

"We have a theatre. We have a cast. We have a script, however annotated. We have props." She turns to you, eyes shining. "And we have a lead."

"Tonight, darling. The Tragedie of the Uncounted King. Opening night. Mortimer Quill has promised to attend, which means he's promised to hate it." She grips your hands. "Let's make him hate it LESS."
strings.dlg.odette.show_open:
The Hollowmere ballroom is full. Every borrowed chair is taken; people are standing at the back, sitting on the stairs, hanging off the gallery. Somewhere in the third row, a pale figure in a top hat sits with a notebook open and a red quill poised. Mortimer Quill.

Odette steps in front of the curtain and the room goes quiet.

ODETTE: "Ladies, gentlemen, ghosts and assorted others. The Velour Players present: The Tragedie of the Uncounted King!"

The curtain rises. You are standing in a pool of light. Two hundred faces look at you. Your mouth is completely dry.
strings.dlg.odette.show_open.c0: [Breathe] Find one friendly face in the crowd, and begin.
strings.dlg.odette.show_open.c1: [Bow first] Take a deep, theatrical bow before saying a single word.
strings.dlg.odette.show_open.c2: [Freeze] Stare at the audience in silent terror.
strings.dlg.odette.act1_freeze:
You open your mouth. Nothing comes out. The silence goes on for long enough that somebody coughs. Then a little longer. Mortimer Quill writes something down.

From the prompter's box, a voice right at your ear, warm and sure: "Line. 'I wake. And no one knows my name.'"

And suddenly, you do remember. Of course you do.
strings.dlg.odette.act1_freeze.c0: "I wake. And no one knows my name."
strings.dlg.odette.act1:
ACT ONE. The stage is the inside of a great ledger, pages towering like walls. You are the Uncounted King, waking in the margin of a book where your name has been struck out.

THE NARRATOR: "Once there was a King whom all the world forgot. Not by war, nor plague, nor the slow grey dust of years, but by a single stroke of ink."

The script says the King now delivers a sorrowful line. The audience is waiting.
strings.dlg.odette.act1.c0: [As written] "Who struck my name? Who dares to strike a king?"
strings.dlg.odette.act1.c1: [Improvise] "Is this the Bureau? I'd like to file a complaint."
strings.dlg.odette.act1.c2: [Your audition voice] Deliver it exactly the way you did for Odette.
strings.dlg.odette.act1_laugh:
The audience laughs. Then laughs harder. Somebody in the back shouts "FORM 27-B!" and the whole room loses it. In the front row, Clerk Oakhaven is wiping his eyes.

Odette, in the wings, is making frantic 'more of that' gestures. Mortimer Quill's quill has stopped moving.
strings.dlg.odette.act1_style: You give it your audition voice. The audience has no idea what's coming.
strings.dlg.odette.act1_style.c0: [The dramatic one] Arms flung wide. "WHO STRUCK MY NAME?!"
strings.dlg.odette.act1_style.c1: [The haunted whisper] Barely audible. Everyone leans in.
strings.dlg.odette.act1_style.c2: [The Italian witch] "Who struck-a my NAME? Mamma mia, the PAPERWORK!"
strings.dlg.odette.act1_style.c3: [The nervous detective] "Who struck my name? And, more importantly... WHY?"
strings.dlg.odette.act1_style.c4: [The monster hunter] Stare at the ledger. "Hmm."
strings.dlg.odette.act2: ACT TWO. Enter PRINCE VALIANT, sword drawn, and the GHOST OF THE OLD KING, rising from behind the ledger in a drift of dry ice. They are meant to duel over your fate.
strings.dlg.odette.act2.c0: Watch Rolf and Ashgrave take the stage.
strings.dlg.odette.act2.c1: Watch Odette play both parts at once, in a false moustache.
strings.dlg.odette.act2_pair:
ROLF (as Prince Valiant, raising his sword): "Spectre! Release the King!"

ASHGRAVE (as the Ghost, sweeping his cape): "Never! For I too was forgotten, and I will not be forgotten ALONE!"

They circle each other. Swords touch. And then Rolf, very quietly, not in the script at all, says: "You don't have to be alone."

Ashgrave freezes. The audience freezes. Odette, in the wings, has stopped breathing. They are both looking at you, the King, for what comes next.
strings.dlg.odette.act2_pair.c0: [Stay in character] "Then let us all be counted. Together." Join their hands.
strings.dlg.odette.act2_pair.c1: [Break character] Step back, gesture to the two of them, and let them have the moment.
strings.dlg.odette.act2_pair.c2: [Prompt them back] Cough, loudly, and say "Act Two, Scene Two?"
strings.dlg.odette.act2_moment:
You step back into the shadows. On the stage, a werewolf and a vampire stand very close together under a single spotlight, not saying anything at all.

Then Ashgrave, very slowly, takes Rolf's hand. Somewhere in the gallery, someone starts clapping. Then everyone is clapping. Then everyone is standing.

Mortimer Quill has put his quill down entirely.
strings.dlg.odette.act2_moment.c0: Let the applause die down, and carry on.
strings.dlg.odette.act2_solo:
Odette sweeps on in a cape, a moustache and a crown, and plays both the Prince and the Ghost by spinning round between every line. "Spectre! Release the King!" Spin. "NEVER!" Spin. "Then have at thee!" Spin, spin, spin.

By the end of the duel she is very dizzy and has stabbed herself twice. The audience has never seen anything like it.
strings.dlg.odette.act2_solo.c0: [Roll] Catch her before she falls off the stage.
strings.dlg.odette.act3: ACT THREE. The lights go red. The floor trembles. From the back of the stage, rising over the painted mountains, comes THE DRAGON.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_hollis:
Hollis, in the dragon costume, rises up behind the mountains. He looks out at two hundred people. Two hundred people look back.

HOLLIS (as THE DRAGON, in a voice like a cellar door): "Hmm."

It is the scariest thing anyone in the room has ever heard. A child in the front row bursts into delighted tears. The dragon's one line is delivered. Now the King must face it.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_hollis.c0: [Roll: Athletics] Dodge the dragon's lunge with a dramatic roll across the stage.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_hollis.c1: [Speak to it] "I know you. You were forgotten too." Offer the dragon your hand.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_blanket:
Two stagehands under a green blanket shuffle out from behind the mountains. One of them is clearly Odette. The other one might be a goat.

ODETTE (from inside the blanket): "ROAR."

The goat bleats. The audience is delighted.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_blanket.c0: [Roll: Athletics] Dodge the 'dragon' with a dramatic roll across the stage.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_blanket.c1: [Speak to it] "I know you. You were forgotten too." Offer the dragon your hand.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_fall:
You roll dramatically across the stage, misjudge the edge, and roll straight off it into the orchestra pit, which is Sabrino's soup pot. There is a splash. There is a silence.

Then you climb back onto the stage, dripping minestrone, raise one fist, and the audience goes absolutely wild.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_fall.c0: Shake off the soup. On with the show.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_fx: Now: the big moment of Act Three. The dragon is defeated, and the stage directions say simply: SOMETHING GOES BANG.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_bang:
Sabrino, in the wings, raises a ladle like a conductor.

The fireworks go off. All of them. At once. Gold and green and purple stars burst over the stage, a rocket shoots up into the ballroom chandelier and turns it, briefly, into a second sun. For one glorious moment the whole room is full of light, and smoke, and somewhere, faintly, the smell of garlic.

When the smoke clears, the curtains are only slightly on fire. Nobody minds.
strings.dlg.odette.act3_thunder:
Backstage, someone shakes the great tin thunder-sheet that Oakhaven confiscated in a previous decade. It makes a noise like the sky falling down a staircase. The candles shiver. A dog outside howls back. Rolf, somewhere, howls back at the dog.

It is magnificent.
strings.dlg.odette.act4:
ACT FOUR. The finale. The stage is bare now, except for a single desk: the desk of the Bureau, and behind it, a clerk with a quill, ready to strike the last name from the ledger. Yours.

The room goes completely still. This is the Great Speech. In the prompter's box, someone is holding their breath.
strings.dlg.odette.act4.c0: [As written] Deliver the Great Speech exactly as Odette wrote it.
strings.dlg.odette.act4.c1: [From the heart] Put down the script. Speak about being remembered, in your own words.
strings.dlg.odette.act4.c2: [Your audition voice] Do it the way you did it the very first time.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_speech:
"Though the ledger strike my name, though the ink run dry,
    Though every clerk in every hall forget that I was I,
    I stand here still, I breathe here still, and this I swear:
    A name held true by one who loves is never truly bare."

And now, the line. The one that brings the house down.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_heart:
You put the script down on the clerk's desk.

You tell them about the notice that arrived saying you were dead. About a baker who couldn't remember her sister's name, and a detective who never stopped looking for a girl with flour on her nose. About a ghost who laid a table for ninety years. About how a ledger can say anything it likes, but it can't stop people remembering each other.

Nobody in the room is moving. Odette is crying openly in the wings. And now, the last line.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_style: You give the Great Speech your audition voice, the very one that got you the part.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_style.c0: [The dramatic one] Every word to the rafters.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_style.c1: [The haunted whisper] So quiet that two hundred people hold their breath to hear it.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_style.c2: [The Italian witch] With hand gestures. ALL the hand gestures.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_style.c3: [The nervous detective] As if you've just solved the case of your own existence.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_style.c4: [The monster hunter] Read the entire speech. Pause. "Hmm."
strings.dlg.odette.act4_cucumber:
You take a mighty breath. You open your mouth. And from somewhere deep in your memory, from the audition, it comes out again:

"I AM CUCUMBER!"

A silence. And then the entire audience, who have all heard about the audition because it is a very small town, roars it back at you: "I AM CUCUMBER!" It becomes a chant. It goes on for some time.

It's not what Odette wrote. It might be better.
strings.dlg.odette.act4_counted:
"I AM COUNTED."

For a heartbeat there is nothing. Then the clerk behind the desk, Oakhaven or Odette or someone in a borrowed hat, lowers the quill, and closes the ledger, and stands, and begins to applaud.

The curtain comes down.
strings.dlg.odette.bow_hub:
Behind the curtain the whole cast is clutching each other, shaking, laughing, half of them crying. Odette has fainted into Hollis's arms. On the other side of the velvet, the noise of the audience is like rain on a roof.

The curtain begins to rise again for the curtain call.
strings.dlg.odette.bow_disaster: Applause, laughter, and at least one thrown vegetable.
strings.dlg.odette.after:
Odette is sitting on the edge of the stage with her hat in her lap, looking at the empty ballroom with an expression you haven't seen on her before. Peaceful.

"Do you know, darling, I've been travelling with that cart for thirty years. Every town, the same: set up the stage, find a cast, open, close, move on. Never stayed long enough to learn anybody's name."

"Bellwether is the first place that learned mine." She puts her hat back on. "I think the Velour Players might stay a while. There's a ghost in the library who's already writing reviews of the next one."
strings.dlg.mortimer.root:
Between two bookshelves, a thin, translucent gentleman in a top hat is reading a book with an expression of profound disgust. Without looking up, he licks a ghostly finger and turns the page.

"An intruder. How derivative." He makes a note in a red notebook. "Your entrance: one star. Your coat: two. Your general air of having been declared legally dead: three and a half. That's quite good, actually. Don't let it go to your head."
strings.dlg.mortimer.root.c2: "You stole Madame Odette's script. I want it back."
strings.dlg.mortimer.root.c4: "So. What did you think of the show?"
strings.dlg.mortimer.who:
"Mortimer Quill. Critic. The most feared pen in the history of the stage." He says it without pride, as a simple statement of fact, like 'the sea is wet'.

"In life I reviewed four thousand plays. Three thousand nine hundred and ninety-eight of them were bad. Then I died, during the second act of a farce, which I maintain was the farce's fault. And I found I simply couldn't stop."

"I have been reviewing ever since. The weather. Furniture. Other ghosts. This library: two stars. The bestsellers: one."
strings.dlg.mortimer.review:
Mortimer looks around for something to review. His eyes settle on you.

"THE ADVENTURER. A production in one act, apparently endless. The lead has energy, if not direction. The costume is practical but uninspired. The sword work: competent. The inventory management: frankly alarming. Why are you carrying nine loaves of bread?"

He snaps the notebook shut. "Two and a half stars. Shows promise. Needs an editor."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_1:
Mortimer closes his book with a soft, final thump.

"The Velour woman's play. Yes. I have it." He pats a pocket that rustles. "I took it to save the public from another evening of her work. It is a kindness. One day, they will thank me."

"But you are welcome to try to change my mind. In the traditional way." He rises, hovering slightly. "A duel of criticism. Three rounds. I critique. You defend. If you win, the play is yours. Round one: the opening. 'A King wakes in a ledger.' Derivative. Done to death. Literally, in my case. Defend it."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_1.c0: [Roll: Lore] "Every great story starts with someone forgotten. That's not derivative. That's ancient."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_1.c1: [Personal] "I woke up last week to a letter saying I was dead. It's not derivative. It's documentary."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_1w:
Mortimer's quill hovers over the notebook. Hovers a little longer.

"...Point taken." He writes something. It might be the first point he has conceded in two hundred years. "Round two."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_1l: "Hm. Weak. Fumbled. You started a sentence with 'Um'." He writes a single scathing word. "Round one to me. Round two."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_2: "Round two: the characters. A werewolf who wants to be loved. A vampire who wants to be tragic. A dragon who says nothing. A baker who shouts. These are not characters. These are your NEIGHBOURS." He sneers. "Where is the art in that?"
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_2.c0: [Roll: Persuasion] "That's exactly the art. You've watched kings and gods for two hundred years. When did you last watch your neighbours?"
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_2.c1: [Theatrical] "They're not my neighbours. They're my FRIENDS. Two stars for you, sir."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_2w:
Mortimer opens his mouth to reply. Then closes it.

"...When did I last..." He looks, for just a moment, out of the library window, towards the lights of Bellwether. Then he coughs, very firmly. "Irrelevant. Round two to you. Barely. Final round."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_2l: "Sentiment! Pure sentiment!" Mortimer makes a long, scratchy note. "Round two to me. One more, and I keep the play. Final round."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_3: "Final round. And I warn you, I have been saving this one for forty years." He leans in. "Act Three. What, precisely, is WRONG with Act Three?"
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_3.c2: "It needs a dragon. A better one."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_3w:
Mortimer Quill goes absolutely still. His quill falls out of his hand and floats gently to the floor.

"...It needs a better dragon," he whispers. "I wrote that in the margin. Forty years ago. Of her first draft. Nobody ever READ the margins." He stares at you. "You read the margins."
strings.dlg.mortimer.duel_3l: "Wrong." He sounds almost disappointed. "The answer was in the margins. It's always in the margins. Nobody ever reads the margins."
strings.dlg.mortimer.verdict: Mortimer gathers himself, straightens his hat, and makes a final, ceremonial note.
strings.dlg.mortimer.verdict_win:
"The duel is yours." He draws a velvet-bound script out of his coat and holds it out with both hands, the way you'd return a sword.

"Tell the Velour woman I shall attend her opening night. In the third row, where I have always sat. I shall bring my notebook. I shall almost certainly hate it." A pause. "But I shall attend."

He drifts back towards his bookshelf. Without turning round, he adds: "Your defence: four stars. Don't tell anyone."
strings.dlg.mortimer.verdict_win.c0: "See you in the third row, Mortimer."
strings.dlg.mortimer.verdict_lose:
"The duel is mine." Mortimer looks at the script in his hand for a long moment. Then, with a sound like a very old door, he sighs, and holds it out anyway.

"Take it. I've read it eleven times now. It's... it's not as bad as I said. Don't tell her that."

"Tell the Velour woman I shall attend. Third row. To make sure it's as bad as I remember." He turns away. "It won't be. That's the worst part."
strings.dlg.mortimer.coming:
"Opening night?" He sniffs. "I wouldn't miss it. Somebody has to be there to be disappointed."

He tries to look disdainful. It doesn't quite work. "Third row. Centre. Reserve it. And tell the Velour woman I will not tolerate a goat in the dragon costume. Again."
strings.dlg.mortimer.after_show:
Mortimer is sitting on the edge of a bookshelf, his notebook closed in his lap. He doesn't look up.

"Two hundred years," he says quietly. "Four thousand plays. And I never once watched one with people I knew in it."

He opens the notebook to the review he wrote last night and looks at it for a long time. "I'm going to keep coming, you know. To her plays. Every one. Third row." A pause. "To be disappointed, obviously."
strings.dlg.baggy.players.topic_cast_baggy: "Baggy, how would you feel about being in a play?"
strings.dlg.baggy.players.cast_baggy:
Baggy freezes. "A play. On a STAGE. With an AUDIENCE." The magnifying glass is clutched to the chest.

"What's the part? Is it a detective? It's a detective, isn't it. Tell me it's a detective."

You explain it's the Second Guard. One line. 'Who goes there.'

"Who goes there." A long pause. "WHO goes there. Who goes THERE." Baggy's eyes are shining. "I can work with this. There's a lot of character in 'who'. I'm in. I'm so in. I'm going to need a hat."
strings.dlg.rolf.players.topic_cast_rolf: "Rolf, a theatre company needs a Prince Valiant. Dashing, heroic, sword fight. Interested?"
strings.dlg.rolf.players.cast_rolf:
Rolf drops his trowel. "A PRINCE?" He looks down at himself, then up at you. "Me? I'm a gardener. I'm a werewolf gardener. Princes don't have fur on their knuckles."

Then, slowly, with growing hope: "...Is there a ghost in it? Like, a pale tragic ghost? Who might need rescuing? Or who might rescue me? Either. Both." He clears his throat. "I'll do it. Will I have to wear a shirt?"
strings.dlg.ashgrave.players.topic_cast_ashgrave: "Lord Ashgrave, a play needs a Ghost of the Old King. Pale. Tragic. Very still."
strings.dlg.ashgrave.players.cast_ashgrave:
Ashgrave turns from the window so fast his cape wraps round him twice.

"A GHOST. A tragic, forgotten king, doomed to haunt the halls of his own lost glory." He places a hand on his chest. "I have been rehearsing for this role for three hundred years."

Then, suspiciously: "Who plays the Prince?"
strings.dlg.hollis.players.topic_cast_hollis: "Hollis. How do you feel about playing a dragon?"
strings.dlg.hollis.players.cast_hollis:
"No."

You explain about the play. Hollis listens without blinking.

"No."

You explain that the dragon has only one line. Hollis looks at you for a long moment.

"...What's the line?"
strings.dlg.hollis.players.cast_hollis.c0: [Roll: Persuasion] "'ROAR.' With three exclamation marks. Nobody else could do it justice."
strings.dlg.hollis.players.cast_hollis_yes:
Hollis is quiet for a long time.

"Hmm," he says at last, which you have learned means yes.
strings.dlg.hollis.players.cast_hollis_cards:
"No." He shuffles a deck. "Tell you what. I win this hand, I'm not doing it."

He loses the hand. He looks at his cards for a long time. You're fairly sure he lost on purpose.

"Hmm. Fine. Dragon."
strings.dlg.sabrino.players.topic_cast_sabrino: "Sabrino, a theatre company needs someone who knows about fire."
strings.dlg.sabrino.players.cast_sabrino:
Sabrino stops stirring. Sabrino turns, very slowly, ladle dripping.

"Pyrotechnics?" A whisper. "You are asking ME to set things on fire, on purpose, in front of an audience, for ART?"

"I accept. I also do the catering. Interval snacks. Fireworks in Act Three. A small, tasteful explosion for the finale. I will not be taking questions."
strings.dlg.sabrino.players.topic_prop_bang: "Odette needs something that goes BANG for Act Three."
strings.dlg.sabrino.players.prop_bang:
Sabrino opens the hat. It contains, among other things, a frankly alarming number of rockets.

"Gold, green, purple, and one I call The Goose. Do not ask about The Goose." They are pressed into your arms. "Light the fuse, step back, then step back further. Then further than that. Then, enjoy."
strings.dlg.marta.players.topic_cast_marta: "Marta, a theatre company needs a prompter. Someone who remembers everything."
strings.dlg.marta.players.cast_marta:
Marta laughs. "Me? Remember everything? Seventeen years I couldn't remember my own sister's face."

Then she stops laughing, and thinks about it. "...But I remember every order in this inn. Who takes their ale warm, who wants the crust, who's not to be served after the third." She dusts off her hands. "I'll do it. I'll whisper your lines. I'm very good at whispering. I whisper to the bread."
strings.dlg.fenwick.players.topic_cast_fenwick: "Fenwick, a play needs a Narrator. A commanding voice. A love of words."
strings.dlg.fenwick.players.cast_fenwick:
Fenwick draws himself up to his full height, which is not very high, and adjusts his spectacles with great ceremony.

"A Narrator. The voice that carries the tale. The one who stands between the story and the dark." He clears his throat. "I have been reading stories aloud to empty aisles for forty years. Yes. YES. I accept."

"I shall require a lectern. And absolute silence from the audience. Absolute."
strings.dlg.fenwick.players.topic_prop_crown: "Odette needs a crown for the King. Anything in the library?"
strings.dlg.fenwick.players.prop_crown:
Fenwick vanishes into the stacks and comes back with a crown made of gold paper, carefully folded from the dust jacket of a very bad romance novel.

"'Fifty Shades of Grey Robes'," he says, without meeting your eye. "Chapter Nine is printed on the inside. Wear it facing forward, and nobody will know."
strings.dlg.clerk.players.topic_cast_oakhaven: "Clerk Oakhaven, a play needs a Herald. Loud. Official. Fond of paperwork."
strings.dlg.clerk.players.cast_oakhaven: Oakhaven puts down his quill. "A Herald." He considers it. "I would of course require Form 99-T, Application to Participate in Theatrical Entertainment." He produces it. It is four pages long. "Question one. Is the performance intended to be: (a) amusing, (b) tragic, or (c) a tax write-off?"
strings.dlg.clerk.players.form_2: He ticks a box. "Question two. Will the performance contain any of the following: dragons, fire, ghosts, witches, or singing?"
strings.dlg.clerk.players.form_3:
He ticks another box, slightly faster. "Question three, final question. Is the applicant, at the time of application, legally alive?"

He looks up at you over his spectacles. You look back at him.
strings.dlg.clerk.players.form_done:
Oakhaven stamps Form 99-T with a sound like a judge's gavel, then, after a moment's thought, stamps it again for luck.

"Approved. I shall be the Herald." He looks down at his plain grey coat. "Is there... a hat?"

You assure him there is a hat.

"Then I am at your service." A very small smile. "Nobody has ever asked me to be in anything before."
strings.dlg.clerk.players.topic_prop_thunder: "Odette needs something that goes BANG. Anything in the confiscated property cupboard?"
strings.dlg.clerk.players.prop_thunder:
Oakhaven's eyes light up the way a clerk's only do when asked about a cupboard. He returns with a huge sheet of tin and a label: CONFISCATED - 'THUNDER, THEATRICAL, ONE (1)'.

"Shake it," he says. "Firmly. Fill out the receipt."
strings.dlg.vaelen.players.topic_prop_dragon: "I need a dragon costume. A proper one."
strings.dlg.vaelen.players.prop_dragon:
Vaelen doesn't even blink. He disappears into the back room and returns with an enormous green costume: scales sewn from old leather, wings of oilcloth on willow frames, a head with real glass eyes and a jaw that opens.

"Somebody ordered it nine years ago and never collected it. A monster hunter, I think. Said it was 'for a contract'." He shrugs. "On the house. Just get it out of my shop. It watches me."
strings.campaign.players.name: The Bellwether Players
strings.campaign.players.desc: Madame Odette Velour has a cart, a costume trunk and the greatest play ever written. All she needs is a cast. And you.
strings.quest.casting.title: Act I: Casting Call
strings.quest.casting.summary: A travelling impresario needs a lead for The Tragedie of the Uncounted King. Apparently you have the face for it.
strings.quest.casting.stage0: Audition for Madame Odette Velour, near Bellwether's south gate.
strings.quest.casting.journal0: A woman in a very large magenta hat told me I have a face that has suffered. She wants me to audition.
strings.quest.casting.stage10: Recruit at least four cast members and tell Odette. Prince, Ghost, Dragon, Herald, Narrator, Second Guard, prompter, fireworks: ask around Bellwether, the Old Road and Hollowmere.
strings.quest.casting.journal10: I got the lead. The only other person who auditioned was a goat. Now I need a cast, and I know exactly the right collection of lovely, ridiculous people.
strings.quest.casting.stage100: Completed: the Velour Players have a cast.
strings.quest.casting.journal100: The cast is assembled. Odette hugged me hard enough to realign my spine. Then she opened her trunk and the script was gone.
strings.quest.script.title: Act II: The Missing Script
strings.quest.script.summary: Mortimer Quill, the most feared critic in history (deceased), has stolen the only copy of Odette's play and scattered the pages.
strings.quest.script.stage0: Find the five scattered script pages. Look anywhere dusty, gloomy or important: the Records Office, the Old Road, the Annex, Vault III, Hollowmere's library.
strings.quest.script.journal0: Somebody stole Odette's script and left a card: 'One and a half stars. Derivative. - M.Q.' Mortimer Quill, a critic who has been dead for two hundred years and hasn't let it slow him down.
strings.quest.script.stage10: The trail ends in Hollowmere's library. Confront Mortimer Quill and win back the script.
strings.quest.script.journal10: The last page was in Hollowmere's library, and so was the critic: a thin ghost in a top hat, reviewing the books. I'll have to win the script back. In a duel. Of criticism.
strings.quest.script.stage20: Bring the script back to Madame Odette.
strings.quest.script.journal20: Mortimer gave me the script. He's coming to opening night, third row, to be disappointed.
strings.quest.script.journal100: Odette kissed the script three times and read the margins with growing outrage. We rehearse at Hollowmere.
strings.quest.rehearsal.title: Act III: Dress Rehearsal
strings.quest.rehearsal.summary: A cast of a werewolf, a vampire, a monster hunter, a detective, a witch, a baker, a librarian and a clerk, in one ballroom. What could go wrong?
strings.quest.rehearsal.stage0: Join Odette in the Hollowmere ballroom and get the cast through rehearsal (solve at least three backstage dramas).
strings.quest.rehearsal.journal0: Odette has turned Hollowmere's ballroom into a theatre. The cast has turned it into a circus.
strings.quest.rehearsal.stage10: Find the three props: a CROWN (Fenwick, or a real one), a DRAGON costume (Vaelen) and SOMETHING THAT GOES BANG (Sabrino, or Oakhaven's confiscated cupboard). Then tell Odette.
strings.quest.rehearsal.journal10: We survived rehearsal. Odette says we're a magnificent disaster, which is apparently what every great company is the night before it opens.
strings.quest.rehearsal.journal100: Crown, dragon, bang. Opening night is tonight.
strings.quest.opening.title: Act IV: Opening Night
strings.quest.opening.summary: The Tragedie of the Uncounted King. One night only. Probably.
strings.quest.opening.stage0: Tell Odette when you're ready for curtain up, in the Hollowmere ballroom.
strings.quest.opening.journal0: Two hundred people, one ballroom, one ghost critic in the third row. My mouth is already dry.
strings.quest.opening.stage100: Completed: the Tragedie of the Uncounted King has opened.
strings.quest.opening.journal100: We did it. Whatever Mortimer Quill wrote, the whole town was in that room, and every one of them knows my name now.
strings.npc.odette.name: Madame Odette Velour
strings.npc.odette.title: Impresario of the Velour Players
strings.npc.mortimer.name: Mortimer Quill
strings.npc.mortimer.title: The Last Critic (Deceased, Unimpressed)
strings.bark.odette.1: DARLING! Yes, you! The face! The SUFFERING!
strings.bark.odette.2: Five acts, two intervals, one dragon. And a cast of NOBODY. Yet.
strings.bark.odette.3: Projection, darlings! The back row is always full of farmers!
strings.bark.odette.after: Bellwether learned my name. I think I'll stay a while.
strings.bark.mortimer.after: Third row. Every play. To be disappointed. Obviously.
strings.story.show.curtain:
The curtain rises for the bows, and the room is on its feet.

The cast comes forward in a ragged line, holding hands: whoever you brought, in whatever costumes survived. Somebody is still slightly on fire. Somebody is still wearing oven gloves. Odette, in the middle, bows so low her hat falls off, and two hundred people in a ballroom in the rain cheer for a play about a king nobody remembered.

In the third row, Mortimer Quill is writing.
strings.story.show.review_triumph:
The next morning, a review is nailed to the door of the Lantern Inn, in spidery red ink:

"THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING. The Velour Players, Hollowmere.

I have attended four thousand and one plays. This was the first at which I forgot to take notes.

The lead was luminous. The dragon was terrifying. The second act contained an unscripted moment between a prince and a ghost that I will not describe, because it was not mine to review.

Five stars. I have never given five stars. I have checked whether I am still dead. I am. - M.Q."
strings.story.show.review_good:
The next morning, a review is nailed to the door of the Lantern Inn, in spidery red ink:

"THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING. The Velour Players, Hollowmere.

Uneven. Overlong. A dragon of questionable provenance. At least one actor was clearly reading from the inside of a paper crown.

And yet. When the lead spoke the final line, an entire village stood up at once, and I found that I had stood up with them. I am not sure how this happened. I am investigating.

Three and a half stars. Would attend again. Do not quote me. - M.Q."
strings.story.show.review_disaster:
The next morning, a review is nailed to the door of the Lantern Inn, in spidery red ink:

"THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING. The Velour Players, Hollowmere.

A catastrophe. A triumph of catastrophe. Lines were forgotten, scenery collapsed, a goat appeared in a role for which it was not cast, and the climax of the evening was the word 'cucumber', chanted by two hundred people.

I have not laughed since 1592. I laughed last night until I was nearly corporeal.

One star. The best one star I have ever given. I shall be back for the second night. - M.Q."
strings.story.show.after:
Long after the audience has gone home, the cast is still sitting on the edge of the stage, sharing Sabrino's interval snacks, passing round the paper crown, retelling the night to each other as if none of them were there.
