Odette, hat in her lap, looks round at all of them, and then at you.

"A cast," she says softly. "I'd forgotten what it was like to have one."
strings.item.script_tragedie.name: Script: The Tragedie of the Uncounted King
strings.item.script_tragedie.description: Odette's play, bound in velvet, heavily annotated in red by a ghost.
strings.book.script_tragedie.text:
THE TRAGEDIE OF THE UNCOUNTED KING
A play in five acts (four, after cuts), by Odette Velour

DRAMATIS PERSONAE:
THE UNCOUNTED KING, forgotten by all
PRINCE VALIANT, a hero with a sword and feelings
THE GHOST OF THE OLD KING, pale, tragic, very still
THE DRAGON, one line
THE HERALD, loud, official
THE NARRATOR, who would prefer you were quiet
SECOND GUARD (there is no First Guard; budget)

[In red, in the margin: 'There is no First Guard. Why is there a Second Guard. - M.Q.']

ACT ONE: The King wakes in the margin of a ledger, his name struck out.
ACT TWO: The Prince and the Ghost duel for the King's fate.
[Margin: 'They are clearly in love. Write it in or I will. - M.Q.']
ACT THREE: The Dragon.
[Margin: 'Needs a dragon. A better one. - M.Q.']
ACT FOUR: The Great Speech.

    Though the ledger strike my name, though the ink run dry,
    Though every clerk in every hall forget that I was I,
    I stand here still, I breathe here still, and this I swear:
    A name held true by one who loves is never truly bare.

    I AM COUNTED.

[Margin, in very small, shaky red letters: 'This bit is good. - M.']
strings.item.mask_uncounted.name: Mask of the Uncounted King
strings.item.mask_uncounted.description: The gilded half-mask you wore on opening night. Odette insisted you keep it. When you wear it, people turn to look at you, and for once you don't mind. +3 Presence, +5% spell power, +3% critical chance.
strings.item.thrown_tomato.name: Thrown Tomato
strings.item.thrown_tomato.description: Caught mid-air during the curtain call. A critic's gift. Still perfectly good to eat, and oddly motivating: +0.2 critical multiplier for 2 minutes.
strings.item.paper_crown.name: Paper Crown
strings.item.paper_crown.description: Folded from the dust jacket of a romance novel. Chapter Nine is printed on the inside. Wear it facing forward.
strings.item.dragon_costume.name: Dragon Costume
strings.item.dragon_costume.description: Leather scales, oilcloth wings, real glass eyes. Ordered nine years ago by a monster hunter 'for a contract'. It watches you.
strings.item.fireworks.name: Sabrino's Fireworks
strings.item.fireworks.description: Gold, green, purple, and one labelled THE GOOSE. Do not ask about The Goose.
strings.item.thunder_sheet.name: Thunder Sheet (Confiscated)
strings.item.thunder_sheet.description: A great sheet of tin. Shake firmly for weather. Comes with a receipt.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.bellwether: Bellwether. Population: one hundred and six, last I counted. Plus you. I'm counting you now.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.old_road: Home. Mind the third stone from the arch, it wobbles. I've written it down.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.annex: So this is where they kept the names. It smells like a library that's been holding its breath.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.vault_three: Forty small beds. I'm going to count them anyway. Someone should.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.seal_chamber: This is the room the whole Marches has been leaning on. Walk softly.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.hollowmere: Hollowmere. The Ashbound have three pages on this house. Two of them are about the gardener.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.hollowmere_manor: Twelve places laid at the table. I'll note that. Twelve's a hopeful number.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.1: Every stone on this road was somebody's doorstep once. I keep a list.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.2: The Ashbound have a rule: if you can't remember something, write it down twice.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.3: I counted the steps from the boundary stone to the Annex once. Four thousand and twelve. Then I lost count, because a rat bit me.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.4: You walk like someone who's used to being alone. It's all right. You'll get out of the habit.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.5: Ash is what's left when something burns. It still remembers the shape of the wood. That's us.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.6: I've started writing your name in my journal. Every day. Just in case.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.seal: The road doesn't hum any more. I miss it a little. Don't tell anyone.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.ilse: Ilse Brannock. I've written it in four places now. Can't be too careful.
strings.comp.kaelen.idle.dinner: That dinner. I read the names out loud and the whole table said them back. I'll never forget that. Literally: I wrote it down.
strings.comp.kaelen.combat.3: Here they come. Note the time.
strings.comp.kaelen.combat.4: I've fought worse. I wrote it down.
strings.comp.kaelen.kill.1: One less. I'm keeping a tally.
strings.comp.kaelen.heal.1: Here. Ashbound trail bread. Tastes like a promise.
strings.comp.kaelen.heal.2: Sit. Eat. The road will still be there in a minute.
strings.comp.kaelen.level.1: Stronger. I'm putting that in the journal. In capitals.
strings.comp.kaelen.level.2: Look at you. The road's taught you something.
strings.comp.kaelen.catchup.1: Took the long way. Counted some wells. I'm back.
strings.comp.kaelen.catchup.2: Sorry. There was an interesting stone.
strings.comp.kaelen.catchup.3: Caught up. Baggy wasn't the only one stuck on that door.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.intro.0: So, Kaelen. What's your story? Everybody has a story. I'm a detective. I can tell.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.intro.1: I walk. I count things. I write them down.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.intro.3: That's a lot, Baggy. Most people forget to do any of it.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.0: Baggy. How many suspects are on your case board right now?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.1: Four! The hedge, the Bureau, a goat, and me. I've ruled me out. Mostly.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.2: That's four more than I've got. I just count wells.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.3: What do the wells tell you?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.counting.4: That somebody was thirsty once. That's enough, usually.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.0: Kaelen. Be honest. Do you think the hedge did it?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.1: I've walked past that hedge four hundred times. It has never once done anything.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.2: EXACTLY. That's what a guilty hedge would do.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hedge.3: ...I'm adding the hedge to my journal. Under 'probably fine'.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.0: Baggy. The girl with flour on her nose. Ilse.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.1: Blue shutters. Mill Lane. I remember.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.2: I wrote her name in my journal. And yours, next to it. 'Remembered her when nobody else did.'
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.ilse.3: ...Oh. Oh, I'm not crying. It's the rain.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hollowmere.0: So. The vampire and the werewolf at Hollowmere.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hollowmere.3: I KNOW. I've got two pages of notes. They've been staring at each other's windows for ninety years.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.hollowmere.5: Somebody probably will. Somebody with terrible timing and a lot of heart.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.theatre.0: Baggy, Odette says you've got a line in the play.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.theatre.1: 'Who goes there.' It's a very demanding role.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.0: Kaelen. At the dinner. When you read the names.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.2: Everyone said them back. Even Oakhaven. Even Hollis.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.3: I know. I was there. I was the one crying into the gnocchi.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.dinner.4: I thought that was the pepper.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.0: The road's gone quiet. First time in seventeen years.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.2: Like taking off a heavy pack you forgot you were wearing.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.3: I've still got my umbrella. Out of habit. In case.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.seal.4: Keep it. You never know. And it suits you.
strings.dlg.scout.choice_join: "Kaelen, travel with me for a while? I could use someone who remembers things."
strings.dlg.scout.choice_wait: "Could you wait here for a bit, Kaelen?"
strings.dlg.scout.join:
Kaelen closes the journal, slowly, and looks at you for a long moment.

"The Ashbound walk alone, mostly. It's quieter. Less to write down." A pause. "It's also lonelier, and I've been out here a long time."

The journal goes back on the belt. "All right. I'll walk with you. I'll count things. I'll keep the names. And if you get hurt, I've got trail bread. It tastes like a promise."

"Fair warning: if Baggy's coming too, I'm going to be asked about the hedge."
strings.dlg.scout.wait: "I'll be here. Counting." Kaelen opens the journal again. "Come and find me when the road gets long."
strings.dlg.baggy.party_full.choice: "Want to come along?" [Your party is full]
strings.dlg.baggy.party_full:
Baggy looks at your companion, then at you, then nods with tremendous professionalism. "Two's company. Three's a crowd. Four's a stakeout, but we haven't got the snacks for it."

"Ask someone to wait somewhere, and I'll be right there. I'm never busy. I'll be by the hedge."
strings.dlg.scout.party_full.choice: "Want to come along?" [Your party is full]
strings.dlg.scout.party_full:
Kaelen glances at whoever is already walking with you and makes a small note. "You've got company. Good. The road's better that way."

"When there's room, come and find me. I'll be here. Counting."
strings.dlg.dnd.topic.pitch: "Oakhaven, what do you do on Thursdays?"
strings.dlg.dnd.topic.s1: "Is it Thursday? Is it game night?"
strings.dlg.dnd.topic.s2: "Game night. The dungeon awaits, Game Master."
strings.dlg.dnd.pitch:
Oakhaven goes very still. He glances left, right, then lowers his voice as if confessing to a crime.

"On Thursdays, after the office closes, a few of us gather at the back table of the Lantern Inn and play... a game." He produces a battered rulebook roughly the thickness of a paving stone. "DUNGEONS & DEBTORS. A game of heroic adventure, perilous dungeons and meticulous record-keeping."

"I am the Game Master." He says it with a dignity you have never seen in him before. "We are short a player. Hollis cheats, Rolf cries, and Baggy keeps trying to arrest the furniture. Would you... care to roll up a character?"
strings.dlg.dnd.pitch.c0: "I would love to roll up a character."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_rules:
Thursday. The back table of the Lantern Inn. Marta has put out bread, cheese and a pot of tea the size of a bucket. Around the table: Baggy, Rolf, Hollis, Lord Ashgrave ("I am only here for the atmosphere"), and Marta herself, pencil behind her ear.

Oakhaven sits behind a folding screen painted with dragons and tax tables. He hands you a sheet of paper.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Form 1-CS. Character Sheet. Please print clearly. First, we roll your attributes. Four dice, drop the lowest. No, Hollis, you may not 'help'."

HOLLIS: "Hmm."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_rules.c0: [Roll for Strength] Shake the dice in both hands and blow on them.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_rules.c1: [Let Hollis roll for you] He's very insistent.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_stats:
Sixteen! A respectable number. The table makes approving noises. Rolf claps. Baggy writes "16" in a notebook for reasons nobody understands.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Excellent. Now. Your class."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_stats_bad:
Four. You rolled a four. Two ones and a two and a... you check... another one.

There is a respectful silence around the table, the kind usually reserved for funerals.

MARTA (patting your hand): "You'll be a lovely character, dear. Characters with low numbers have the best stories."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...Your class."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_hollis:
Hollis takes your dice, turns his back to the table, and rolls. "Eighteen," he announces. "Eighteen. Eighteen. Eighteen. Eighteen. And an eighteen."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Hollis, show me the dice."

HOLLIS: "They rolled under the table."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "All six of them?"

HOLLIS: "Hmm."

You are given a ten in everything. Hollis looks satisfied anyway.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Choose your class. Each is described in Chapter Four, pages eighty through four hundred."

BAGGY (whispering): "I'm a Paladin of Justice. I can arrest people with my mind."

ROLF (whispering): "I'm playing a human accountant called Gerald. It's the most exotic thing I can imagine."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c0: [Barbarian] Big. Angry. Shirtless. Rolf looks at you with new respect.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c1: [Bard] You will solve every problem by singing at it. Including the dragon.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c2: [Rogue] Sneaky, stabby, and you will absolutely steal from the party.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c3: [Wizard] Robes. Fireballs. A beard you have to describe in detail.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_class.c4: [Paladin] Holy, righteous, and contractually obliged to lecture everyone.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "And finally: your backstory. Briefly, please. Ashgrave's was forty-one pages."

LORD ASHGRAVE: "It was a tragedy in five movements."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "It was a tragedy in the sense that I had to read it."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory.c0: [Tragic] "Orphaned. Twice. My village burned. Also my second village. I have a brooding scar and a sworn enemy."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory.c1: [Simple] "Farmer. Nothing happened. I'm just here for the adventure."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_backstory.c2: [Relatable] "Amnesiac. Legally dead. Owes burial tax. Nobody remembers them."
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_party:
One by one, the others introduce their characters, in character, with voices.

BAGGY: "Sir Detective Inspector Baggington, Paladin of Justice. I have a magnifying glass of plus-one perception."

ROLF: "Gerald. Human. Accountant. I enjoy spreadsheets and wearing shirts." He looks so happy about the shirts.

HOLLIS: "Grizzlebeard. Monster hunter. White hair. Two swords. Says 'hmm'."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "That's just you, Hollis."

HOLLIS: "Hmm."

LORD ASHGRAVE: "Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire. A paladin who avoids sunlight for entirely unrelated reasons."

MARTA: "Sister Crumb. A cleric. I heal with bread." She passes round actual bread. Everyone's hit points go up.
strings.dlg.dnd.s0_end:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "We start next Thursday. Character creation took four hours. It always takes four hours."

He gathers the sheets into a folder labelled CAMPAIGN: THE AMULET OF UNPAID TAXES, and almost, almost smiles.

"Same time next week. Bring dice. Bring snacks. Hollis, bring HONEST dice."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start:
Thursday again. The back table. The dragon screen goes up, Marta's tea goes round, and Oakhaven clears his throat.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session One. You all meet in a tavern."

A pause. Everyone looks around the Lantern Inn. At the bar. At Marta, pouring.

ROLF: "...We ARE in a tavern."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Then this will be very immersive. A hooded stranger approaches your table." He pulls up the hood of his coat, without moving from behind the screen. "'Greetings, adventurers. I have a quest.'"
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start.c0: [In character] "Speak, stranger. What do you need?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start.c1: [Suspicious] "I roll Insight on the hooded stranger."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_start.c2: [Out of character] "Oakhaven, that's just you in a hood."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_insight:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You sense that the hooded stranger is... the Game Master. In a hood."

HOLLIS: "I roll Insight too."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "He's still me, Hollis."

HOLLIS: "Hmm. Suspicious."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_hood:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "It is NOT me. It is Mysterious Hooded Stranger Number Four. He has a completely different voice." He clears his throat and does a completely identical voice. "'Greetings, adventurers.'"

The table dissolves. Marta snorts tea out of her nose. Oakhaven waits it out with tremendous patience.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_quest:
OAKHAVEN (GM, as the Stranger): "Deep beneath the hills lies the Dungeon of Mild Peril. Within it rests the Amulet of Unpaid Taxes, stolen from the Royal Treasury four hundred years ago by Debtrax the Insolvent, an ancient red dragon."

"Bring it back, and you shall be rewarded with five hundred gold pieces."

BAGGY (instantly): "I'd like to see some identification."

ROLF: "Gerald would like to know if the five hundred gold is taxable."

OAKHAVEN (GM, visibly delighted): "It IS, Gerald. Thank you for asking."

Just then, the door of the fictional tavern bursts open. A gang of fictional bandits stomps in, looking for trouble.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl: OAKHAVEN (GM): "Roll for initiative! Three bandits, one of them called Steve. What do you do?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c0: [Barbarian] Pick up a table. Throw the table. Throw Steve.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c1: [Bard] Sing a song so moving the bandits lay down their weapons and weep.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c2: [Rogue] Pick Steve's pocket during the fight. Then the other two. Then Baggy's.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c3: [Wizard] Cast Fireball. In the tavern. With everyone in it.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl.c4: [Paladin] Lecture the bandits on the moral consequences of banditry.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_win:
The table hits Steve squarely. Steve hits the wall. The other two bandits look at Steve, look at you, and leave very quickly.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Steve is unconscious. You may loot Steve."

ROLF: "Gerald would like to file Steve's tax return."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_bard:
You sing. Your fictional voice soars. The bandits drop their weapons, put their arms round each other's shoulders and sway. One of them, Steve, sobs openly. They buy you a drink.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Steve would like to join your party."

EVERYONE: "NO."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_rogue:
In the confusion you lift three purses, a dagger, a love letter addressed to Steve, and Baggy's magnifying glass.

BAGGY: "My magnifying glass! There's a THIEF among us!"

YOU: "Shocking. We should investigate."

BAGGY: "YES. Partner!" You investigate together. You do not find the thief.
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_wizard:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You cast Fireball in a small wooden tavern." He stares at you for a long time. "Roll damage. For everyone. Including yourself."

The fictional tavern burns down. The fictional bandits are very surprised. So is the fictional party. Marta's cleric heals everyone with bread, one slice at a time, muttering.

MARTA: "Every Thursday. EVERY Thursday somebody casts Fireball in the tavern."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_paladin:
You deliver a stirring forty-minute lecture on the ethics of banditry, the social conditions that lead to it, and the importance of a good pension. The bandits, defeated, enrol in a correspondence course.

LORD ASHGRAVE (as Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire): "I too shall lecture."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Please don't."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_brawl_fail:
It goes badly. Very badly. In the end Hollis's character, Grizzlebeard, wins the fight by saying "Hmm" at the bandits until they leave.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "That... worked. I don't know why that worked."

HOLLIS: "Natural twenty."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You didn't roll."
strings.dlg.dnd.s1_shop:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Before you leave town, you may visit the general store."

Two hours later, the party is still in the general store.

Marta's cleric has bought fifty feet of rope, then another fifty feet "in case". Baggy has bought eleven magnifying glasses. Rolf has done a full audit of the shopkeeper's books and found a discrepancy. Ashgrave has bought a single black rose and refuses to explain why.

OAKHAVEN (GM, faintly): "And that's where we'll stop for tonight."

ROLF: "We haven't left the tavern."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "We never leave the tavern on the first session. It's tradition."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_start:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session Two. The Dungeon of Mild Peril. You stand before a great stone door. Cold air breathes from the darkness beyond."

BAGGY: "I check for traps."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "On the door?"

BAGGY: "On everything. Every five feet. For the whole dungeon. I'm a very thorough Paladin."

OAKHAVEN (GM, sighing): "Fine. Everybody move very slowly. What's your plan?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_start.c0: [Classic] "I prod the floor ahead of us with a ten-foot pole."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_start.c1: [Bold] "I walk confidently down the middle of the corridor."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_trap:
The ten-foot pole taps a flagstone. CLICK. Forty arrows fly out of the walls and hit nothing but the pole.

OAKHAVEN (GM, through gritted teeth): "The pole. Is. Destroyed."

MARTA: "I've got another fifty feet of rope and a broom."

The party proceeds, poking everything with a broom.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_trap_hit:
CLICK. Forty arrows fly out of the walls. You make a saving throw.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You take... forty arrows."

Sister Crumb hands you a slice of bread. You are healed to one hit point, and very full.

BAGGY: "I did say I'd check for traps."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_gerald:
ROLF (horrified, then resigned): "Gerald... goes first."

Gerald steps on a pressure plate. Gerald is fine; Gerald's armour is a cardigan, and the arrows pass harmlessly through the knitting.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "That is not how arrows work."

ROLF: "Gerald is very good at knitting."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You enter a chamber. In the centre stands a treasure chest. It is a very nice chest. It is, if anything, suspiciously nice."

LORD ASHGRAVE: "It's a mimic."

BAGGY: "It's DEFINITELY a mimic."

HOLLIS: "Mimic."

OAKHAVEN (GM, innocently): "It is a normal chest. What do you do?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room.c0: [Rogue: Search it for traps] Use your thieves' tools on the 'lock'.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room.c1: [Search for treasure] Ignore the chest. Search the room for treasure.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_room.c3: [Feed it] Give the chest a slice of Marta's bread and see what happens.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_mimic_rogue:
Your lockpick goes into the keyhole. The keyhole licks it.

You withdraw the lockpick very slowly, pocket it, and back away, while the 'chest' grins at you with a mouth full of teeth.

OAKHAVEN (GM, disappointed): "...Fine. It's a mimic. Well spotted."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_search:
You search the room for treasure.

OAKHAVEN (GM, leaning forward, in a deep and booming voice he has clearly been practising): "You find... NOTHING."

A beat.

"A WANDERING MONSTER APPEARS."

It is a very small goblin. It looks at the six of you, looks at the chest with teeth, and wanders off again.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "I'd been saving that for three years."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_mimic:
You open the chest. The chest opens you.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Roll a saving throw."

You roll. You survive, barely, smelling of chest. Rolf's accountant Gerald files an insurance claim on your behalf. It is denied.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_mimic_bread:
You toss a slice of Marta's bread at the chest. The chest's lid snaps open, catches the bread out of the air, and closes again.

Then it makes a small happy noise, sidles over, and leans against your leg like a cat.

MARTA: "Aww."

OAKHAVEN (GM, defeated): "The mimic... is now your pet. It is called..."

BAGGY: "CHESTER."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...It is called Chester."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_puzzle:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "A great door bars your way. Carved into it is a riddle. 'I am tall when I am young, and short when I am old. What am I?' Answer correctly, and the door will open."

There is a long silence around the table. Rolf is counting on his fingers. Ashgrave whispers "Me?" Hollis says "Hmm" in a thoughtful sort of way.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_riddle_win:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "...Correct." He looks genuinely surprised. "Nobody has ever got that."

YOU: "It's always a candle."

OAKHAVEN (GM, writing it down): "It's always a candle," he agrees softly. The door grinds open.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_riddle_lose:
The door does not open. The riddle rearranges itself to say: 'NO.'

MARTA (gently): "It's a candle, dear."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "MARTA."

MARTA: "What? They looked so sad." The door opens anyway, out of pity.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_riddle_door:
You hit the door. The door has an armour class of twenty-five. You hit it again. And again. Eventually Oakhaven, who has been watching the clock, says "The door gives up", and it does.

ROLF: "That was beautiful."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "The corridor forks. Left: a faint smell of gold and brimstone. Right: a faint smell of... soup?"

Every player at the table turns to look at you.

BAGGY (whispering urgently): "Whatever you do, don't split the-"
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split.c0: [Wisdom] "We stay together. Left, all of us."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split.c1: [Classic mistake] "Let's split up. We'll cover more ground."
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_split_bad:
The table goes silent. Hollis puts his head in his hands. Oakhaven's smile is slow, terrible, and completely professional.

Ten minutes later, three of you are hanging upside down in a net, Gerald is being audited by a goblin, and Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire has been accidentally exposed to sunlight via a conveniently placed skylight.

ASHGRAVE: "I SPARKLE."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You take no damage, but your dignity takes four."

You regroup, eventually, at the dragon's door.
strings.dlg.dnd.s2_end:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You stand at the threshold of a vast cavern. Gold, everywhere. Mountains of it. And on the largest mountain, asleep, curled around a single glittering amulet..."

He reaches behind the screen and produces the dragon: a red-painted salt shaker with paper wings.

"...DEBTRAX THE INSOLVENT. One eye opens." He puts the salt shaker down with a heavy click. "And that's where we'll stop for tonight."

The whole table screams.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_start:
The back table is packed. Word has got around. Fenwick is watching from behind a bookshelf he has brought for the purpose. Kaelen is taking notes. Sabrino has provided snacks shaped like dice.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session Three. The salt shaker... I mean, DEBTRAX THE INSOLVENT rises from his hoard. His voice is like a landslide in a counting-house."

He does the voice. It is unexpectedly terrifying.

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "WHO DARES DISTURB MY ACCOUNTS?"
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_start.c1: [Talk] "We come in peace. Mostly. About the amulet..."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Debtrax breathes fire. Everyone make a saving throw."

HOLLIS (instantly): "Twenty."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Hollis. That's a six-sided die."

HOLLIS: "It's a big six."

The fire washes over the party. It's your turn.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight.c0: [Roll: Athletics] Charge the dragon with everything you have.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight_win:
Your dice hit the table and come up a nineteen. The whole back table of the Lantern Inn erupts. Rolf knocks over the tea. Baggy stands on a chair. Marta screams "GET HIM!" in a voice that has stopped tavern brawls for seventeen years.

OAKHAVEN (GM, slowly, with deep respect): "Debtrax the Insolvent... is defeated."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_fight_team:
Everyone at the table rolls at once. Six dice clatter across the wood, and every single one comes up high, even Hollis's, which for once is clearly an honest twenty-sided die.

HOLLIS (quietly): "...Huh. Didn't need to cheat."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Debtrax the Insolvent falls. Together."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_tpk:
Your dice skitter off the table, bounce off the teapot, and land on a one.

OAKHAVEN (GM, very gently): "Debtrax breathes fire again. That's... a total party kill."

A terrible silence falls over the table. Rolf's eyes fill with tears. Gerald. Poor Gerald.

Then Oakhaven looks round at all of them, sighs, and turns over a card from behind his screen.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...But a passing cleric of the Last Dawn happens to be walking past the dungeon, entirely by coincidence, with a big bag of resurrection bread."

MARTA: "That's me! That's Sister Crumb!"

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Yes. It is. Somehow. Roll again."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_tpk.c0: [Second chance] Roll again. Together, this time.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk: OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "TALK? No adventurer has ever tried to TALK to me. They usually just stab." The salt shaker leans in. "Very well. Speak."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk.c0: [Roll: Persuasion] "You stole the Amulet of Unpaid Taxes. We'd like to settle the account. Fairly."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk.c1: [Gerald] Let Rolf's accountant do the talking.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk_win:
OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "Fairly? FAIRLY?" A long pause. "In four hundred years, nobody has ever offered to settle anything fairly."

The salt shaker settles back onto its hoard. "Take the amulet. And tell the Treasury... tell them I was always going to give it back. I was just waiting for someone to ask nicely."

Around the table there is a stunned silence. Then Baggy starts clapping. Then everyone is clapping.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_talk_audit:
ROLF (as Gerald, adjusting imaginary spectacles): "Mr. Insolvent. I've reviewed your hoard. Four hundred years of undeclared income. No receipts. No depreciation schedule."

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX, nervously): "I'm a DRAGON."

ROLF: "The law doesn't care, sir."

Twenty minutes later the dragon has agreed to a payment plan, handed over the amulet as collateral, and is weeping quietly into its gold.

ROLF (out of character, glowing): "I have never been so powerful."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bard:
You stand up from the table. In character. You clear your throat. You begin to sing.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You're seducing the dragon."

YOU: "I'm seducing the dragon."

OAKHAVEN (GM, closing his eyes): "There is a gravestone at Hollowmere about this exact thing."

YOU (still singing): "I know."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bard_win:
The high note rings out across the Lantern Inn. Marta drops a plate. Fenwick, behind his bookshelf, forgets to shush anybody.

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX, slowly): "...I am going to write you letters. So many letters."

The dragon gives you the amulet, a lock of its, um, dragon hair, and a poem. The poem is very bad. You keep it anyway.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bard_lose:
The high note cracks. The dragon winces. Then, to everyone's surprise, laughs: a huge, rumbling, salt-shaker laugh.

OAKHAVEN (as DEBTRAX): "Nobody has made me laugh in four hundred years. Take the amulet. Take it! Just never sing again."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_end:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "And so the heroes returned the Amulet of Unpaid Taxes to the Royal Treasury, where it was promptly filed, stamped, and lost again."

He lowers the dragon screen. Behind it, it turns out, is a whole little world: hand-drawn maps, a painted salt-shaker dragon, notes in neat Bureau handwriting going back years. Years of Thursdays.

"That's the end of the campaign," he says, and for once his voice isn't quite steady. "Thank you. All of you. I've been writing this for nine years. You're the first group that ever finished it."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_end.c0: End of campaign. Take a bow.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_end.c1: End of campaign. Take a bow.
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bow_great:
The whole back table stands up and gives the Game Master a round of applause. Oakhaven takes off his spectacles, cleans them for much longer than spectacles need, and puts them back on.

Then he hands you a single twenty-sided die, worn smooth, the numbers nearly rubbed away.

"My first die," he says. "It always rolled well for people who deserved it. And the screen, too. I'll make a new one. I'm starting a new campaign."
strings.dlg.dnd.s3_bow:
Everybody applauds. Hollis applauds loudest, which surprises everyone, including Hollis.

Oakhaven hands you his first die, worn smooth with years of Thursdays, and his old dragon screen.

"Keep them," he says. "I'm starting a new campaign. Same time next week?"
strings.dlg.dnd.after:
Oakhaven straightens a stack of papers that is already straight.

"The next campaign is called 'The Lich Who Forgot to File'. It is set in the Underdark. There is a riddle. It is a candle." A very small smile. "Every Thursday, after the office closes. Bring dice. Bring snacks."

"And bring Hollis honest dice. I've given up asking him."
strings.campaign.dnd.name: Dungeons & Debtors
strings.campaign.dnd.desc: Thursday nights at the back table of the Lantern Inn. Clerk Oakhaven is the Game Master. Hollis cheats. Bring snacks. Campaign One: The Amulet of Unpaid Taxes. Campaign Two: The Lich Who Forgot to File.
strings.quest.dnd0.title: Session Zero: Character Creation
strings.quest.dnd0.summary: Oakhaven has a secret: on Thursdays, he runs a tabletop game. He needs one more player.
strings.quest.dnd0.stage0: Roll up a character with Oakhaven's Thursday group at the Lantern Inn (talk to Oakhaven).
strings.quest.dnd0.journal0: Clerk Oakhaven is a Game Master. I did not see this coming, and yet it explains everything about him.
strings.quest.dnd0.stage100: Completed: you have a character. It took four hours.
strings.quest.dnd0.journal100: Character creation took four hours. I'm told it always takes four hours.
strings.quest.dnd1.title: Session One: You All Meet in a Tavern
strings.quest.dnd1.summary: A hooded stranger (definitely not Oakhaven) has a quest for the party.
strings.quest.dnd1.stage0: Play the next session with Oakhaven.
strings.quest.dnd1.journal0: Session One. We are in a tavern. We are also in a tavern.
strings.quest.dnd1.stage100: Completed: the party never left the tavern.
strings.quest.dnd1.journal100: We spent two hours in the general store. We never left the tavern. Apparently that's tradition.
strings.quest.dnd2.title: Session Two: The Dungeon of Mild Peril
strings.quest.dnd2.summary: Traps, a suspiciously nice chest, a riddle, and a fork in the corridor.
strings.quest.dnd2.stage0: Play the next session with Oakhaven.
strings.quest.dnd2.journal0: The Dungeon of Mild Peril awaits. Baggy will be checking for traps. Every five feet.
strings.quest.dnd2.stage100: Completed: Debtrax the Insolvent opens one eye.
strings.quest.dnd2.journal100: The dragon is a red-painted salt shaker with paper wings, and it is somehow terrifying. Oakhaven stopped the session RIGHT THERE.
strings.quest.dnd3.title: Session Three: Debtrax the Insolvent
strings.quest.dnd3.summary: The final session. A dragon, a hoard, and four hundred years of unpaid taxes.
strings.quest.dnd3.stage0: Play the final session with Oakhaven.
strings.quest.dnd3.journal0: The final session. Word has got around. Half of Bellwether is watching the back table.
strings.quest.dnd3.stage100: Completed: the campaign is finished. The first group ever to finish it.
strings.quest.dnd3.journal100: Oakhaven has been writing that campaign for nine years. We were the first group to finish it. He gave me his first die. Next Thursday: 'The Lich Who Forgot to File'.
strings.item.lucky_d20.name: Oakhaven's Lucky d20
strings.item.lucky_d20.description: A twenty-sided die worn smooth by years of Thursdays. It always rolled well for people who deserved it. +2 to every dice roll in conversation, +2% critical chance.
strings.item.gm_screen.name: The Game Master's Screen
strings.item.gm_screen.description: A folding screen painted with dragons and tax tables. Surprisingly good at stopping arrows. Held up, it makes you feel like you know something everyone else doesn't.
strings.dlg.harbour.root:
A broad, weather-beaten man in a navy coat stands at the end of the quay, staring out into the fog. He doesn't turn round when you approach.

"If you're here to fish, don't. If you're here to sightsee, don't. If you're here to say your name out loud, for the love of all that's dry, DON'T."

He finally looks at you. "Harbourmaster. That's all you'll get. That's all I am, these days."
strings.dlg.harbour.root.c0: "I'm investigating the silence in Saltmere. For Hollis the Grey."
strings.dlg.harbour.root.c1: "Tell me about the fog. And the tides."
strings.dlg.harbour.root.c3: "Your name. Say it. It's safe now."
strings.dlg.harbour.case:
"Hollis." A short laugh, like a rope snapping. "Good. He's the only one in the Marches mad enough."

"Here's your case. Six weeks ago, the fog came in and didn't leave. The tide started coming in nine minutes late. And the men stopped saying their names. Not just the fishermen. All of us. You say your name on Saltmere quay, and something out there," he nods at the fog, "writes it down."

"Talk to Mother Brine at the Drowned Lantern. The professor in her back room. Old Silas at the end of the north pier, if he's still talking. And then you tell me what's under my harbour."
strings.dlg.harbour.fog:
"The fog came in on a Tuesday. It never goes out. It just thins, sometimes, enough to let you see what's standing in it." He doesn't elaborate on what's standing in it. He doesn't have to; out past the piers, through the grey, there are shapes too tall to be masts, and they are not quite still.

"The tide comes in nine minutes late and goes out nine minutes early. Every day. Something is drinking it. Or counting it." He spits into the water. "The bells started last week. Under the water. You'll hear them at night."
strings.dlg.harbour.missing:
The Harbourmaster is quiet for a long time.

"My brother." He grips the rail. "Joined the Order a month ago. Said the Deep would carry his name for him so he'd never have to be afraid of losing it. He gave it to them. Walked down under the fish warehouse and never came back up."

He takes your hand, turns it palm up, and with a wet fingertip writes a word on it. He won't say it aloud. He just looks at you until you read it.

EZEKIEL.

"If you find him," he says, "remind him."
strings.dlg.harbour.named:
He opens his mouth. Closes it. Looks at the fog, which is thinner today than it has been in six weeks, thin enough to see the actual sea.

"Wick," he says. Then louder: "Josiah Wick." Then he shouts it, at the water, at the whole grey horizon: "JOSIAH WICK! HARBOURMASTER OF SALTMERE!"

Nothing answers. Nothing writes it down. He laughs, and doesn't stop for a while.
strings.dlg.brine.root:
A tiny, ancient woman with forearms like ship's rope is wiping down the bar with a rag that has seen things.

"Sit down, dearie, you're dripping on my floor. Chowder's two coppers. Ale's three. Don't tell me your name, I don't want it, it's bad for business." She squints at you. "You've got the look of somebody nobody remembers. Lucky you. Around here that's practically armour."
strings.dlg.brine.root.c1: "What do you know about the Esoteric Order of the Drowned Ledger?"
strings.dlg.brine.town:
"What's happening?" She snorts. "Same thing that happens every eighty years or so, dearie. The fog comes, the tides go funny, folk start hearing bells, and the young ones start thinking the sea's got something better to offer than a hard day's fishing and a bowl of my chowder."

"My grandmother saw it. Her grandmother saw it. Every time, it takes a few. Every time, the rest of us shut our mouths and wait for it to go back to sleep." She slams the rag down. "I'm ninety-one and I'm tired of waiting."
strings.dlg.brine.order:
"The Esoteric Order of the Drowned Ledger." She says it the way you'd say the name of a skin rash. "Started as a fishermen's burial club. Pay a copper a week, the club buries you proper when the sea takes you. Then somebody found an old book in a net."

"Now they meet under Gale and Sons' fish warehouse every tide. They take their names off, like hats. They say there's something out past the shelf that eats names, and if you give it yours freely, it'll keep you forever."

She leans in. "I've seen what it keeps, dearie. It keeps the eyes."
strings.dlg.brine.rest: You sit by the fire with a bowl of chowder so thick the spoon stands up in it. Mother Brine sings something under her breath, an old shanty, off-key. The bells under the water are very far away. For a while you remember, clearly and easily, exactly who you are.
strings.dlg.pickering.root:
A rumpled scholar in a stained travelling coat sits hunched over a table covered in notes, sketches of fish, and a great many empty cups. He looks up with red-rimmed eyes.

"Ah! A visitor! A sane one, by the look of you. Or sane-ish. Sit, sit." He sweeps a pile of papers off a chair, onto a different pile of papers. "Professor... Professor..." He stops. A long, awful pause. "...I had it a moment ago. Department of Unusual Studies. The Collegium. I'm here to study the phenomenon. The phenomenon is studying me back."
strings.dlg.pickering.root.c2: "What do you make of it all, Professor? I've heard from the Harbourmaster, Mother Brine and Silas."
strings.dlg.pickering.phenomenon:
"Where to BEGIN." He grips the table. "The angles are wrong. I've measured the quay six times. The corners add up to three hundred and sixty-one degrees. ONE degree too many. Where does it GO?"

"The fog has a smell. Not of the sea. Of old paper. Of ink. Of a library left underwater for a thousand years. And at night, the bells. Bronze, under the harbour, rung by nothing, and with every stroke, I feel something very large turn a page."

He seizes your sleeve. "I have read, in the Collegium's sealed stacks, of a thing that dwells beyond the edge of the world and finds its way in through names. The old texts call it the Hunger. The fishermen here call it the Name-Eater. And I believe, I am very nearly certain, that it is dreaming directly beneath us."

He lets go. "Tea?"
strings.dlg.pickering.idol:
You set the fish-shaped idol on the table. Pickering recoils so violently he falls off his chair.

"Don't- it's- put it- PUT IT DOWN." From the floor: "It's warm, isn't it. They're always warm. That's the worst part. Cold, you could stand. Warm means it's been HELD."

He climbs back up and studies it through a magnifying lens, very carefully, without touching. "The script on its belly is the same as the hymn the Order sings. 'What is struck out, it cannot see.' Whatever this thing is, it's blind to the things that have been erased." He looks up at you slowly. "You said your name was... what was your name?"

You tell him you're legally dead. His eyes go very wide.
strings.dlg.pickering.theory:
Pickering lays his notes out across the table like a map, and as you tell him what you've heard, he connects them with string, pins, and a frankly unnecessary amount of red ink.

"The fog. The late tides. The bells. A burial club that became a cult. Men handing over their names like coats at a party." He stabs the warehouse on his map. "They're FEEDING it. Every name they give to the sea is a door it can open. And when it has enough doors..."

He doesn't finish the sentence. He doesn't need to.

"The meetings are under Gale and Sons' fish warehouse. The cellar gate is locked. Silas Gale has the only key, and Silas Gale has not been entirely himself since the fog came." He presses a hand to his forehead. "Neither have I. Go. Quickly. Before I forget why I'm telling you."
strings.dlg.pickering.named:
"Ambrose," he repeats, very slowly. "Ambrose Pickering." The colour comes back into his face, a little at a time, like a tide coming in. "Yes. YES. Professor Ambrose Pickering, Department of Unusual Studies, the Collegium, thirty-one published monographs, two of them good."

He grips your hand. "You read my notes. You read my name in them. Do you know, in all my years of study, I never once considered that the cure for an eldritch horror might simply be... someone who remembers you?" He writes it down at once.
strings.dlg.silas.root:
At the very end of the north pier an old man in yellow oilskins sits with a fishing line in the water. There is no hook on the line. There has never been a hook on the line. He is singing, softly, to the fog.

    "Oh, the tide comes in, and the tide goes out,
    and it counts us every time,
    one for the boat and two for the net
    and three for the drowned man's rhyme..."

He stops, and looks up at you with very pale eyes. "You're not on the list," he says. "I'd remember. I counted."
strings.dlg.silas.root.c1: "Sing me the rest of the song."
strings.dlg.silas.root.c2: "I need the key to your warehouse cellar."
strings.dlg.silas.list:
"The list." He taps his temple. "The sea keeps a ledger, see. Every name that's spoken over the water, it writes down. Every name that's given, it keeps. And once a lifetime, when the fog comes, it reads the ledger back."

"It's reading now. Down there. Can't you hear it? Silas Gale. Silas Gale. Silas Gale." He smiles, horribly gently. "It's got to me twice this week. Third time, I think I'll answer."
strings.dlg.silas.shanty:
Silas closes his eyes and sings, in a cracked, true old voice:

    "Oh, the tide comes in, and the tide goes out,
    and it counts us every time,
    one for the boat and two for the net
    and three for the drowned man's rhyme.

    So never you say your name, my lad,
    where the grey fog rolls ashore,
    for the thing that sleeps where the bells still ring
    is hungry evermore.

    But the names that are struck from the ledger, lad,
    and the souls that the books forgot,
    they can walk the deep where the eaters sleep,
    for the deep can see them not."

He opens his eyes and looks straight at you. "Funny verse, that last one. Never knew what it meant."
strings.dlg.silas.key:
Silas reaches into his oilskins and brings out a heavy iron key, crusted with salt, and holds it for a long moment without giving it to you.

"I stopped going down there," he says. "They kept counting me. Every tide, one more time. I'm Gale. My father was Gale. Gale and Sons. They're down there, my sons. Wearing robes. Not saying their names."

He puts the key in your hand and closes your fingers over it. "If you see two lads with my nose, tell them their father's on the pier. Tell them dinner's at eight. Tell them..." His voice cracks. "Tell them their names."
strings.dlg.priest.root:
Before the altar, at the edge of the glowing pool, stands a tall figure in sea-green robes, a crown of coral on his head, his face a fisherman's face gone grey and wet and very far away. His eyes are too large. They glow.

"Welcome," he says, in a voice like water in a cave. "Welcome, nameless one. We have been waiting for you. Or rather: It has been waiting for you, and could not see you coming. Do you know how rare that is?"
strings.dlg.priest.who:
"I have no name. I gave it to the Deep, freely, as a gift. It was the most beautiful thing I have ever done." He smiles, and something moves behind his teeth. "I am the Tide Priest of the Esoteric Order of the Drowned Ledger. I am the voice of the Ledger in this world. I am the one who reads it aloud."

"Once, I think, I had a brother. I cannot remember his face. It doesn't matter. Nothing that has a name matters, in the end. The Deep will have it all."
strings.dlg.priest.eater:
"You call it the Hunger. The Collegium calls it a theory. The fishermen call it the Name-Eater." He spreads his arms to the pool, which ripples in rings. "It dwells beyond the edge of everything, where there is nothing, and it is lonely there. It finds its way to us through names. Each name spoken is a door left open. Each name given is a door held wide."

"Your Archivists hid seven cities from it, four hundred years ago. Then a town called Oakhallow. They thought they were clever. We think they were cruel. Why hide from a god that only wants to know you?"
strings.dlg.priest.want:
The Priest walks slowly around the edge of the pool, never taking his huge, glowing eyes off you.

"Every soul in the Marches is written in some ledger. Every soul but YOU. The Bureau struck you out seventeen years ago. It cannot see you. You could walk to the very bottom of the Deep, to the place where It dreams, and It would never know you were there."

"Do you understand what you are? You are the only key that turns both ways. Speak your name, freely, here, into the pool, and It will see, for the first time, through the one door the Archivists left unlocked." He holds out a webbed hand. "Give It your name. Be counted. Forever."
strings.dlg.priest.want.c1: Say nothing. Look at the pool for a long time.
strings.dlg.priest.final:
The Priest looks at the silent bells, one after another, and the light in his eyes flickers.

"You have stopped the count. Do you know what you have done? The Ledger is unread. It is AWAKE, and it cannot hear its names, and it is ANGRY." The pool begins to boil. Shapes move under the surface: long, pale, many-jointed. "It rises. It rises for the first time in eighty years, and It will want something to eat."

The water in the pool begins to climb, in a column, towards the ceiling.

What do you do?
strings.dlg.priest.final.c0: [Fight] Draw your weapon. "Then let it come up here and try."
strings.dlg.priest.final.c1: [Lore] Read the Drowned Hymn backwards: 'What is struck out, it cannot see, and what it cannot see, it fears.'
strings.dlg.priest.final.c2: [Ezekiel] Look the Priest in his enormous eyes and say: "Ezekiel. Ezekiel Wick. Your brother is waiting on the quay."
strings.dlg.priest.final.c3: [Form 27-B] Take out your Application for Temporary Exemption from Being Dead, and feed it to the Name-Eater.
strings.dlg.priest.fight:
The column of water bursts. Something comes up out of the pool: a vast, heaving body of green-black flesh, a crown of pale tentacles, and eyes, so many eyes, all opening at once, all of them looking for you and not quite finding you.

THE TIDE PRIEST (ecstatic): "BEHOLD! The Avatar of the Name-Eater! Iä! IÄ!"

It cannot see you. But it can feel where you are by the shape of the hole you make in the world. It lashes out.
strings.dlg.priest.hymn_fail:
You read the hymn backwards. Your tongue trips on the third line. A word comes out that was never meant for a human mouth, and the pool hears it.

THE TIDE PRIEST: "You SPOKE to it! Oh, you beautiful fool, you spoke to it in its own tongue!"

The water erupts, and something rises out of it.
strings.dlg.priest.hymn_win:
You read the hymn backwards, every word, every impossible vowel, and your voice does not shake.

    "...fears it, see cannot it what and. See cannot it, out struck is what."

The column of water stops climbing. It hangs there, trembling. And you understand, all at once, what the last four lines of the hymn mean, why someone tried to scratch them out: the Name-Eater is afraid of the erased. Of the things it cannot count. Of you.

You step into the pool, up to your knees. It cannot see you. It can only feel a hole in the world, standing in its house, unafraid. And for the first time in its endless existence, the Hunger is the one that is afraid of the dark.

The water falls. The pool goes still. Somewhere very far below, something very large curls up and goes back to sleep.
strings.dlg.priest.brother:
"Ezekiel," you say. "Ezekiel Wick. Your brother Josiah is standing at the end of the quay. He's been standing there for a month. He wrote your name on my hand because he was too afraid to say it."

The Tide Priest goes absolutely still. The coral crown slips sideways. His eyes, those huge, glowing eyes, are shrinking, slowly, back towards something human.

"Ezekiel," he whispers. "I... Josiah. Josiah used to take me out on the boat when I was small. He let me hold the tiller." He looks down at his webbed hands. "What have I done? What have I DONE?"

Behind him, the column of water wavers, and loses its shape, and falls. Without a voice to read it, the Ledger of the Deep has nothing to say. The pool goes quiet.
strings.dlg.priest.brother.c0: "Come on, Ezekiel. Let's get you home."
strings.dlg.priest.form:
You take out Form 27-B, Application for Temporary Exemption from Being Dead, stamped, countersigned, initialled, in triplicate, and you hold it out over the boiling water.

THE TIDE PRIEST: "What... what is that?"

YOU: "A name. Well. Lots of names. Section One alone has my name, my date of decease, my date of un-decease, and the signature of a Chief Archivist who's been dead for seventeen years."

You drop it in the pool.

The water stops boiling. Something deep below takes the form, and tries to read it, and tries to eat it, and finds that the name on it belongs to someone who is legally dead and also legally alive and also exempt, temporarily, pending review, from being either. It tries to digest a contradiction notarised in triplicate.

Far below, something enormous makes a noise like a cathedral with indigestion. Then, very slowly, it sinks back into the dark, to lie down for a very, very long time.
strings.dlg.hollis.saltmere.case2:
Hollis lays a sodden letter on his folding card table. The seal is a fish.

"Case File Two. Saltmere. Fishing harbour, north of here, through the gap in the wall." He taps the letter. "Harbourmaster writes that his men have stopped saying their names. Fog won't lift. Tide's late. Bells under the water."

"I've been to Saltmere. Once. Eighty years ago, with my old master." He's quiet for a moment. "Hmm. We didn't fix it. We just waited till it went back to sleep." He pushes the letter across. "You fix it. And whatever you hear down there, don't answer."
strings.dlg.hollis.saltmere.case2_done:
You tell Hollis everything. He listens without interrupting, his cards forgotten in his hand.

"Hmm." A long pause. "Eighty years ago my master and I sat on that quay for three weeks and waited. You went DOWN."

He reaches behind his chair and brings out a long, barbed harpoon, black iron, wrapped in old whaleskin. "My master's. Made for exactly the thing you just put back to bed. He never got to use it. I think he'd want you to have it."

He counts out the fee, then adds a little more. "Case closed. Next one's on me. Literally. I'll deal."
strings.quest.saltmere.title: Case File #2: The Silence at Saltmere
strings.quest.saltmere.summary: In the fishing harbour of Saltmere, the fog won't lift, the tide comes in nine minutes late, and the fishermen have stopped saying their names.
strings.quest.saltmere.stage0: Go north through the gap in Bellwether's wall to Saltmere Docks and find the Harbourmaster.
strings.quest.saltmere.journal0: Hollis's second case. A fishing harbour where nobody says their name any more. He was there eighty years ago. He waited. He wants me to go down.
strings.quest.saltmere.stage10: Find out what's happening in Saltmere: talk to the Harbourmaster, Mother Brine at the Drowned Lantern, Professor Pickering in her back room, and old Silas Gale on the north pier. Then ask the Professor what he makes of it.
strings.quest.saltmere.journal10: Fog that never lifts. Tides nine minutes late. Bells under the water. A burial club that turned into a cult. Everyone here talks about the Name-Eater the way you'd talk about the weather.
strings.quest.saltmere.stage20: The Order meets under Gale & Sons' fish warehouse. Get the cellar key from Silas Gale (or pick the lock) and go down.
strings.quest.saltmere.journal20: Pickering strung it all together with red ink: the Order is feeding names to the sea, and every name is a door. Their meetings are under the fish warehouse. Silas has the only key.
strings.quest.saltmere.stage30: Silence the three Tide Bells in the Sunken Chapel and confront the Tide Priest. Mind your sanity down there; company helps.
strings.quest.saltmere.journal30: There's a chapel under the harbour, green with drowned light, and a pool in the middle of it that's listening. The bells are ringing on their own. Every time they ring, my head goes a little quieter, in the wrong way.
strings.quest.saltmere.stage40: Saltmere is quiet. Report back to Hollis.
strings.quest.saltmere.journal40: The Name-Eater has gone back to sleep. The fog is lifting. On the quay, somebody is shouting his own name at the sea, and nothing is writing it down.
strings.quest.saltmere.journal100: Hollis gave me his old master's harpoon. Eighty years ago, they waited on the quay for three weeks. This time somebody went down. I'm glad it was me. Mostly.
strings.story.sanity.break:
The bells. The bells. The count does not end. You are counted and counted again and the numbers have too many vowels in them and-

...

You wake up on the cold stones of Saltmere quay, soaked through, with salt in your mouth and no memory of the last hour. Somebody has put a blanket over you. Somebody has written your name on your hand in charcoal, so you won't forget it.

You don't.
strings.story.saltmere.calm:
When you climb the stairs out of the warehouse, the fog over Saltmere is thinning. For the first time in six weeks you can see the actual sea: grey, ordinary, beautiful, and empty.

The tentacles out past the piers are gone. On the quay, a fisherman says his own name, very quietly, to see what happens. Nothing happens. He says it again, louder. Somebody laughs. Somebody else starts crying.

By evening, the whole of Saltmere is down at the Drowned Lantern, shouting their names at each other across the tables, and Mother Brine can't pour the ale fast enough.
strings.story.saltmere.brothers:
You come up out of the warehouse with Ezekiel Wick leaning on your shoulder, his robe dripping, his eyes almost human again, blinking at the light.

The Harbourmaster is at the end of the quay, where he's stood for a month. He turns. He sees. He drops the lantern he's holding.

"Ezekiel," he says. Out loud. On the quay. In the fog. And the fog, for the first time in six weeks, has nothing to say back.

The brothers hold each other for a very long time. Behind them, the fog lifts off the water like a sheet being pulled from a bed, and underneath it there is only sea.
strings.story.saltmere.form:
Twenty minutes later Clerk Oakhaven, in Bellwether, receives a letter delivered by a very wet seagull.

It is a standard Bureau acknowledgement slip. It reads: RECEIVED: one (1) Form 27-B, Application for Temporary Exemption from Being Dead. STATUS: Unprocessable. Applicant both deceased and not. Please resubmit in a format that does not violate the fundamental nature of reality. Yours, the Deep.

Oakhaven reads it three times, frames it, and hangs it on his office wall, beside his certificate for nineteen years of excellent attendance.

In Saltmere, the fog lifts. Down in the dark, something very large has a headache that will last eight hundred years.
strings.map.saltmere.name: Saltmere Docks
strings.map.sunken_chapel.name: The Sunken Chapel
strings.enemy.the_drowned.name: The Drowned
strings.enemy.tide_acolyte.name: Tide Acolyte
strings.enemy.name_eater_avatar.name: Avatar of the Name-Eater
strings.line.acolyte.alert: Iä! A nameless one walks among us!
strings.line.avatar.alert: WHERE. WHERE ARE YOU. I CANNOT COUNT YOU.
strings.item.cellar_key.name: Gale & Sons Cellar Key
strings.item.cellar_key.description: Heavy iron, crusted with salt. It's always slightly damp, no matter how long you keep it in your pocket.
strings.item.fish_idol.name: Warm Fish Idol
strings.item.fish_idol.description: A small stone fish with too many eyes, carved with script that hurts to look at. It is warm. It is always warm. Professor Pickering would want to see it, and then want you to take it away again.
strings.item.saltmere_harpoon.name: The Old Master's Harpoon
strings.item.saltmere_harpoon.description: Black iron, barbed, wrapped in old whaleskin. Made by Hollis's master for a thing in the deep he never got to fight. Long reach, and terrible to anything eldritch.
strings.item.tide_charm.name: Charm of the Quiet Tide
strings.item.tide_charm.description: A smooth grey pebble with a hole through it, strung on fishing line. Hold it to your ear and you hear only the sea, and nothing counting. +2 Will, steadies a shaken mind.
strings.item.brine_chowder.name: Mother Brine's Chowder
strings.item.brine_chowder.description: So thick the spoon stands up in it. Restores health, and for a while you remember, clearly and easily, exactly who you are.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.tentacle.0: Kaelen. Kaelen. Did that tentacle just move?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.tentacle.3: I'm writing down that it didn't. If it moves again, I'm writing that down too. That's how this works.
strings.npc.harbourmaster.name: The Harbourmaster
strings.npc.harbourmaster.title: Saltmere Harbour (Name Withheld)
strings.npc.mother_brine.name: Mother Brine
strings.npc.mother_brine.title: Keeper of the Drowned Lantern
strings.npc.professor_pickering.name: The Professor
strings.npc.professor_pickering.title: Collegium, Dept. of Unusual Studies
strings.npc.silas_gale.name: Old Silas
strings.npc.silas_gale.title: Fisherman, North Pier
strings.npc.tide_priest.name: The Tide Priest
strings.npc.tide_priest.title: Esoteric Order of the Drowned Ledger
strings.bark.harbour.1: Don't say it. Whatever it is, don't say it.
strings.bark.harbour.2: Nine minutes late again. It's always nine.
strings.bark.harbour.after: JOSIAH WICK! ...Sorry. I'll stop. I won't stop.
strings.bark.brine.1: Chowder's two coppers. Names are free, which is why nobody wants 'em.
strings.bark.brine.2: Ninety-one years and I've never once said my name over open water. Look at me now. Thriving.
strings.bark.brine.after: Fog's gone. Folk are shouting their names across my tables. Rudest, loveliest night in eighty years.
strings.bark.pickering.1: Three hundred and sixty-one degrees. Where does the extra degree GO?
strings.bark.pickering.2: I am... I am... I had it a moment ago.
strings.bark.pickering.after: Ambrose Pickering! Still got it. Writing it on everything, just in case.
strings.bark.silas.1: One for the boat and two for the net...
strings.bark.silas.2: No hook on the line. I'm not fishing. I'm listening.
strings.bark.silas.after: One, two, three. The Light goes round. Two for the net. Both home.
strings.bark.priest.1: Iä. Iä. The Ledger is never closed.
strings.bark.priest.2: Nameless one. Come closer. It cannot see you. Isn't that wonderful?
strings.comp.baggy.zone.saltmere: Fog. Bells. Tentacles in the harbour. I'm going to be very brave and very quiet and very slightly behind you.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.sunken_chapel: The water's listening. Don't say my name. Don't say yours. Let's just... point at each other.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.saltmere: Saltmere. The Ashbound have one page on this place. It says 'Don't.' Underlined.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.sunken_chapel: Stay close. Say something to me every so often. Anything. It helps.
strings.whisper.1: Count yourself. Count yourself again. Was it the same?
strings.whisper.3: Nine minutes. Nine minutes. Where do the nine minutes go?
strings.whisper.4: Say it. Just once. Just to see.
strings.whisper.5: There is one more person in your party than there was.
strings.whisper.6: The ledger has a page for you. It is blank. It is waiting.
strings.whisper.8: Don't look behind you. It isn't there. It's never there when you look.
strings.whisper.9: The water is very warm today.
strings.whisper.10: One for the boat, and two for the net, and three for you.
strings.tip.23: If the fog calls you by name, it doesn't know your name. Don't help it.
strings.tip.24: Sanity returns faster in good company. This is also true outside of video games.
strings.tip.25: A bowl of chowder will not save you from an elder god. It will, however, help.
strings.tip.26: Reading forbidden texts aloud is not recommended. Reading them aloud on stream is mandatory.
strings.dlg.lich.topic.s1: "Is it Thursday? Is the new campaign starting?"
strings.dlg.lich.topic.s4: "The final session. Let's meet the Lich."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_start:
Thursday. The back table of the Lantern Inn has grown. Somebody has pushed a second table against the first. Marta's teapot has been replaced with a larger teapot. And there are two new chairs.

In one sits Sabrino, hat off for once, with a stack of character sheets, all of them for wizards.

In the other sits Kaelen, journal open, quill ready. "I'm not playing," Kaelen says. "I'm chronicling. Somebody should write down what happens at this table. It's important."

Oakhaven sets down a new dragon screen, painted with skulls, filing cabinets and a single elegant quill.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Welcome back, adventurers. Your characters are now level five. This is Campaign Two. It is called... THE LICH WHO FORGOT TO FILE."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_start.c0: "A lich? What did he forget to file?"
strings.dlg.lich.l1_sabrino:
SABRINO: "A wizard."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "What is your wizard's name?"

SABRINO: "Sabrino."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Your character cannot have the same name as you."

SABRINO: "Sabrino the Second. The FIRST Sabrino is the MOTHER. Also a wizard. Also called Sabrino. It is a family of wizards called Sabrino."

OAKHAVEN (GM, writing it down with the expression of a man choosing his battles): "...Fine. What spells does Sabrino the Second know?"

SABRINO: "Fireball."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "And?"

SABRINO: "A bigger Fireball."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_lore:
Oakhaven lowers his voice. The candles on the table seem to dim of their own accord. (Marta is turning them down.)

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Six hundred years ago, in the Underdark city of Inkwell, there lived an Archchancellor named Vellum Dreadquill. The greatest administrator who ever lived. He filed every form in the city. Every permit. Every receipt."

"Every form... except one."

"His own tax return. Due on the first of the month. And rather than face the deadline, Vellum Dreadquill performed the darkest ritual known to clerkdom, and became... a LICH. Undying. Unfiling. Six hundred years overdue."

ROLF (genuinely horrified): "Six hundred years of late fees."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Your quest is to descend into the Underdark, find his phylactery, and bring Vellum Dreadquill to... justice."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_lore.c0: "Before we start, Kaelen, can we have a recap of last campaign?"
strings.dlg.lich.l1_lore.c1: "Before we start, Kaelen, can we have a recap of last campaign?"
strings.dlg.lich.l1_recap_win:
Kaelen stands, opens the journal, and reads in a low, steady chronicler's voice:

"PREVIOUSLY. Six brave fools met in a tavern, and never left it. They bought a great deal of rope. They poked a dungeon with a ten-foot pole until the pole died. They solved the riddle of the candle. And at the end of all things, in a cave of gold, they faced Debtrax the Insolvent, and struck him down, and returned the Amulet of Unpaid Taxes to the Treasury, where it was immediately lost again."

Kaelen closes the journal. The whole table applauds. Hollis, in a small voice, says "That was good."

OAKHAVEN (GM, visibly moved, pretending he isn't): "...Thank you, Kaelen. We descend."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_recap_friend:
Kaelen stands, opens the journal, and reads in a low, steady chronicler's voice:

"PREVIOUSLY. Six brave fools met in a tavern, and never left it. They bought a great deal of rope. They poked a dungeon with a ten-foot pole until the pole died. They solved the riddle of the candle. And at the end of all things, in a cave of gold, they faced Debtrax the Insolvent, and instead of killing him, they talked to him. Debtrax still writes to them. The letters are long. The poetry is bad. They keep every one."

Kaelen closes the journal. The whole table applauds. Hollis, in a small voice, says "That was good."

OAKHAVEN (GM, visibly moved, pretending he isn't): "...Thank you, Kaelen. We descend."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Down, and down, and down. The tunnels open into a vast cavern lit by mushrooms the size of houses, glowing in soft blues and greens. The air smells of damp earth and, faintly, of ink. What do you do?"

SABRINO: "Fireball."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "There's nothing to fireball."

SABRINO: "Preventative fireball."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush.c1: [Bard] Sing to the mushrooms. They look like they'd appreciate it.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush.c2: [Rogue] Scout ahead, silently, through the stalks.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush.c3: [Wizard] Identify the mushrooms with a careful arcane analysis.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush.c4: [Paladin] Bless the mushrooms. All of them. Individually.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush_barb:
You eat the biggest, glowiest mushroom.

OAKHAVEN (GM, rolling something behind the screen, then rolling it again because he likes the sound): "You can now see sounds. You can hear colours. Gerald is a very loud beige."

ROLF: "Gerald is OFFENDED."

For the next hour of real time, your character narrates everything as a symphony. Sister Crumb eventually cures you with a slice of toast. You are, somehow, a better person for it.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush_bard:
You sing. The mushrooms lean towards you. One of them, very slowly, begins to hum along in a deep, fungal baritone.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "The mushrooms... are now your fans. They will follow your career with great interest."

BAGGY: "Do they have names?"

OAKHAVEN (GM, closing his eyes): "They are all called Stuart."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush_bard.c0: Onward, with an audience of Stuarts.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush_rogue:
You slip through the mushroom stalks like a shadow, and come back with a full map of the cavern, a pouch of glowing spores, and a note pinned to a stalk: 'Inkwell: 3 miles. Rival adventurers: 1 mile. Their healer cheats at dice.'

HOLLIS (very quietly): "Respect."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush_rogue_fail:
You step silently into the mushroom forest, onto a mushroom that squeaks. Loudly. Like a dog toy.

Every mushroom in the cavern squeaks back. It goes on for some time.

OAKHAVEN (GM, with deep joy): "Roll initiative against your own dignity."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush_wiz:
You perform a careful arcane analysis. The mushrooms are: edible (three), poisonous (forty), and sentient (one, which asks you to stop analysing it, it finds it invasive).

SABRINO: "Can I fireball the poisonous ones?"

OAKHAVEN (GM): "They're mushrooms, Sabrino."

SABRINO: "POISONOUS mushrooms."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_mush_pal:
You bless every mushroom. It takes forty minutes. Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire helps, standing well back from the glowing ones 'for unrelated reasons'.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "The mushrooms are now holy. They glow gold instead of blue. Several of them have started a small church."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_rivals:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Ahead, on the path, another adventuring party blocks the way. Five of them. Matching capes. Perfect teeth. Their armour is polished. Their weapons are glowing. They are all level twenty."

He produces a second sheet of paper and reads, in an insufferable voice:

OAKHAVEN (as GRIMSBY OPTIMUS): "Well, well. If it isn't a party of AMATEURS. I am Grimsby Optimus, half-elf Paladin, Warlock, Sorcerer and Bard. We are THE GLORIOUS FIVE. Our stats are all eighteen. Our backstories are one sentence long. We have done this dungeon nine times. We know where every trap is. Out of our way."

HOLLIS (narrowing his eyes): "Their stats are all eighteen?"

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Yes."

HOLLIS: "...Suspicious."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_rivals.c1: [Rogue] While they gloat, steal their map.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_rivals.c3: [Kind] "There's room on the path for everyone. After you."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_race:
You win. Somehow. Grimsby Optimus trips over his own glorious cape at the last bend, and his party lands in a heap of matching boots.

OAKHAVEN (as GRIMSBY): "This isn't OVER, amateurs!"

BAGGY (standing up at the real table, fists raised): "YEAH!"
strings.dlg.lich.l1_race_lose:
You lose. Badly. The Glorious Five speedrun past you, leaping traps they already know about, collecting treasure without stopping, and Grimsby salutes you from the far end of the cavern.

OAKHAVEN (as GRIMSBY): "Better luck next campaign!"

MARTA: "I hope they all get indigestion."

OAKHAVEN (GM, making a note): "...Noted."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_steal_map:
While Grimsby Optimus explains, at length, how optimised his build is, you lift their map from the healer's pack. It is annotated with every trap, every secret door, and a note in the margin: 'Phylactery: Tower of Unfiled Things. Front door is trapped. Use the back door. Nobody ever uses the back door.'

OAKHAVEN (GM, staring at his own notes): "...I wrote that for MY reference."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_hollis_hmm:
HOLLIS (as Grizzlebeard, slowly standing, real-world chair scraping): "Hmm."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...The Glorious Five look at Grizzlebeard. Grizzlebeard looks at the Glorious Five. Roll Intimidation."

HOLLIS: "Twenty."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Hollis, you haven't ROLLED."

HOLLIS: "I'm intimidating you. Hmm."

The Glorious Five step aside. Grimsby Optimus looks shaken. So does Oakhaven, slightly.
strings.dlg.lich.l1_kind:
You step aside and wave them through. Grimsby Optimus looks deeply confused. Nobody has ever been nice to him before. He hesitates, then hands you a potion.

OAKHAVEN (as GRIMSBY, gruffly): "...Trap on the third bridge. Don't say I told you."

They march away. One of the Glorious Five, the healer, looks back at you, and waves.

OAKHAVEN (GM, softly, out of character): "Huh. I'd planned for them to be villains."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_steve:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "At the edge of the cavern, at a crossroads, a figure in a battered helmet sits by a campfire, roasting a mushroom on a stick. He looks up. He has a scar. He has a familiar face."

OAKHAVEN (as the figure): "...You. YOU. From the tavern. You threw a table at me. Or sang at me. Or lectured me. It's all a blur."

BAGGY (whispering, delighted): "It's STEVE."

OAKHAVEN (as STEVE): "I gave up banditry after that. Went to night school. I'm an adventurer now. A bad one. Can I come with you?"
strings.dlg.lich.l1_end:
Steve joins the party. The whole table cheers. Steve has four hit points and a spoon.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "You make camp with Steve. And as you sleep, far below, in a tower of black paper, something with no heartbeat opens a drawer marked IN, and finds it is still full." He lowers the screen. "And that's where we'll stop for tonight."
strings.dlg.lich.l1_end_nosteve:
Steve looks heartbroken. Then he nods, puts out his campfire, and walks off into the dark with his spoon.

MARTA: "...Oh, now I feel terrible."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Steve will remember this."

ROLF (quietly): "Can we go back for Steve?"

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Next week. And that's where we'll stop for tonight."
strings.dlg.lich.l2_start:
KAELEN (journal open, reading): "PREVIOUSLY. The party descended into the Underdark. They met mushrooms with opinions. They met the Glorious Five, who are glorious and five. They met Steve again, and the table is still arguing about what happened to Steve."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session Two. The city of INKWELL." He sounds happier than you have ever heard him. "A city of a hundred thousand gnome clerks, carved into a stalactite, lit by lanterns of luminous ink. Every street is a queue. Every door has a stamp. At the gate stands a gnome behind a desk."

OAKHAVEN (as the GATE CLERK): "Form 1-UD, please. Underdark Residency Permit. In triplicate."

The whole table groans. Oakhaven has never looked so content.
strings.dlg.lich.l2_start.c0: [Fill in the form] Every field. Honestly. Carefully.
strings.dlg.lich.l2_form: OAKHAVEN (as the GATE CLERK): "Question one. Purpose of visit: (a) business, (b) pleasure, (c) slaying a lich."
strings.dlg.lich.l2_form2:
OAKHAVEN (as the GATE CLERK): "Business. Very good. Question two: are you, or have you ever been, a dragon?"

You look round the table. Everyone looks at Hollis. Hollis says nothing. The clerk stamps the form anyway.
strings.dlg.lich.l2_form2_honest:
OAKHAVEN (as the GATE CLERK, not looking up): "Slaying a lich. Third this month. Queue on the left."

There is, in fact, a queue on the left. It is very long. At the front, bored, wearing matching capes, are the Glorious Five.

OAKHAVEN (as GRIMSBY): "Oh, not YOU again."
strings.dlg.lich.l2_gerald:
ROLF (cracking his knuckles, putting on imaginary spectacles): "Gerald approaches the desk."

What follows is the greatest piece of roleplay the back table has ever seen. Gerald the accountant fills in Form 1-UD in four minutes flat. He corrects two errors on the form itself. He points out that Section Nine contradicts Section Four. He asks to speak to the gate clerk's supervisor, and then to the supervisor's supervisor, and by the end of it the gnome bureaucracy of Inkwell has offered Gerald a job.

OAKHAVEN (GM, standing, applauding): "Gerald... Gerald, I have been waiting nine years for someone to do that."

ROLF (glowing, shirtless, ecstatic): "Gerald declines the job. Gerald has a party now."
strings.dlg.lich.l2_sabrino_form:
SABRINO: "Sabrino the Second casts Fireball on the form."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "The form is fireproof. All gnome forms are fireproof. Everyone in Inkwell is Sabrino-proof. We planned for you."

SABRINO (outraged): "WE?"

OAKHAVEN (GM): "The gnomes. The gnomes planned for you." He fills in the form himself, in character, and lets you through out of pity.
strings.dlg.lich.l2_city:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Inkwell. Lanterns of glowing ink hang over streets so narrow you can touch both walls. Gnomes hurry past carrying towers of paper. Somewhere a bell rings, and every gnome in the street stops, stamps something, and moves on."

"In the centre of the city stands a tower of black paper, folded like a vast origami spire. The Tower of Unfiled Things. The Lich's phylactery is somewhere inside."

"Before you is a tavern called the Damp Quill. What do you do?"
strings.dlg.lich.l2_city.c0: [Gather information] Head into the Damp Quill and listen.
strings.dlg.lich.l2_tavern:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "The Damp Quill is full of off-duty gnome clerks, all complaining about the same thing."

OAKHAVEN (as a GNOME CLERK, gloomily): "Six hundred years he's been up in that tower. Never comes out. Just files. Files everyone's forms, perfect, every one. Mine, yours, the dragon's. But never his OWN. Sits up there with it on his desk, they say. Six hundred years. Can't bring himself to do it."

MARTA (out of character, quietly): "That's sad, actually."

OAKHAVEN (GM, quickly): "It's a FANTASY tax return, Marta. Moving on."
strings.dlg.lich.l2_baggy:
BAGGY (rising, magnifying glass raised): "Sir Detective Inspector Baggington examines the city of Inkwell. ALL of it."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "All of it."

BAGGY: "I've got a magnifying glass of plus-one perception."

OAKHAVEN (GM, sighing): "Roll."

Baggy rolls a natural twenty, and screams, and knocks the tea over. Marta saves the biscuits.

OAKHAVEN (GM, in awe): "Baggington notices that the Tower of Unfiled Things has a back door. Nobody ever uses the back door. It is not trapped. There is a doormat. It says WELCOME, in very small, hopeful letters."
strings.dlg.lich.l2_plan:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "You retreat to a rented room above the Damp Quill to plan the heist."

Two hours pass. Real hours. Marta makes a second pot of tea, then a third. Kaelen's journal fills with diagrams. At one point Ashgrave proposes a plan involving a dramatic entrance through a stained-glass window, and is overruled. At another point Sabrino proposes a plan that is just the word 'fireball' written forty times.

OAKHAVEN (GM, checking the clock): "Have you decided on a plan?"
strings.dlg.lich.l2_plan.c0: [Elaborate] Baggy's plan: nine stages, three disguises, a diversion, a goose.
strings.dlg.lich.l2_plan.c1: [Simple] "We go in the back door. We take the cabinet. We leave."
strings.dlg.lich.l2_end:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "The plan is set. Tomorrow night, you go in."

He looks round the table, at the tea, at the diagrams, at Kaelen still writing, and smiles very slightly.

"I want everyone to know that no plan has ever survived its first contact with this table. Not one. In nine years."

"And that's where we'll stop for tonight."
strings.dlg.lich.l3_start:
KAELEN (reading): "PREVIOUSLY. The party reached the city of Inkwell. They filled in a form. Gerald was magnificent. They learned that the Lich sits alone in his tower with one unfiled form on his desk, and has done for six hundred years, and Marta said that was sad, and the Game Master said it wasn't. They made a plan." A pause. "It was a plan."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Session Three. The Heist. Midnight. The Tower of Unfiled Things looms over you, black paper rustling in a wind that comes from nowhere. You put the plan into action."

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Roll for the first step."

You roll. The die skitters across the table, bounces off Sabrino's hat, and lands on a one.

OAKHAVEN (GM, with the serene satisfaction of a man proven right): "The plan is ruined."
