strings.dlg.lich.l3_ruined:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Already. Every part of it."

"The diversion goose escapes and joins the city guard. The disguises turn out to be the uniforms of a department that was closed in the year 412. Somebody, and I'm not saying who, Sabrino, has already set fire to the front door."

"Alarm bells are ringing all over the tower. Paper golems are unfolding from the walls. What do you do?"

Around the table, everyone looks at each other. And then, at once, everyone starts improvising.
strings.dlg.lich.l3_ruined.c0: [Rally the party] "Everyone! Do what you're good at!"
strings.dlg.lich.l3_moments:
It's chaos, and it's glorious.

Sister Crumb throws bread at the paper golems; it turns out paper golems love bread, and three of them sit down to eat. Lord Definitely-Not-A-Vampire stands in a beam of magical lantern light and sparkles so brightly the guards are blinded. Gerald stops the head guard and audits him on the spot. Sir Detective Inspector Baggington investigates a suspicious door, which turns out to be the right door. Sabrino the Second casts Fireball, finally, on something that deserves it.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "And you?"
strings.dlg.lich.l3_moments.c0: [Rogue] Pick the lock on the vault door.
strings.dlg.lich.l3_moments.c2: [Bard] Sing the vault door a lullaby until it nods off and swings open.
strings.dlg.lich.l3_vault: The vault door swings open with a sound like a very old book being opened for the first time.
strings.dlg.lich.l3_vault_kick:
You kick the vault door. It's made of six hundred years of compressed paperwork. It does not move. You kick it again. Hollis gets up, walks round the table, and kicks the real table leg in solidarity. The vault door, for reasons nobody can explain, opens.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "...Narrative momentum."
strings.dlg.lich.l3_vault_polite:
You knock on the vault door. Politely.

OAKHAVEN (GM, after a long pause): "...From inside, a dry, quiet voice says: 'Come in.'"

The whole table goes silent.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Nobody has ever knocked before."
strings.dlg.lich.l3_steve:
OAKHAVEN (as STEVE, trembling, gripping his spoon): "Me? Really?"

Steve, four hit points, armed with a spoon, walks up to the vault door, and turns the handle.

It was never locked. Nobody had ever tried the handle.

OAKHAVEN (as STEVE, in a whisper): "...Night school."

The table erupts. Rolf is crying. Baggy is standing on a chair. Steve is, briefly, the greatest hero in the history of the Lantern Inn.
strings.dlg.lich.l3_cabinet:
OAKHAVEN (GM): "Inside the vault there is no gold. No treasure. Only a single, ordinary, four-drawer filing cabinet, standing alone in the middle of the room. The top drawer is labelled IN. The bottom drawer is labelled OUT. The OUT drawer is empty. It has been empty for six hundred years."

"This is the phylactery. In the IN drawer is a single sheet of paper: a tax return, every field blank, and pinned to it, a note in thin, shaking handwriting."

He reads the note aloud, and his voice is very quiet.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "'To whoever finds this. Please file it for me. I find that I cannot. I have filed everyone else's for six hundred years, and I cannot do my own, because when it is done, there will be nothing left for me to do. I am so tired.'"
strings.dlg.lich.l3_end:
As your fingers touch the paper, every lantern in the vault goes out.

OAKHAVEN (GM, slowly, in a voice like dry pages): "A figure stands in the doorway. Robes the colour of old ink. A face like a skull wearing spectacles. In one bony hand, a quill."

OAKHAVEN (as THE LICH): "Who... has touched... my IN tray?"

He lowers the screen.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "And that's where we'll stop for tonight."

The entire back table of the Lantern Inn screams at him in unison. Sabrino throws a biscuit. Oakhaven has clearly never been happier.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_start:
Word has got round. The back table is surrounded. Fenwick has brought his bookshelf again. Vaelen is selling snacks. Brother Aldous is pretending he just happened to be passing. Even Mortimer Quill, the ghost critic, is floating by the fireplace with his notebook, "strictly in a professional capacity".

KAELEN (reading, voice catching slightly): "PREVIOUSLY. The plan failed in the first ten seconds. The party improvised. They found the phylactery, and it was a filing cabinet, and inside it was a note from a very tired man. And then he came home, and found them in his vault."

OAKHAVEN (GM, quietly): "Session Four. The Lich."

OAKHAVEN (as ARCHCHANCELLOR VELLUM DREADQUILL): "Who... has touched... my IN tray?"
strings.dlg.lich.l4_start.c2: [Paladin who knocked] "You said 'come in'. So we came in."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_fight:
OAKHAVEN (as THE LICH): "So be it." Bony hands rise. Paper whirls up from every drawer in the room like a storm.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "The Lich casts... Audit. Everyone make a saving throw against paperwork."

Around the table, dice fly. Gerald makes his save with ease. Sabrino the Second fails the save and is buried in receipts. Hollis rolls a d6, very obviously, and says "Twenty." Oakhaven doesn't even look.

OAKHAVEN (GM): "Your turn."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_fight.c0: [Roll] Strike the Lich with everything you have.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_fight.c1: [Stop] Lower your weapon. Something about this feels wrong.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_fight_win:
Your blow lands. The Lich staggers. Paper scatters. For a moment, it looks as though you might actually win.

And then the Lich does something nobody expects. He doesn't fight back. He just sits down, very slowly, on the floor of his vault, among the drifting paper, and puts his skull in his hands.

OAKHAVEN (as THE LICH, very quietly): "Thank goodness. I thought no one would ever come."

The whole table goes silent.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_fight_stop:
You lower your weapon. One by one, the others lower theirs. Even Sabrino.

SABRINO (quietly): "He's not attacking. Look at him. He's just... tired."

The paper storm settles. The Lich stands alone in the middle of his vault, a skull in spectacles, holding a quill he hasn't put down in six hundred years.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_talk:
OAKHAVEN (as THE LICH): "You read it." The skull tilts. "Then you know. I am the greatest administrator who ever lived. I have filed four million, six hundred thousand and twelve forms. Births. Deaths. Permits. Complaints."

"And I cannot file my own. Because when it is done, I will be done. There will be nothing left on my desk. No reason to stay. And I do not know who I am without something left to do."

Behind the dragon screen, Oakhaven has stopped doing the voice. He is just reading. His hands, you notice, are not quite steady.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_talk.c0: [Gerald] "Rolf. Gerald could help him file it."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_talk.c1: [Bard] Sing the Lich a song about rest.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_talk.c2: [Heart] "You don't have to finish everything to be allowed to rest."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_file:
ROLF (softly, putting on the imaginary spectacles): "Gerald pulls up a chair. 'Archchancellor. May I?'"

And the whole table does it together. Gerald reads out each field. Sister Crumb finds the receipts. Baggington investigates six hundred years of deductions. Sabrino the Second, very carefully, does not set anything on fire. Kaelen writes down every line as it's filled in. And at the bottom, where it says SIGNATURE, Gerald hands the Lich his own quill.

OAKHAVEN (as THE LICH, barely a whisper): "...Oh. Oh, that wasn't so hard. Was it."

He signs. He places the form in the OUT tray.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_song:
You stand at the real table and sing. A lullaby, slow and simple, about putting down your pen at the end of a long day, about a desk that's finally clear, about someone waiting for you at home.

Nobody laughs. Nobody even moves. In the crowd round the table, Mortimer Quill has stopped writing.

OAKHAVEN (as THE LICH): "...Someone waiting. I had forgotten that was a thing that could happen."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_song_crack:
Your voice cracks on the high note. You stop. You're embarrassed.

And then, from round the table, Marta picks it up. Then Rolf. Then Baggy, very off-key. Then the whole crowd, Fenwick and Vaelen and even Hollis, humming, until the song isn't yours any more, it's everyone's.

OAKHAVEN (as THE LICH): "...All of you. For me."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_heart:
You put down your dice.

"You don't have to finish everything to be allowed to rest," you say. "Nobody does. Not a lich. Not a clerk. Nobody's desk is ever really empty. You're allowed to stop anyway."

There's a long silence. Behind the dragon screen, Oakhaven takes his spectacles off. He doesn't do the Lich's voice when he speaks. He just speaks.

OAKHAVEN: "...Nineteen years. Excellent attendance. Not one day off. Not one." He looks round the table, at all of you. "I wrote the Lich nine years ago. I didn't realise until just now who I'd written."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_heart.c0: "Then take a day off, Oakhaven. We'll still be here on Thursday."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_heart.c1: Reach across the table and put a hand on his shoulder.
strings.dlg.lich.l4_rest:
OAKHAVEN (GM, his voice steady again, gentle): "The Archchancellor looks at the OUT tray. For the first time in six hundred years, it is not empty."

"He sets down his quill. He takes off his spectacles. He folds them, carefully, and places them on the desk."

"'Thank you,' says Vellum Dreadquill. 'I think I'll take the rest of the day off.'"

"And he walks out of the vault, and out of the tower, and out of the city of Inkwell, and nobody in the Underdark ever sees him again, though some say there's a skeleton in spectacles who sits by an underground lake, feeding the fish, doing absolutely nothing at all."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_bow_great:
The crowd around the back table bursts into applause. It goes on and on. Mortimer Quill is applauding. Hollis is applauding. Steve, somewhere in everyone's imagination, is applauding with his spoon.

Oakhaven slides something across the table to you: a slim, elegant quill, black as ink, with a silver nib.

"The Archchancellor's quill," he says. "I carved it for the campaign. I'd like you to have it." Then, after a moment: "I've booked a day off. Monday. My first in nineteen years. I don't know what people do on days off. I'll write and tell you."
strings.dlg.lich.l4_bow:
Everyone applauds. It's a little messy, a little teary, and nobody is quite sure how the session ended up being about Oakhaven, but everybody knows it was.

He slides a black quill across the table to you. "The Archchancellor's. I carved it. Keep it." And then: "I've booked a day off. Monday. I'll write."
strings.dlg.lich.l_after:
Oakhaven is at his desk, as always. But there's a seashell beside his inkwell that wasn't there before, and a very faint sunburn across his nose.

"I went to the coast," he says. "I sat on a beach. I did nothing. For six hours." He considers. "It was terrifying. I'm going again next month."

He taps a stack of papers. "Campaign Three. 'The Mimic Who Wanted to Be a Real Chest.' Chester returns. Steve gets a subplot. Thursdays."
strings.quest.lich1.title: The Lich Who Forgot to File I: The Descent
strings.quest.lich1.summary: Oakhaven's second campaign. A lich, six hundred years overdue on his tax return. Two new players at the table.
strings.quest.lich1.stage0: Play the session with Oakhaven's Thursday group.
strings.quest.lich1.journal0: Campaign Two. Sabrino is playing a wizard called Sabrino. Kaelen is writing everything down.
strings.quest.lich1.stage100: Completed: the party is in the Underdark (and Steve's story continues).
strings.quest.lich1.journal100: Mushrooms with opinions, a rival party called the Glorious Five, and Steve. Steve went to night school.
strings.quest.lich2.title: The Lich Who Forgot to File II: The City of Inkwell
strings.quest.lich2.summary: A city of a hundred thousand gnome clerks. Oakhaven has never been happier.
strings.quest.lich2.stage0: Play the session with Oakhaven's Thursday group.
strings.quest.lich2.journal0: The city of Inkwell. Every street is a queue. Every door has a stamp.
strings.quest.lich2.stage100: Completed: the party has a plan. Oakhaven says no plan has ever survived this table.
strings.quest.lich2.journal100: We spent two real hours planning a heist. Oakhaven looked delighted the whole time, which is worrying.
strings.quest.lich3.title: The Lich Who Forgot to File III: The Heist
strings.quest.lich3.summary: The Tower of Unfiled Things. The plan. The plan's first ten seconds.
strings.quest.lich3.stage0: Play the session with Oakhaven's Thursday group.
strings.quest.lich3.journal0: Heist night. I rolled a one on the first step. The plan is gone. Everyone is improvising.
strings.quest.lich3.stage100: Completed: the phylactery was a filing cabinet. Oakhaven stopped RIGHT THERE.
strings.quest.lich3.journal100: Inside the vault: a filing cabinet, an empty OUT tray, and a note from a very tired man. Then the Lich came home.
strings.quest.lich4.title: The Lich Who Forgot to File IV: The Lich
strings.quest.lich4.summary: Archchancellor Vellum Dreadquill, and the one form he could never file.
strings.quest.lich4.stage0: Play the final session with Oakhaven's Thursday group.
strings.quest.lich4.journal0: Half of Bellwether is crowded round the back table. Even the ghost critic came.
strings.quest.lich4.stage100: Completed: the Lich took the rest of the day off. So did Oakhaven.
strings.quest.lich4.journal100: The Lich's form went in the OUT tray at last. Somewhere in the middle of it, the session stopped being about the Lich and started being about Oakhaven. He's booked a day off. His first in nineteen years.
strings.item.lich_quill.name: The Archchancellor's Quill
strings.item.lich_quill.description: A slim black quill with a silver nib, carved by Oakhaven for the Lich who finally put his down. +2 Intellect, +8% spell power, +1 to dice rolls in conversation.
strings.item.oakhaven_postcard.name: A Postcard from Oakhaven
strings.item.oakhaven_postcard.description: A postcard of a beach, written in neat Bureau handwriting.
strings.book.oakhaven_postcard.text:
A painted postcard of a pale beach, a grey sea and a very blue sky. On the back, in small, careful Bureau handwriting:

"Dear friend,

I am at the coast. I have been sitting on the sand for three hours. I have done nothing. Nobody has asked me to stamp anything. A gull stole my sandwich. I did not file a complaint.

I found myself thinking of the Archchancellor, by his underground lake, feeding the fish. I think he would have liked it here.

Thank you for Thursdays. Thank you for knocking.

Yours, unofficially,
Oakhaven

P.S. There is a seashell in the envelope. It is for your desk. Everyone should have something on their desk that isn't work."
strings.bark.clerk.holiday: Did you know the sea just... keeps going? Nobody tells you that. There's no form for it.
strings.dlg.trout.t.open: "You're not playing cards, Hollis. What's wrong?"
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_open:
For the first time since you've known him, Hollis isn't playing cards. The deck sits squared on the folding table, untouched. He's staring west, over the village wall, at the treeline.

"Hmm." A long pause. "Whistled this morning. Like always. Two notes." He doesn't whistle them now. "Nothing."

"Thirty years I've had that horse. I've whistled from the bottom of a well, from the top of a tower, from inside a dragon. Once. Briefly. And every time, she's there. Sometimes in a wall. Sometimes upside down. Sometimes on the roof of a building that doesn't have a roof. But there."

He slides something across the card table. A sheet of paper, folded four times, written in charcoal.
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_note:
It says, in large, wobbly capitals:

"WE HAV YOUR HORS.
LEEVE 300 GOLD AT THE OLD OAK IN THE WISSLING WOOD.
COME ALONE. NO MONSTER HUNTERS.
- THE HORSE THEIVES GILD (EST. THIS WEEK)"

HOLLIS: "Hmm. I'm a monster hunter."

He taps the note. "Problem one: nobody steals that horse. I've seen her walk out of a burning stable, look back, and walk in again for the hay. Rope goes straight through her. Problem two: if somebody HAD taken her, I'd still whistle and she'd still come. She's never once failed to come."

He looks at you, and for a moment the cat-yellow eyes are not a monster hunter's eyes at all. Just an old man's.

"Something's wrong. I want to know what. You're better at the asking-questions part than me. I'm better at the hitting."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_trout:
HOLLIS: "Found her as a foal. Standing on the top of a lighthouse. Inside the lamp. Keeper had no idea how she got up there, and neither did she, and she didn't seem to think it mattered."

"Called her Trout because the first thing she ever did was eat one. Whole. Out of my hand. Looked me in the eye while she did it."

He turns a card over in his fingers without looking at it.

"Monster hunters... we don't keep much. You move on. Villages forget you. Contracts end. People don't write. But you whistle, and the horse comes." A pause. "Hmm. That's all. Find her."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_take:
HOLLIS: "Keep the note. You'll want to show it round."

"People keep telling me they've SEEN her. On roofs. In the sea. At a party. Places she can't be. Ask them. Look where they say. Come back when you know what happened, not when you've guessed. Guessers get it wrong in front of the horse, and she remembers."

He picks up the cards at last, shuffles once, puts them down again.
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_hint:
HOLLIS (counting on his fingers): "Vaelen sells everything to everybody, so somebody bought something. Fenwick's read every book about every tree within a hundred miles. Your detective friend, Baggy, will look at that note through a magnifying glass and say something wrong, and then something right, usually in that order."

"Sightings: the library roof here in the village. The quay at Saltmere. Up on the boundary stone on the Old Road. The werewolf's garden, the vampire's balcony. And the wood to the west, with the sign at the edge."

"Four good clues and you'll see it. Hmm. Probably."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_deduce:
Hollis sweeps the cards off the table into a box, and lays the ransom note in the middle, and folds his arms.

HOLLIS: "Go on. Start with the note. Who wrote it?"
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_deduce.c0: "Rolf. The werewolf. He ate her, and wrote the note to cover it up."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_deduce.c1: "Lord Ashgrave. Look at him. He is OBVIOUSLY guilty of something."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_deduce.c4: "A man called Steve, who camps in the Whistling Wood."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_deduce.c5: "Actually, I need to look into this more."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_w_rolf:
HOLLIS: "Rolf is a vegetarian. On weekdays. And on weekends he eats exclusively cake. I've seen him apologise to a lettuce."

"Also, he can't spell 'gild' wrong. He can't spell it at all. He signs his name with a paw print. Hmm. Try again."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_w_ash:
HOLLIS: "Ashgrave is guilty of many things. Bad poetry. Standing in windows. Glittering. Being three hundred years old and still writing in his diary about how nobody understands him."

"But stealing a horse would mean going outside during the day, and he'd rather die. Again. Hmm. Try again."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_w_sab:
HOLLIS: "Sabrino says a newt-horse would come back. Angry. On the roof. Sabrino has apparently tried this, with a different horse, which I'm choosing not to ask about."

"And Sabrino would have signed the note. With a flourish. And a small drawing of a hat. Try again."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_w_baggy:
HOLLIS (very slowly): "...Baggy."

"Baggy spent last Tuesday investigating Baggy, because Baggy found a set of suspicious footprints that turned out to be Baggy's. Baggy then interviewed Baggy for three hours and released Baggy without charge."

"No. Hmm. Try again."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_q2:
HOLLIS: "Steve." He frowns. "Hmm. Steve. Fine. Steve writes a note, Steve wants gold, Steve can't spell. Simple."

"But that's not the question, is it. Nobody can STEAL her. So the question is why she won't come when I whistle."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_q2.c2: "She IS coming when you whistle. Just not to you."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_w_angry:
HOLLIS: "She's a horse. She doesn't do angry. Once I accidentally sold her saddle and she just appeared on the buyer's roof and stared at him till he gave it back."

"That isn't angry. That's... administration. Hmm. Again."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_w_rope:
HOLLIS: "Told you. Rope goes straight through her. So do walls, sometimes. So does a moat. She stood in a moat once for a week, just at the bottom, quite happily. Fish loved her."

"Again."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_notyet: HOLLIS: "Hmm. Then go and find out. Fenwick knows the woods. And that wood out west's got a name. Places get named for things."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_solved:
You tell him about the Old Oak in the Whistling Wood. The hollow in its trunk. The wind blowing through it, two notes, low then high, short and sharp.

His whistle.

Hollis is very still for a long time.

HOLLIS: "...I grew up near a wood like that. Learned to whistle walking past it. Never knew which of us learned it from which."

"So she's been coming. Every time the wind blew. Thirty years she's come when I whistled, and now the wood whistles louder than me, and she's out there, standing wherever she is, wondering why I never turn up." He clears his throat. "Hmm."

"Go. Stop that tree whistling. And if this Steve's out there, there'll be wolves too: wolves can smell a horse from a mile off, and a man with four hit points from two."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_wood: HOLLIS: "Gate in the west wall. Follow the path. Steve's camp's down the left fork, the oak's at the end of the right. Kill the wolves before you start a conversation. Talk to Steve before you start hitting. Different order, normally, but Steve's not normal."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_home:
Hollis turns round.

Trout is standing behind him. She was not there a moment ago. She is there now, with the calm of a creature who has always been exactly where she meant to be, and she lowers her long brown nose, and bumps it into the middle of his chest.

Hollis doesn't say anything. He just puts his forehead against hers, and closes his eyes, and stands like that for a while.

You look at the treeline. It seems polite.

HOLLIS (eventually, gruffly): "Hmm." He clears his throat. "Something in my eye. Monster hunter thing. Mutations."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_home2:
HOLLIS: "Tell me everything."

You do. The wood. The wolves. Grandmother's nightgown. The oak. Steve.
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_home2.c0: "Steve's coming to live in Bellwether. Oakhaven has a seat for him on Thursdays."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_home2.c1: "Steve's staying in the wood. Honest camping, from now on."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_home2.c2: "Steve and I had words. He won't be writing ransom notes again."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_home2.c3: "Steve's still working out what to do with himself."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_steve_unsure: HOLLIS: "Hmm. Aren't we all." He scratches Trout behind the ears. "Tell him there's a seat at the card table if he wants one. Tell him to bring buttons."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_steve_town:
HOLLIS: "The man who stole my horse is joining a games night." He thinks about it. "Hmm. Good. I'll play him at cards. Take everything he owns. Give it back. Teach him to shuffle."

"Everybody needs a table to sit at."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_steve_wood: HOLLIS: "Honest camping." A short huff that might be a laugh. "There's no such thing. But there's no such thing as an honest monster hunter either, and here I am."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_steve_scared:
HOLLIS: "Hmm. Hope you didn't frighten him too badly. A man who writes 'please come and get your horse' at the bottom of his ransom notes isn't a villain. He's just lonely, and bad at it."

He looks at Trout. "Lot of that about."
strings.dlg.trout.hollis.c3_reward:
Hollis reaches into a saddlebag that Trout was not wearing a moment ago, and takes out two things.

The first is a horseshoe, old, worn smooth on one side, with tiny marks scratched into it: a lighthouse, a well, a tower, a roof, a roof, another roof.

HOLLIS: "Her first shoe. Every place she's turned up that she shouldn't have. Brings luck. Or at least it makes luck turn up somewhere odd."

The second is a battered deck of cards in a leather case.

HOLLIS: "My deck. Rules are inside. You'll lose. Everyone loses the first hundred games." He pauses. "Thank you. For the asking-questions part."

Trout looks at you. Then she is, briefly, standing on top of the notice board, and then she is back beside Hollis, as if nothing happened. You decide this is how she says thank you.
strings.dlg.steve.root:
A smallish man in a cooking pot (worn as a helmet) and a coat with more patches than coat jumps to his feet as you approach, brandishing a spoon.

"STAND AND DELIVER! Or... stand. Standing's fine. You don't have to deliver. Hello."
strings.dlg.steve.root.c2: "The wolves are dead, Steve. Start talking."
strings.dlg.steve.root.c3: "Steve, have you decided what you'll do now?"
strings.dlg.steve.deny:
STEVE: "Horse? What horse? Never seen one. Don't know what they look like. Is it a sort of soup? I've had soup. Recently. There was nothing in it. Nothing at all. Especially not a horse."

Behind him, very clearly, on the very top of the ridge of his tent, is a single muddy hoofprint.

Next to the campfire is a pile of carrot tops, roughly forty of them.

STEVE: "...Those are mine. I love carrots. I am famously a carrot man. Goodbye."
strings.dlg.steve.wolves:
Steve is standing on top of a crate, with his spoon out in front of him like a sword. Grey shapes slink through the trees round the camp, circling.

STEVE: "They came with the dark! They can smell the HORSE! Well, they can smell where the horse WAS, she doesn't stay anywhere long, she was on the tent, then the crate, then in the SOUP-" He catches himself. "What horse. Help."
strings.dlg.steve.confess:
Steve sits down by the fire, takes the pot off his head, and holds it in his lap. Without it he looks younger, and very tired.

STEVE: "Alright. Alright. Three days ago I woke up and there was a horse in my tent. Inside. Standing. The tent's four foot high. I don't know how she fitted. I don't think she knew either."

"And I thought: Steve. Here is your chance. Night school said every career starts with one big job. A horse that valuable, owned by a monster hunter, he'd pay anything to get her back."

"So I wrote a ransom note. On the back of my character sheet. It was the only paper I had."
strings.dlg.steve.sheet:
STEVE (brightening, despite himself): "Oh! Yes! A man called Oakhaven gave it to me. Nineteen years ago. I tried to rob him on the west road. With this spoon. He looked at me, and looked at the spoon, and said, 'You're doing it wrong, but you're committed, and that counts for something.'"

"Then he gave me a character sheet. 'STEVE. Level One Bandit. Four hit points.' Said he'd put me in a game. He sends me the session notes. Every Thursday, for nineteen years. I've been in a tavern brawl. I've been thrown through a window. I went to NIGHT SCHOOL." He sniffs. "Best thing that ever happened to me."

"And I wrote a ransom note on the back of it. Because I was hungry, and alone in a wood, and I wanted to be... somebody in a story. Even the villain."
strings.dlg.steve.where:
STEVE: "That's the thing! I don't KNOW! She won't stay! Every time the wind blows through that old oak she's off, and I find her somewhere ridiculous. On the tent. In the soup. On top of the oak. She's up there NOW. She's been up there two days. She ate all my carrots first."

"I wrote six more notes asking him to come and get her. I couldn't bring myself to post them. A monster hunter! He'd chop me up!"

He looks over at the great oak at the end of the path. Faint on the wind, you hear it: two notes, low then high.
strings.dlg.steve.where.c0: "We need to stop that tree whistling."
strings.dlg.steve.plug:
You walk to the Old Oak together. Steve keeps a careful step behind you, spoon raised, glancing at the shadows.

The hollow in the trunk is a knot-hole the size of a fist. Every gust pulls the whistle out of it: low, high. High above, something big shifts in the branches and snorts.

STEVE: "What do we stuff it with? I haven't got anything. I haven't got ANYTHING."

He looks at the bundle of crumpled ransom notes in his coat pocket. All seven of them.
strings.dlg.steve.plug_sheet:
Steve goes pale and clutches his coat.

STEVE: "Not the sheet. Please. Not the sheet. It's the only thing anyone ever gave me."

You nod. Not the sheet.
strings.dlg.steve.plug2:
Steve balls up his seven ransom notes, one by one, and stuffs them into the hollow. "WE HAV YOUR HORS." In it goes. "PLEASE come and get your horse." In it goes.

The wind blows. The oak creaks.

It doesn't whistle.

STEVE (quietly, amazed): "That's the first useful thing I've ever written."
strings.dlg.steve.whistle:
You put two fingers to your lips, and whistle. Low, then high. Short and sharp, the way Hollis does it.

Trout is standing next to you.

She doesn't arrive. There's no hoofbeat, no rustle of branches, no sense of travel. One moment she is on top of a forty-foot oak, and the next she is standing beside you with her nose in your pocket, looking for carrots, as if she has always been there and you are the one who just turned up.

She is a bay mare with a white blaze and a red saddle and the calm, ancient, faintly judgemental eyes of a creature who has stood on a thousand roofs and never once explained herself.

STEVE (in a whisper): "She does that."

Then she lifts her head, ears pricked, towards the east. Towards the village. Towards a whistle you can't hear, and probably nobody else could either.

And she's gone. Home.
strings.dlg.steve.future:
Steve looks at the empty space where the horse was, and at his camp, and at his spoon.

STEVE: "I don't know. I'm not a very good bandit. I'm not very good at anything. I'm a level one everything."
strings.dlg.steve.future.c0: "There's a table at the Lantern Inn on Thursdays. Oakhaven's been writing you into the game for nineteen years. Come and play in person."
strings.dlg.steve.future.c1: "Stay in the wood, Steve. But be a camper. An honest one. You're good at camping."
strings.dlg.steve.future.c2: [Intimidation] "If I ever see another ransom note, Steve, I'll bring the monster hunter."
strings.dlg.steve.future_town:
Steve stares at you.

STEVE: "In... person? At the actual table? With the actual dice?" His voice cracks. "Do you think they'd mind? I've only got four hit points."

"Rolf's playing an accountant," you tell him. "Hollis cheats. Sabrino only casts Fireball. You'll fit right in."

Steve packs his entire camp into one sack in under a minute. At the last moment he stops, and presses something into your hand.

STEVE: "My spoon. For luck. I'll get another one. I'm going to be a new Steve."
strings.dlg.steve.future_wood:
STEVE: "Honest camping." He tries the words out. "Steve's Honest Camping. Tents, fires, directions to the village. No horses. Absolutely no horses."

He nods slowly, then faster.

"I'll paint a sign. I'm good at signs. Bad at spelling, good at signs." He presses something into your hand. "My spoon. For luck. You need it more than me. You go places with WOLVES."
strings.dlg.steve.future_scared:
Steve goes very white and sits down very fast.

STEVE: "No more notes. No more notes ever. I'll write shopping lists. I'll write POETRY. Please don't bring him."

He fumbles in his coat and holds out his spoon with both hands, like a man surrendering a sword.

STEVE: "Take it. It's all I've got."

You take it. You feel, briefly, like Grimsby Optimus.
strings.dlg.steve.camp: STEVE: "It's quiet without her. I keep looking up at the oak." He prods the fire. "She left a hoofprint on my tent. I'm keeping it."
strings.dlg.steve.town:
Steve is sitting at the back table of the Lantern Inn, in a clean shirt Marta found him, with a mug of tea, a plate of biscuits, and his battered character sheet laid out in front of him like a holy text.

STEVE: "Last Thursday I rolled a natural twenty. The whole table cheered. Hollis took all my money at cards afterwards and then gave it back and taught me to shuffle." He beams. "Oakhaven says I'm level two now."

"Level two."
strings.dlg.trout.root: Trout. A bay mare with a white blaze, a red saddle, and the deep, unbothered calm of a creature who has stood on a thousand rooftops and never once explained herself.
strings.dlg.trout.oak:
Trout looks down at you from the very top of the Old Oak, forty feet up, standing on a branch that could not possibly hold a horse. She chews something. She considers you.

She does not come down.

Somewhere below, the wind moves through the trunk, and the hollow whistles, two notes, and her ears flick towards it. Not towards you.
strings.dlg.trout.pat:
You rub the white blaze on her nose. She leans into it with her whole considerable weight, and huffs warm hay-breath into your face, and for a moment the world is quiet and simple and smells of horse.

You feel better. Clearer. As if something that had been whispering at the edge of your hearing has politely gone away.
strings.dlg.trout.carrot:
Trout takes the carrot with great delicacy, crunches it, and is briefly standing behind you. Then in front of you again. Then, for no reason you can see, on top of the nearest roof, and then back.

You understand, somehow, that this was a thank-you.
strings.dlg.trout.where:
Trout looks at you with the infinite patience of a horse who has been asked this question for thirty years by a man who has never once got an answer.

She does not answer.

But she does, very gently, put her nose on top of your head. You decide that counts.
strings.dlg.trout.vaelen.trout:
VAELEN: "Unusual? Friend, I sell bucket-helmets to adventurers who think they're stealth equipment. Unusual is my business."

"But. Since you ask. Three days ago, a nervous little man in a cooking pot came in and bought every carrot I had. Forty. Paid in buttons. When I asked what they were for, he said, and I quote, 'a friend who keeps appearing.'"

"Then he asked if I sold 'ransom paper'. I don't. I sold him a quill. He tried to pay for it with a spoon. I said no. He seemed very attached to the spoon."
strings.dlg.trout.fenwick.t: "What do you know about the Whistling Wood?"
strings.dlg.trout.fenwick.trout:
Fenwick lights up like a man who has waited his whole life for that exact question, and pulls down a book called 'Trees of the Western Marches, Volume Nine: Oaks That Make Noises'.

FENWICK: "The Old Oak! Hollow trunk, a knot-hole low on the east side. When the west wind blows, it whistles. Always the same two notes. Low, then high. Short, sharp."

He turns a page, then stops, and looks up.

"There's a footnote. 'The local monster hunter is said to have learned his whistle from this tree as a boy. Or possibly the tree learned it from him. Nobody has asked the tree.'"

"Low, then high..." Fenwick frowns. "Why does that sound familiar?"
strings.dlg.trout.baggy.t: "Baggy, could you examine this ransom note?"
strings.dlg.trout.baggy.trout:
Baggy seizes the note, produces a magnifying glass, and examines it from a distance of about one inch.

BAGGY: "Aha. Charcoal. Written by a left-handed giraffe."

"...No. Hold on. Wrong way up."

"Aha! Written by a right-handed person of average height who is frightened, hungry and has never been to school. Except night school. You can tell from the spelling. Night school spelling is very confident."

Baggy turns it over.

BAGGY: "And on the back... a grid. Boxes. 'STR', 'DEX', 'HP: 4'. It's a CHARACTER SHEET. From the Thursday games at the Lantern Inn! Name at the top: 'STEVE. Level One Bandit. Equipment: one spoon.'"

Baggy lowers the magnifying glass slowly.

BAGGY: "I've cracked it. Either our culprit is a man called Steve, or a very clever criminal who has FRAMED a man called Steve. Or Steve is a giraffe. I'm keeping all three open."
strings.dlg.trout.oakhaven.trout:
Oakhaven puts down his pen. He takes off his spectacles. He polishes them for much longer than spectacles need.

OAKHAVEN: "Nineteen years ago, on the west road, a young man jumped out from behind a tree and tried to rob me. With a spoon. He was shaking so badly he dropped it twice."

"I had nothing to give him but paper. So I gave him a character sheet. I told him he was in a game now. I wrote him a part."

"I post him the session notes every Thursday. To a hollow tree in the Whistling Wood. He has never written back. I assumed he'd moved on. Or..." He doesn't finish.

"Steve is real. Steve was always real. Please don't hurt him."
strings.dlg.trout.rolf.trout:
Rolf goes white, then red, then a sort of mottled grey, and clutches his trowel to his bare chest.

ROLF: "EAT a HORSE? I've never eaten anything with a face! I don't even eat cabbages with a face, and I've met two!"

He calms down, slowly, and wipes his eyes.

ROLF: "I did SEE her, though. Hollis's horse. Two nights ago. She was standing on the roof of my greenhouse. Then she was standing IN the greenhouse. The greenhouse was locked. She ate a marrow. I'm not angry. It was a beautiful marrow. I hope she enjoyed it."

"She went west. Towards the wood. I heard whistling."
strings.dlg.trout.ash.t: "Have you seen a horse, my lord?"
strings.dlg.trout.ash.trout:
Ashgrave doesn't turn from the window. A single tear, which might be glitter, runs down his cheek.

ASHGRAVE: "At midnight, on my balcony, she stood. A great brown mare, bathed in moonlight, gazing at me. Not with fear. Not with hunger. With... understanding."

"It was the most romantic moment of my three hundred years."

"Then she ate one of my roses and vanished. I have written eleven poems about it. Would you like to hear—"

"...No? No. Nobody ever does." A pause. "She went west."
strings.dlg.trout.sabrino.t: "Sabrino, did you turn a horse into a newt?"
strings.dlg.trout.sabrino.trout:
Sabrino looks deeply offended, and then, after some thought, only moderately offended.

SABRINO: "Sabrino has turned many things into newts. A tax collector. Two tax collectors. A rival witch, briefly, during an argument about hats. Never a horse."

"Horses do not stay newts. They come back. Angry. On your roof. Sabrino has learned this lesson the way Sabrino learns all lessons: once, loudly, with property damage."

"Besides, that horse is not a normal horse. That horse is one of those things the world forgets to check on. Sabrino respects her. Sabrino would never."
strings.quest.trout.title: Case File #3: The Horse Who Wasn't There
strings.quest.trout.summary: Hollis whistled, and for the first time in thirty years, his horse didn't come. There's a ransom note. It's spelled wrong.
strings.quest.trout.journal0: Hollis isn't playing cards. Something's wrong.
strings.quest.trout.stage10: Find out what happened to Trout: ask around, follow up the sightings, then tell Hollis (4+ clues).
strings.quest.trout.journal10: A ransom note from 'The Horse Theives Gild', and a horse nobody can steal. People keep seeing Trout where she can't be: on roofs, in the sea, at parties. Somebody bought a lot of carrots. Hollis says don't guess.
strings.quest.trout.stage20: Go to the Whistling Wood (west gate). Save Steve from the wolves, then stop the Old Oak whistling.
strings.quest.trout.journal20: The Old Oak in the Whistling Wood whistles Hollis's whistle: two notes, low then high. Trout's been answering it. And a man called Steve wrote the ransom note.
strings.quest.trout.journal30: Steve stuffed his ransom notes into the hollow, the oak went quiet, and when I whistled, Trout was beside me. Then she went home.
strings.quest.trout.journal100: Hollis put his forehead against his horse's and stood there a while. He says it was something in his eye. He gave me Trout's first horseshoe, and his deck of cards, and said thank you for the asking-questions part.
strings.npc.steve.name: Steve
strings.npc.steve.title: Bandit (Level One)
strings.npc.trout.name: Trout
strings.npc.trout.title: Hollis's Horse
strings.bark.steve.2: Night school said: always have a backup plan. My backup plan is also a spoon.
strings.bark.trout.1: (Trout chews thoughtfully, looking at a roof.)
strings.bark.trout.2: (Trout is standing slightly to the left of where she was. You did not see her move.)
strings.bark.hollis.trout: Hmm. She's on the chapel roof again. Good. That means she's home.
strings.bark.clerk.steve: Steve rolled initiative last Thursday and cried. Happy tears. I've added a new rule to page 213.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.whistling_wood: Whistling Wood. Don't whistle. Don't whistle. Why does that make me want to whistle?
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.whistling_wood: Old trees. Older than the Bureau. Somewhere a wind is making the same two notes, over and over.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.trout.0: Kaelen. Kaelen. Hypothetically. If a horse were standing on a roof... how would you get it down?
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.trout.1: You wouldn't. You'd wait. Horses come down on their own time. So do most things worth waiting for.
strings.comp.kaelen.banter.trout.3: It's a horse, Baggy. Everything doesn't have to be a clue.
strings.map.whistling_wood.name: The Whistling Wood
strings.enemy.grey_wolf.name: Grey Wolf
strings.enemy.granny_wolf.name: A Wolf in Grandmother's Nightgown
strings.line.granny_wolf.alert: Oh, my dear! Come closer, so I can... no. No, I'm not doing the bit. You know the bit.
strings.line.granny_wolf.death: Tell her... the bonnet... DID suit me...
strings.item.ransom_note.name: The Ransom Note
strings.item.ransom_note.description: Charcoal on paper, spelled with great confidence. There's a grid printed faintly on the back.
strings.book.ransom_note.text:
WE HAV YOUR HORS.
LEEVE 300 GOLD AT THE OLD OAK IN THE WISSLING WOOD.
COME ALONE. NO MONSTER HUNTERS.
- THE HORSE THEIVES GILD (EST. THIS WEEK)

On the back, faint under the charcoal smudges, a printed grid: boxes labelled STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, CHA, and in neat Bureau handwriting at the top: "STEVE. Level One Bandit. HP: 4. Equipment: one spoon. Notes: committed."
strings.item.hollis_deck.name: Hollis's Deck
strings.item.hollis_deck.description: A battered deck of cards in a leather case. The rules are folded inside. They are long.
strings.book.hollis_deck.text:
THE RULES OF 'HMM', AS PLAYED BY HOLLIS THE GREY

1. Each player draws ten cards. Do not look at them yet. Say 'Hmm.'
2. Look at them. Say 'Hmm' again, differently.
3. Play cards in three rows: Swords, Bows, and Things That Are Not Clear. Highest total wins the round.
4. Win two rounds out of three to win the game.
5. Weather cards make everybody's cards worse. Nobody likes the weather cards. Hollis plays three of them in a row.
6. A card called 'The Horse' can be played into any row, including rows that don't exist yet, and occasionally into your opponent's hand.
7. If at any point you are in a burning village, a besieged city or the middle of a war, you must still stop and ask everyone you meet if they would like a game.
8. The innkeeper always has the best card. You must beat the innkeeper. You will not beat the innkeeper.
9. Hollis is allowed to look at your cards because he has mutations.
10. You will lose. Everybody loses the first hundred games. That's how you know you're learning.

Scrawled at the bottom: "If you are reading this, you are a friend. I don't have many. Deal. -H"
strings.item.carrot.name: Carrot
strings.item.carrot.description: Crunchy. Restores a little health and puts a spring in your step. Horses go mad for them. One particular horse goes mad for them in several places at once.
strings.item.trout_horseshoe.name: Trout's First Horseshoe
strings.item.trout_horseshoe.description: Worn smooth on one side, scratched with tiny pictures: a lighthouse, a well, a tower, a roof, a roof, another roof. +1 Agility, +8% movement speed, faster stamina and sanity recovery. You will occasionally turn up somewhere odd.
strings.item.red_hood.name: The Red Hood
strings.item.red_hood.description: Grandmother's granddaughter gave up on it and took up archery. She's very good. +1 Agility, +30% ranged critical damage. Wolves look at you funny.
strings.item.steve_spoon.name: Steve's Spoon
strings.item.steve_spoon.description: Tin. Bent. Nineteen years of brandishing. Hilariously weak, until it isn't: 30% critical chance, triple critical damage, and +50% against beasts. Night school taught Steve one thing: aim for the eyes.
strings.tip.27: If a wolf is wearing a nightgown and a bonnet, it is not your grandmother. Your grandmother is in Saltmere. Hit it.
strings.tip.28: Can't find your horse? Look up.
strings.dlg.reef.t.offer: "The fog's thinner, Silas. What can you see out there?"
strings.dlg.reef.t.row: "Row me out to the Light, Silas."
strings.dlg.reef.t.final: "Silas. Look who's coming down the jetty."
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_offer:
Silas doesn't look up from his hookless line. But he isn't singing, and his pale eyes are fixed on a point far out in the fog.

"Since you put it back to sleep, the fog's thinned. First time in forty years I can see the old Light from the end of this pier. The Saltmere Light. On the reef, out past where the big ones sleep."

"And last night there was a fire on the reef. A little one. Two shapes sat by it."

He's quiet for a long time.

"My lads went into the fog with the Order. Gave the sea their names, same as all of them. When you came back up out of that chapel, they didn't. I've been telling myself they're drowned. Easier."

"But two shapes. By a fire." His hands are shaking on the line. "Nobody's rowed out there since my father's time. The things in the water are asleep, mostly. I'll row. You walk the reef. The sea can't see you, can it. Not you."
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_offer.c1: "Soon. I'll come back when I'm ready."
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_row:
Silas stands, stiffly, and climbs down into a little clinker boat tied under the pier. He fits the oars into the rowlocks with the ease of seventy years.

SILAS: "Some folk want to close their eyes and arrive. I call those folk cargo. Boat trips take as long as they take. Sit down. Don't trail your hand in the water. And if anything big opens its eye, don't look back."
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_row.c0: Climb in. Push off into the fog.
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_home: SILAS: "Back we go." He looks past you, up at the dark tower. "Mind, I'll come out again whenever you like. I've rowed further for worse reasons."
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_final:
Silas is sitting in the boat at the end of the jetty with the oars across his knees. Behind you, the Saltmere Light swings its slow white beam over the water, and for the first time in forty years it touches Saltmere's roofs.

Two men are walking down the jetty. Torn robes. Same nose.

Silas sees them. He stands up in the boat. The boat rocks. He doesn't notice.

THOMAS: "Dad?"
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_final.c0: Stay quiet. This isn't your moment.
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_final2:
SILAS (in a voice like a rope about to go): "Tom." He swallows. "Abel."

ABEL: "You remember us."

SILAS: "Remember you? I counted you. Every tide. Every night. Two for the net. I never stopped."

He climbs up onto the jetty, an old man in yellow oilskins, and gets his arms round both of them at once, and they're taller than him, both of them, and none of that matters at all.

SILAS (muffled, into a shoulder): "Dinner's on the table. It's been on the table six weeks. It'll be cold."

THOMAS: "We'll eat it cold, Dad."

ABEL: "We'll eat it frozen."
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_final3:
Eventually Silas lets go, and wipes his face with an oilskin sleeve, and turns to you.

SILAS: "You walked out onto that reef with the big ones sleeping all round it and you picked my boys' names up off the rocks like shells." He shakes his head. "I don't have anything to give you that's worth that."

"But I've got the song. The whole of it. My father's, and his father's. Nobody's heard the last verse in a hundred years, because nobody had anything to sing it about." He presses a folded, salt-stained paper into your hand. "I wrote it out. Spelled it wrong. Sing it to somebody."

The four of you squeeze into a boat built for two, and Silas rows home in the light.
strings.dlg.reef.silas.r_after:
Silas has two fishing lines in the water today. Both have hooks. Tom and Abel are mending nets behind him and arguing about knots.

SILAS: "They're terrible at knots. Always were." He's smiling. You don't think you've seen him smile before. "The Light turns every night now. I sit here and count it. One, two, three. It's a good thing to count."

"Want to row out again? I don't mind. The big ones don't mind either. They're dreaming about it."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.root:
Two men sit by a driftwood fire, sharing one blanket and arguing quietly. Their robes are torn and stiff with salt. They have the same nose.

TALLER STRANGER: "Oh! Hello. You can see us. Good. We weren't sure."

SHORTER STRANGER: "We don't know who we are. We know we're brothers. We think. He's got my nose."

TALLER STRANGER: "I had it first."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.root.c2: Hold out the two bottles from the shore.
strings.dlg.reef.bro.root.c4: "The Light's burning. Silas is waiting at the jetty."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.who:
TALLER STRANGER: "That's the thing. We gave them away."

SHORTER STRANGER: "We call each other 'You' and 'Also You'. I'm Also You."

TALLER STRANGER: "I think I'm the elder. He thinks he's the elder. We tried counting our birthdays to settle it, but it turns out we gave our counting to the sea as well. Everything past four is just a sort of fog."

SHORTER STRANGER (quietly): "Sometimes I almost remember. Somebody stitching. Somebody saying 'bad at knots, good at laughing'. And a man on a pier."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.who.c0: "Your names might have washed up on the shore. I'll look."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.how:
TALLER STRANGER: "There was an Order. It had robes. Lovely robes. And they said: give the Deep your name, and you'll live forever. Partially."

SHORTER STRANGER: "It was in the small print. 'Eternal life (partial).' We also signed away swimming. Also in the small print."

TALLER STRANGER: "Then one night everyone stopped singing, and the big thing under the water went back to sleep, and we woke up here. On the rocks. With nothing. Not even who we were."

SHORTER STRANGER: "And there's a lady. On the tower. She's see-through. She's very kind. She keeps asking if anyone's come to relieve her."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.names:
You hold out the green bottle and the brown one. The taller man takes the green. His hands are shaking so hard he can hardly pull the wax.

He reads the sailcloth. Out loud. Slowly.

"Thomas... Gale."

And something comes back into his face, all at once, like a tide coming in: the colour, the lines round his eyes, a man's whole history.

THOMAS: "Mum stitched this. When I was seven. I lost my boots and she said, 'You'll not lose your name, at least.' ...Oh. Oh, I'm Tom. I'm Tom Gale. I'm bad at knots."

The other one has the school primer open on his knee, his finger moving under the enormous letters, again and again.

ABEL: "Abel. Abel Gale. That's me. I wrote that. I was so proud." He looks at the line at the bottom. "'He was so proud when he could write it. -S.' S. That's..."

THOMAS and ABEL (together): "Dad."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.names.c0: "He's on the pier at Saltmere. He rowed me out here."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.names2:
THOMAS: "Dad's on the pier. Dad's been on the pier the whole time, hasn't he."

ABEL: "Course he has. Where else would he be. He'll have made dinner."

They're both on their feet, then both stop, and look up at the dark tower behind them.

THOMAS: "Not in the dark, though. Dad always said: never row in the dark without the Light. And there's something under the reef. I can feel it turning over in its sleep, since the Light went out. Like someone with a bad dream."

ABEL: "The lady on the tower. Ask her. She'll know."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.wait:
THOMAS: "Not until the Light's lit. Dad would skin us."

ABEL: "Dad would row out here personally to skin us."
strings.dlg.reef.bro.ready: Tom and Abel look at each other. Then, as one, they start running down the rocks towards the jetty, and Abel trips, and Tom catches him, and they keep going, laughing like boys.
strings.dlg.reef.home.root:
Tom and Abel Gale are mending a net beside their father, badly. Every so often one of them says his own name, quietly, as if checking it's still there.

THOMAS: "Thank you. We don't say it enough. We say our names a lot, though."

ABEL: "Abel. Abel Gale. Sorry. I'll stop. I won't stop."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.root:
A woman stands by the dark lamp, faint as breath on glass, a lantern on a pole in her hand that gives no light at all. She looks at you, and then through you, and then at you again, and her face fills with a careful, enormous hope.

"You're solid. And it can't see you. Oh, that's good. That's very good."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.root.c2: "Show me how to light the lamp."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.root.c3: "Show me how to light the lamp."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.root.c4: "The Light's burning. And the thing under the reef is asleep again."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.who:
"Ondine Marsh. Keeper of the Saltmere Light. Fourth Marsh to keep it. Last, it turns out."

She smiles, a little embarrassed. "I died some time ago. Fell on the stairs in a storm. I got up the next night and trimmed the wick anyway, because nobody else was going to. I've done it every night since. Nobody came to relieve me." A pause. "I don't mind. Mostly. Somebody has to."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.for:
"Not for ships. That's what we told the guild. It's for the thing under the reef."

She looks down, past the rail, into the black water between the great sleeping limbs.

"While it can see the Light, it dreams. While it dreams, it isn't hungry. My great-grandfather worked that out, and built a tower, and his children and their children kept a lamp burning on top of a monster for four hundred years so that Saltmere could go fishing. Nobody ever thanked us. Nobody knew."

"That's lighthouse keeping. You do it so that nothing happens. And nothing happening never makes anybody's song."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.out:
"The men in robes came out in their boats and sang. All of them, all night. And the Light went out. It has never gone out. Not in four hundred years."

She holds up a hand. You can see the lamp's iron cage through it.

"I can't relight it. My hands go through the matches. I need somebody solid. And I need somebody it can't see, because the moment that wick catches, it will feel the light on its eyelids, and it will not want to go back to sleep, and it will reach up to find out who's done it."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.out.c0: "It can't see me. My name was struck from the Register."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.struck:
Ondine stares at you. Then she laughs, softly, the first laugh this tower has heard in a very long time.

"Struck. You're struck. Uncounted." She shakes her head. "Four hundred years of Marshes hiding from that thing, and the one person who could walk right past it shows up after I'm dead. Typical."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.first:
"Not yet. Not with those two boys down on the rocks with no names."

"When the wick catches, it'll stir, and it'll reach. Names are anchors. A man who knows his name can hold on to the rocks. A man who doesn't, the sea just... takes back. Find their names first. The tide washes things up on this reef. It always has. Bottles, mostly. People send their names out to sea and the sea sends them back here."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.light:
Ondine shows you: the brass wick-key, the oil reservoir, the box of long matches on its hook, still dry after all these years because she kept it dry.

You strike a match. It flares. You touch it to the wick.

The Saltmere Light comes on.

It doesn't flicker up. It blooms, white and steady and enormous, and the great lens begins to turn, and the beam goes sweeping out over the black water, across the reef, across the sleeping limbs, all the way to Saltmere.

And under the reef, something feels it on its eyelids.

The water by the north rocks heaves. A limb the thickness of a house rises out of the sea, eyes opening along its length one after another, looking for whoever did this, looking everywhere, looking straight through you.

ONDINE: "It can't see you. It can still HIT you. Go!"
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.farewell:
Ondine stands at the rail watching the beam go round. Round, and round. Out to sea, and back.

"Listen to it," she says. "Nothing's happening. Isn't it lovely."

She's fainter than she was. You can see the stars through her now, and she doesn't seem to mind.

"It'll burn on its own for a long while, now it's lit properly. Longer than I did. And I think..." She looks at her hands. "I think I've been relieved."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.farewell.c0: "I found your name on the shore. Ondine Marsh. Keeper. I'll tell everyone."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.farewell.c1: "I'll tell Saltmere who kept the Light."
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.farewell_named:
Ondine goes very still.

"You found it. I threw that into the sea a hundred years ago, the night I fell on the stairs. I thought nobody would ever..."

She holds out her lantern on its pole. As your hand closes round it, it becomes solid, and warm, and it is lit.

"Take it. It doesn't need me any more. Tell them I was here. Tell them I kept the Light."

And then she isn't there. Just the beam, going round, and the sound of the sea, and somewhere very far below, something enormous sighing in its sleep.
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.farewell_end:
"Thank you." She holds out her lantern on its pole. As your hand closes round it, it becomes solid, and warm, and it is lit.

"It doesn't need me any more. Take it. Somebody should carry a light who can walk where I couldn't."

And then she isn't there. Just the beam, going round, and the sea, and something enormous sighing in its sleep.
strings.dlg.reef.keeper.trout:
ONDINE: "The horse? She's been up here since Tuesday. She was also up here in the year of the Long Tide, when my great-grandfather laid the first stone. He wrote about her. 'A brown mare with a white blaze, standing on the scaffolding, watching.' I've stopped asking."

Trout, at the rail, chews thoughtfully and looks out to sea.
strings.quest.reef.title: The Light Past the Fog
strings.quest.reef.summary: Old Silas has seen a fire on the reef past Saltmere's fog, and two shapes beside it. His sons went into the fog with the Order.
strings.quest.reef.stage0: Ask Silas to row you out to the Saltmere Light (end of the north pier).
strings.quest.reef.journal0: Silas can see the old lighthouse again for the first time in forty years. And a fire on the reef.
strings.quest.reef.stage10: Explore the Sleeper's Reef. Find out who's by the fire, and what happened to the Light.
strings.quest.reef.journal10: Silas rowed me out between the sleeping limbs. Two men by a fire who don't know their names. A ghost on the lighthouse. Bottles all along the shore.
strings.quest.reef.stage20: Ask the keeper on the lighthouse gallery how to relight the lamp.
strings.quest.reef.journal20: Tom and Abel Gale. Their names came back to them out of two bottles, and they remembered their father. They won't row home in the dark.
strings.quest.reef.stage30: Something under the reef has woken. Fight off the Dreaming Limb.
strings.quest.reef.journal30: I lit the Saltmere Light. The thing under the reef felt it on its eyelids and reached up to find whoever had done it.
strings.quest.reef.stage40: The reef is quiet. Say goodbye to the keeper, then meet Silas at the jetty.
strings.quest.reef.journal40: The Light is turning again. Nothing is happening, which, the keeper says, is the whole point.
strings.quest.reef.stage100: Completed: Silas rowed his sons home.
strings.quest.reef.journal100: Silas counted his boys every tide for six weeks. Two for the net. He never stopped. He gave me the whole of his song, including the last verse, which nobody's sung in a hundred years.
strings.story.reef.row1:
The pier falls away behind you into the grey. After a dozen strokes there is no Saltmere, no shore, no sky: only the fog, the creak of the rowlocks, and Silas's breathing.

He sings under his breath as he rows. One for the boat. Two for the net.
strings.story.reef.row2:
Shapes rise out of the fog on either side. Pillars, you think at first. Then you see the suckers, each one the size of a cartwheel, and the slow, enormous rise and fall of something breathing in its sleep.

Silas doesn't stop rowing. He doesn't look at them. "Don't trail your hand," he says, very quietly.

As you pass the largest, an eye opens in its flank, grey-green, the size of a door. It turns towards the boat. It looks straight at Silas. Then it looks at the place where you are sitting, and finds nothing there, and slowly, puzzled, closes again.
strings.story.reef.row3:
A light, low and red, ahead. A fire. Then rocks, and a jetty of black timbers, and above it all a tower, dark at the top, where a light should be.

The keel grinds on stone.

"Reef," says Silas, and shipped oars have never sounded so loud. "I'll wait here. However long."
strings.story.reef.home: Silas rows you back through the fog, between the sleeping limbs, singing under his breath. Nothing opens its eye. The pier comes up out of the grey like an old friend.
strings.story.reef.homecoming:
Behind you, the Saltmere Light turns, slow and white, laying a path across the water all the way to the shore. The sleeping limbs lie quiet in it. Something under the reef is dreaming about the light, and the dream is a good one.

Ahead, Saltmere's windows are lit. Somebody on the quay sees the boat and shouts. Then everybody's shouting. Mother Brine is standing at the end of the pier with a pot of chowder and a face like a storm breaking.

Tom and Abel Gale come home, and they say their own names all the way up the pier, and nobody tells them to stop.
strings.map.sleepers_reef.name: The Sleeper's Reef
strings.npc.keeper_ondine.name: Ondine Marsh
strings.npc.keeper_ondine.title: Keeper of the Saltmere Light
strings.npc.gale_elder.name: The Taller Stranger
strings.npc.gale_elder.title: Nameless
strings.npc.gale_younger.name: The Shorter Stranger
strings.npc.gale_younger.title: Also Nameless
strings.npc.tom_gale.name: Thomas Gale
strings.npc.tom_gale.title: Bad at Knots
strings.npc.abel_gale.name: Abel Gale
strings.npc.abel_gale.title: Good at Writing His Name
strings.bark.keeper.1: Trim the wick. Fill the oil. Wind the clock. Never let it go out. ...It went out.
strings.bark.keeper.2: Round, and round. Nothing's happening. Isn't it lovely.
strings.bark.gale.reef.1: I think I'm the elder. He thinks HE'S the elder.
strings.bark.gale.reef.2: Somebody used to stitch things. I almost remember.
strings.bark.gale.home.1: Thomas Gale. Still bad at knots. Still here.
strings.bark.gale.home.2: Abel Gale. A-B-E-L. I can write it, you know.
strings.comp.baggy.zone.sleepers_reef: Why is everything here so... big? And wet? And LOOKING at me? No, wait, it's looking past me. Rude.
strings.comp.kaelen.zone.sleepers_reef: Walk softly. Whatever this is, it was old when the Bureau was a rumour.
strings.enemy.dreaming_limb.name: The Dreaming Limb
strings.line.dreaming_limb.alert: (Somewhere far below, something says a name. Not yours. It doesn't have yours.)
strings.line.dreaming_limb.death: (The limb sinks back into the sea, slowly, like a sleeper pulling the blanket up.)
strings.item.keeper_lantern.name: The Keeper's Lantern
strings.item.keeper_lantern.description: Ondine Marsh's lantern on its pole, lit at last. Carried in the off hand. +1 Will, +8% spell power, steady sanity recovery. Things in the dark find it soothing, which is not the same as friendly.
strings.item.silas_shanty.name: The Drowned Man's Rhyme
strings.item.silas_shanty.description: Old Silas's song, all of it, written out on salt-stained paper. Spelled wrong. Meant to be sung.
strings.book.silas_shanty.text:
THE DROWNED MAN'S RHYME
(as sung by the Gales of Saltmere, written out by Silas, spelling his own)

Oh, the tide comes in, and the tide goes out,
and it counts us every time,
one for the boat and two for the net
and three for the drowned man's rhyme.

So never you say your name, my lad,
where the grey fog rolls ashore,
for the thing that sleeps where the bells still ring
is hungry evermore.

But the names that are struck from the ledger, lad,
and the souls that the books forgot,
they can walk on the reef where the big ones sleep,
for the sea can see them not.

And the Marsh girl keeps the Light, my lad,
on the rock past the edge of the grey,
and while it turns, the sleeper dreams,
and the boats come home to stay.

(LAST VERSE. Nobody's sung it in a hundred years. My father said you only sing it when you've got cause.)

So here's to the one with no name, my lads,
who walked where the sleepers lie,
and picked our names off the rocks like shells
and brought them home to dry.

One for the boat, and two for the net,
and both of them home tonight.
And the sea can count whatever it likes.
We've got the Light.

- S. Gale, his song.
strings.spell.cold_shoulder.name: Cold Shoulder
strings.spell.cold_shoulder.desc: A ring of brittle, disapproving frost bursts out from you. Everyone nearby is chilled (slowed). Chill anything three times and it freezes solid. Set fire to something frozen and it SHATTERS.
strings.spell.chain_of_command.name: Chain of Command
strings.spell.chain_of_command.desc: Lightning passed down the line: it hits the nearest foe in front of you, then jumps to three more, each jump a little weaker. Shocked foes take 25% more damage from everything. Shock something that's on fire and it OVERLOADS.
strings.spell.standing_ovation.name: Standing Ovation
strings.spell.standing_ovation.desc: Thunderous applause from nowhere. Everything near you is staggered and shocked. Odette says it's the only spell that has ever made a critic leave early.
strings.spell.slow_burn.name: Slow Burn
strings.spell.slow_burn.desc: A small, patient flame. Barely stings on impact, then burns for six seconds. Mother Brine used it to keep the chowder warm for eleven years.
strings.spell.redacted.name: [REDACTED]
strings.spell.redacted.desc: A bar of perfect black blots out a target's eyes. Inked foes can barely see, lose track of you, and miss almost half their attacks. [The remainder of this description has been redacted.]
strings.spell.clerical_error.name: Clerical Error
strings.spell.clerical_error.desc: The universe briefly misfiles your position. You are six metres further forward than you were. (Never through walls: even the universe has rules.)
strings.item.grimoire_cold.name: On Cold Shoulders
strings.item.grimoire_cold.description: A grimoire from the Bellwether Library's Restricted Section, decades overdue. Return it to Fenwick, who will let you copy Cold Shoulder into your spellbook.
strings.book.grimoire_cold.text:
ON COLD SHOULDERS: A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO BROODING AT A DISTANCE

Chapter One: The Turn. Present the shoulder. Not the whole back; that is rude. The shoulder says: I am wounded, and you may not ask why.

Chapter Two: The Frost. Should the observer approach regardless, channel your disdain outward in a ring. It should sparkle. Everything sparkles, eventually.

In the margins, in elegant violet ink: "so true" ... "SO true" ... "this is me" ... "she never understood this" -A.

[The spell inside is locked behind a library binding-charm. Fenwick can unlock it.]
strings.item.grimoire_chain.name: Chain of Command: Lightning in the Workplace
strings.item.grimoire_chain.description: A grimoire from the Bellwether Library's Restricted Section, decades overdue. Return it to Fenwick, who will let you copy Chain of Command into your spellbook.
strings.book.grimoire_chain.text:
CHAIN OF COMMAND
Lightning in the Workplace

A directive issued at the top must reach every desk. So it is with lightning. Strike the nearest subordinate; the charge will be passed down the line, losing a little conviction at each desk, until it reaches someone who simply does not care.

Pickering's pencilled notes: "cf. tide-bell harmonics?? the bells passed the COUNT down the line the same way. must ask Fenwick for an extension. must ask Fenwick for an extension. must"

[The spell inside is locked behind a library binding-charm. Fenwick can unlock it.]
strings.item.grimoire_ovation.name: The Standing Ovation (Advanced Theatrical Thaumaturgy)
strings.item.grimoire_ovation.description: A grimoire from the Bellwether Library's Restricted Section, decades overdue. Return it to Fenwick, who will let you copy Standing Ovation into your spellbook.
strings.book.grimoire_ovation.text:
THE STANDING OVATION
Advanced Theatrical Thaumaturgy

The audience must be ROUSED. Not persuaded. Not charmed. ROUSED. Gather the room's anticipation into your hands and RELEASE it as applause so overwhelming that everyone within five paces is physically knocked back by your genius.

Warning: do not cast during the quiet bit.

On the flyleaf, in magenta: "Borrowed for research. Returning SOON. Darling. -O" (dated nine years ago)

[The spell inside is locked behind a library binding-charm. Fenwick can unlock it.]
strings.item.grimoire_slow.name: Slow Burn: Patience in Pyromancy
strings.item.grimoire_slow.description: A grimoire from the Bellwether Library's Restricted Section, decades overdue. Return it to Fenwick, who will let you copy Slow Burn into your spellbook.
strings.book.grimoire_slow.text:
SLOW BURN: PATIENCE IN PYROMANCY

The impatient pyromancer throws the biggest fire they can. The patient one throws a small fire and waits. The small fire is still going when the impatient pyromancer is being rebuilt by a healer.

The book smells strongly of chowder. Every page has a ring where a hot pot was set down on it. Pencilled at the back: "Low simmer = 3 pages of Chapter Two. Rolling boil = Chapter Four. DO NOT READ CHAPTER SIX NEAR THE STEW. -B"

[The spell inside is locked behind a library binding-charm. Fenwick can unlock it.]
strings.item.grimoire_redacted.name: [REDACTED]: A Guide to Discreet Omission
strings.item.grimoire_redacted.description: A grimoire from the Bellwether Library's Restricted Section, decades overdue. Return it to Fenwick, who will let you copy [REDACTED] into your spellbook.
strings.book.grimoire_redacted.text:
[REDACTED]
A Guide to Discreet Omission

Chapter One. ████ ███ ██████ ███ ███ ███████. ██ ███ ████, ████████.

Chapter Two. ███████████████████████████████████████████████████████.

The only unredacted line in the book, on the last page: "Brother Aldous: Please return the hymn book's naughty verses when you've finished blacking them out. They're library property. -F"
